memories.body:
# Starlink

Starlink is a **PM creative workflow system** that integrates with the **cehua AI platform** (策划 AI platform). It handles creative ideas, star map review, and workflow events for games.

## Services & Components
- **Frontend**: SolutionHub
- **BBC**: Python write backend (part of starlink infrastructure)
- **wirerope-gql**: Rust GraphQL read API
- **Ding**: OpenResty gateway
- **Other services**: starflow, vector, hfrog, pgpour, and fakeuser (LGH only)

The codebase is **hs-code-keeper**.

## Environments
- **Dev all-in-one server**: `archteam-starlink-dev-all-in-one` (hosts JDMJ LGH environment)
- **LGH environment**: `/data/starlink-lgh-jdmj/`
- **Production environment**: `archteam-starlink-jdmj-prod-1`

## Game Served
- **Guofeng Mahjong** (国风麻将)

## Kafka Topics
- Feature config workflow updates: `biz.starlink.{game}.{env}.public.feature_config_workflow_info`
- Environment variable `KAFKA_STARLINK_UPDATE_DATA_TOPIC` uses prefix `biz.starlink.{game}.{env}.public.`
- Outbox topic configured via `KAFKA_PLAN_STATE_SYNC_TOPICS`
- Biz topics are filtered by Lua to project only update events with a whitelist of fields; raw topics contain full CDC envelope.

## Registry
- **BBC service**: Aliyun VPC registry
- **Frontend, gql, starflow**: `registry.hs99.vip`

## Integration
- Integrates with the planning side (策划).
- The system is part of the Starlink platform/project that hosts services including BBC.

## Starlink Overview

- **Starlink** is a platform or project that hosts services including BBC, and is a team in Alibaba Cloud caikuai-cn billing.
- It is a PM creative workflow system that integrates with the cehua AI platform, handling creative ideas, star map review, and workflow events for games.
- Starlink has 6 game variants and 14 dev environments, each with ~14 services.

### Components
- **Frontend**: SolutionHub
- **Backend (BBC)**: Python write backend
- **GraphQL Read API**: wirerope-gql (Rust)
- **Gateway**: Ding (OpenResty gateway)
- **Other services**: vector, hfrog, pgpour, fakeuser (LGH only)

### Codebase
- The `hs-code-keeper` repository is part of the Starlink project.
- The BBC backend service is included.

### Environments
- **Production**: archteam-starlink-jdmj-prod-1
- **LGH**: archteam-starlink-dev-all-in-one (hosts JDMJ LGH environment at `/data/starlink-lgh-jdmj/`)
- **Registry**: BBC uses Aliyun VPC registry; frontend, gql, starflow use registry.hs99.vip.

### Services per Environment
- Services: bbc, frontend, gql, starflow, vector, hfrog, pgpour, fakeuser (LGH only).
- Starlink serves Guofeng Mahjong (JDMJ) and other games: BlockCrush, BlockBlast, MJWD, N8N, pgpour.

### Kafka Topics
- Feature config workflow updates: `biz.starlink.{game}.{env}.public.feature_config_workflow_info`
- Environment variable `KAFKA_STARLINK_UPDATE_DATA_TOPIC` configured with prefix `biz.starlink.{game}.{env}.public`
- Outbox topic configured via `KAFKA_PLAN_STATE_SYNC_TOPICS`
- Biz topics filtered by Lua to project only update events with a whitelist of fields; raw topics contain full CDC envelope.

memories.body:
- **Starlink** is a platform/project that hosts games and services including BlockCrush, BlockBlast, JDMJ, MJWD, N8N, and pgpour. It is also a team in Aliyun caikuai-cn billing.
- It is a **PM creative workflow system** that integrates with the cehua AI platform, handling creative ideas, star map review, and workflow events for games.
- **Components**:
  - Frontend: SolutionHub
  - BBC: Python write backend
  - wirerope-gql: Rust GraphQL read API
  - Ding: OpenResty gateway
  - Other services: starflow, vector, hfrog, pgpour, fakeuser (LGH only)
- **Environments**:
  - Production: archteam-starlink-jdmj-prod-1
  - LGH: archteam-starlink-dev-all-in-one (hosts JDMJ LGH environment) at /data/starlink-lgh-jdmj/
  - 14 dev environments total, each with ~14 services
- **Game variants**: 6 game variants
- **Kafka topics**:
  - Feature config workflow updates: `biz.starlink.{game}.{env}.public.feature_config_workflow_info`
  - Environment variable `KAFKA_STARLINK_UPDATE_DATA_TOPIC` configured with prefix `biz.starlink.{game}.{env}.public`
  - Outbox topic configured via `KAFKA_PLAN_STATE_SYNC_TOPICS`
  - Biz topics are filtered by Lua to project only update events with a whitelist of fields; raw topics contain full CDC envelope
  - pgpour uses `starlink_hs99_vip_client/bbc_publication`, only `_pm_idea_flow_outbox_event` table, topics `starlink.starlinkpm.prod` and `biz.starlink.starlinkpm.inner.prod`
  - Starlink has a forwarder component for outbox events

memories.body:
- **Overview**: Starlink (星链) is a project/system that hosts multiple games and services. It is a PM creative workflow system integrating with the cehua AI platform and planning side (策划).
- **Games**: BlockCrush, BlockBlast, JDMJ (Guofeng Mahjong), MJWD, N8N, pgpour.
- **Services**: frontend (SolutionHub), BBC (Python backend), wirerope-gql (Rust GraphQL read API), Ding (OpenResty gateway), starflow, vector, hfrog, pgpour, fakeuser (LGH only). The BBC service is part of the Starlink infrastructure.
- **Environments**: 6 game variants, 14 dev environments, each with ~14 services. Production: archteam-starlink-jdmj-prod-1. LGH: /data/starlink-lgh-jdmj/. Dev all-in-one: archteam-starlink-dev-all-in-one.
- **Infrastructure**:
  - Object storage: MinIO (10.254.3.107), migrating to Aliyun OSS.
  - Kafka topics: biz.starlink.{game}.{env}.public.feature_config_workflow_info; environment variable KAFKA_STARLINK_UPDATE_DATA_TOPIC sets prefix. Outbox topics via KAFKA_PLAN_STATE_SYNC_TOPICS. Biz topics are filtered by Lua to project only update events with whitelist fields.
  - Registries: BBC uses Aliyun VPC registry; frontend, gql, starflow use registry.hs99.vip.
  - Starlink 3.5.0 configuration: pgpour uses starlink_hs99_vip_client/bbc_publication, only _pm_idea_flow_outbox_event table, topics starlink.starlinkpm.prod and biz.starlink.starlinkpm.inner.prod.
- **Teams**: Starlink is a team under Aliyun caikuai-cn bill.
- **Additional**: Has a forwarder component for outbox events. The hs-code-keeper codebase is part of the project.

memories.abstract: Starlink is a PM creative workflow platform hosting games (BlockCrush, BlockBlast, JDMJ, MJWD) with 6 variants, 14 dev environments, ~14 services each, using Kafka, MinIO/OSS, and integrated with cehua AI.
memories.body:
## Starlink Overview

- **Purpose**: Starlink is a PM creative workflow system that integrates with the cehua AI platform. It handles creative ideas, star map review, and workflow events for games.
- **Game Variants**: 6 game variants, including BlockCrush, BlockBlast, JDMJ, MJWD, and others (e.g., Guofeng Mahjong).
- **Environments**: 14 development environments, each with ~14 services. Notable environments: production (archteam-starlink-jdmj-prod-1), LGH (/data/starlink-lgh-jdmj/), and an all-in-one server (archteam-starlink-dev-all-in-one).

### Services
- **Core services**: bbc (Python write backend), frontend (SolutionHub), gql (Rust GraphQL read API), starflow, vector, hfrog, pgpour, and fakeuser (LGH only).
- **Infrastructure**: Uses Kafka (topic prefix `biz.starlink.{game}.{env}.public`), MinIO (at 10.254.3.107) and Aliyun OSS for object storage. Artifacts are being migrated from MinIO to OSS.

### Storage
- **Buckets**: `starlink-blockcrush-pm-artifacts` on OSS; `starlink-artifacts-prd` for PM artifacts. Artifact upload URLs stored in `pm_work_item_meta` table.
- **Migration**: Only `task-acceptance` prefix copied during PoC; `art-submit` not yet migrated.

### Integration & Configuration
- **Kafka topics**: Feature config workflow updates use `biz.starlink.{game}.{env}.public.feature_config_workflow_info`. Environment variable `KAFKA_STARLINK_UPDATE_DATA_TOPIC` with same prefix. Outbox topic via `KAFKA_PLAN_STATE_SYNC_TOPICS`.
- **Filtering**: Biz topics filtered by Lua to project only update events with whitelisted fields; raw topics contain full CDC envelope.
- **Registry**: In production, bbc uses Aliyun VPC registry; frontend, gql, starflow use registry.hs99.vip.

### Project Scope
- **Sub-projects**: BlockCrush, JDMJ, BlockBlast (yl-blockblast, yy-blockblast). Starlink is the project prefix for BlockCrush PM and BlockBlast systems.
- **CI/CD**: Jenkins for BlockBlast environments.
- **Team**: Aliyun caikuai-cn billing team.

### Known Issues
- `/download` endpoint does not redirect to presigned URL; returns 404 in production, error in development.

memories.body:
# BlockCrush

BlockCrush is an existing game project integrated with the cehua AI platform and Starlink (Starlink AI platform). It is a sub-project of Starlink.

## Hosting & Environments
- **Production**: `starlink-blockcrush.youxi123.com` (hosted on Starlink)
- **Staging (LGH)**: `https://lgh-blockcrush.ext.hs99.vip`
- Production servers: `app-1` and `app-2`
- BlockCrush has a `.ext` subdomain configuration on `hs99.vip`.

## Databases
- **Production schema**: `prd_blockcrush_client`
- Other databases: `lhh_blockcrush_client` and `lhh_blockcrush_hfrog`

## Architecture
BlockCrush is a project management application with a PM UI and a client library. It has a four-layer architecture:
1. Frontend (PM UI)
2. hfrog (service layer)
3. hfrog database
4. Object storage (MinIO and Aliyun OSS)

The PM UI does not connect directly to the database; it uses BBC for metadata and hfrog for uploads. PM work item metadata is stored in the `prd_blockcrush_client` database.

## Storage
- BlockCrush produces PM artifacts (attachments). These were migrated from MinIO to Aliyun OSS.
- BlockCrush PM uses BlockBlast's hfrog and a shared MinIO bucket in production.
- BlockCrush has private and public buckets under Starlink.
- To download task acceptance videos, the UI reads `meta_value → file.url`.

## Integration
BlockCrush is integrated with the Starlink AI platform. It is also integrated with the cehua AI platform. The project uses the Starlink AI platform integration.

## hfrog Service

hfrog is an artifact storage service that provides presigned URLs for uploading and downloading artifacts. It runs as a container on `starlink-dev-all-in-one` and listens on port 8001. The container is named `starlink-lhh-blockcrush-hfrog` and is part of the `lhh-blockcrush` PoC, cloned from BlockBlast's production hfrog.

### Key Features
- Provides presigned upload and download URLs for artifacts.
- Serves as a presign/lookup gateway for OSS/MinIO object storage.
- JSON API endpoint: `GET /hfrog/api/artifactory/get_object_presigned_url` (keyed on `pid` or `name+ver+runtime`, not `s3Key`).
- As of 2026-08-04, lacks a browser-accessible download redirect endpoint.
- Stores files with `create_time` metadata.

### S3 Backends
- Has three S3 backends: `s3_0`, `s3_1`, `s3_2`, each pointing to MinIO buckets.
- Also configured to point to OSS (Alibaba Cloud Object Storage Service) for the BlockCrush PoC.

### Databases
- Stores artifactory metadata in databases: `prd_blockblast_hfrog` (for BlockBlast prod) and `prd_jdmj_hfrog` (for Jade Mahjong).
- The `artifactory` table manages objects and presigned URLs.

### Webhooks
- Expects webhook payloads in flat JSON format with `event_name` and `key` fields, as used by MinIO S3 events.
- The `s3_hook` webhook endpoint is located at the `starlink-jade-mahjong` domain.

### Usage in Applications
- **BlockCrush PoC**: Used for artifact storage with OSS configuration.
- **Jade Mahjong game**: Service component handling artifact storage.
- **BlockBlast prod**: Presigns uploads and registers artifacts.
- **WorkItemCommentInput.vue**: Uploads via hfrog with `pkgName` 'work-item-comment'.

memories.body:
## Starlink (星链)

**Identity**
- Starlink is a project/system (also referred to as a platform or infrastructure) that hosts multiple games and services. It is a team in the Aliyun caikuai-cn bill.
- It is a creative evaluation system using stakeholder review with art and dev gates, and integrates with the cehua AI platform.
- It is the project prefix for BlockCrush PM and BlockBlast systems.

**Components**
- Frontend: SolutionHub
- Backend: BBC (Python write backend)
- Read API: wirerope-gql (Rust GraphQL)
- Gateway: Ding (OpenResty)
- Other services: starflow, vector, hfrog, pgpour, fakeuser (LGH only)
- The hs-code-keeper codebase is part of the project.
- The project includes the block_crush (bbc) submodule.

**Games**
- BlockCrush, BlockBlast, JDMJ (Jade Mahjong), MJWD (Mahjong Wonders), Guofeng Mahjong, and others (6 game variants total).
- Each game has its own PM artifacts bucket (e.g., starlink-blockcrush-pm-artifacts, starlink-jdmj-pm-artifacts-public).

**Environments**
- 14 dev environments per game, each with ~14 services.
- Production: archteam-starlink-jdmj-prod-1
- LGH (dev): archteam-starlink-dev-all-in-one, path /data/starlink-lgh-jdmj/
- Hostnames: starlink-jade-mahjong.youxi123.com, lgh-jdmj.hs99.vip
- Use Host isolation for projects (no appname field needed).

**Infrastructure**
- **Kafka**: Topic naming: starlink.{game}.{env}.{schema}.{table}. Feature config workflow updates: biz.starlink.{game}.{env}.public.feature_config_workflow_info. Environment variable KAFKA_STARLINK_UPDATE_DATA_TOPIC prefix. Outbox topic via KAFKA_PLAN_STATE_SYNC_TOPICS. Lua filters for biz topics.
- **Storage**: Two-bucket architecture per game (private and public). MinIO server at 10.254.3.107, with migration to Aliyun OSS. Artifact upload URLs stored in pm_work_item_meta table. Credential file at e.credentials/starlink/pm-artifacts-oss.txt. RAM policy v2 covers four buckets. hfrog s3.ini template for bucket types.
- **Deployment**: Services use registry.hs99.vip (frontend, gql, starflow) and Aliyun VPC registry (bbc). Jenkins for CI/CD.
- **Forwarder**: Starlink has a forwarder component for outbox events.
- **Runbook**: Exists for adding new games.

**Miscellaneous**
- The /download endpoint does not redirect to presigned URL; returns 404 in production, error in dev.
- During PoC migration, only task-acceptance prefix was copied to OSS; art-submit prefix was not.

# Starlink

## Overview
- Starlink is a platform or project that hosts services including BBC.

- Starlink is a system that integrates with the planning side (策划).
- Starlink is a creative evaluation system that uses a stakeholder review process with art and dev gates.
- Starlink is the project prefix for the BlockCrush PM and BlockBlast systems.

## Architecture & Services
- Starlink is a system with frontend (SolutionHub), BBC (Python write backend), wirerope-gql (Rust GraphQL read API), and Ding (OpenResty gateway).
- The starlink project includes the hs-code-keeper codebase and the BBC backend service.
- The BBC service is part of the Starlink infrastructure.
- Starlink has a forwarder component for outbox events.

## Storage
- **MinIO**: server at 10.254.3.107, used for artifact storage (production)

memories.body:
## BBC Service

- **Identity**: BBC (hs-code-keeper/bbc) is the Python write backend in the Starlink stack, deployed via Jenkins on the starlink platform. It is a Flask backend application.
- **Purpose**: Service for building and deploying game backends, keyed by `APP_ID`. Handles BlockCrush business logic and PM work item meta upsert.
- **Features**:
  - Contains `EAvatarScope` enum and `Avatar.get_scope()` logic.
  - Login API returns two scope lists: the cookie (`user_info`) contains only `:v` scopes, while the API `data.task.scope` contains non-`:v` API permission strings.
  - Handles login ticket verification by calling SSO's `ADDR_SSO_VERIFY_TICKET` endpoint.

memories.abstract: hfrog is an artifact storage service that provides presigned upload/download URLs via S3/MinIO backends, used in BlockCrush, Jade Mahjong, and Starlink projects.
memories.body:
# hfrog

## Identity
- **hfrog** is a Rust-based artifact storage service that manages object storage and provides presigned URLs.
- It runs on `starlink-dev-all-in-one` as a container named `starlink-lhh-blockcrush-hfrog`, listening on port **8001**.

## Purpose & Usage
- Used for the **BlockCrush PoC** (cloned from BlockBlast's production hfrog).
- Also a component of the **Jade Mahjong** game.
- Serves artifacts in the **Starlink** project.

## Technical Details
- Provides **presigned upload and download URLs** for artifacts.
- Endpoint: `GET /hfrog/api/artifactory/get_object_presigned_url` (keyed by `pid` or `name`+`ver`+`runtime`, not by `s3Key`).
- As of **2026-08-04**, lacks a browser-accessible download redirect endpoint.
- Handles file upload, signs upload URLs, and writes metadata to the **artifactory** database.

## Backends
- Three S3 backends: `s3_0`, `s3_1`, `s3_2`, each pointing to **MinIO** buckets.
- Also connects to OSS (Object Storage Service) for some configurations.

## Webhooks
- Expects MinIO-style flat JSON payloads with `event_name` and `key` fields.
- Webhook endpoint hosted on the `starlink-jade-mahjong` domain.

## Databases
- Stores metadata in `prd_blockblast_hfrog` (for BlockBlast) and `prd_jdmj_hfrog` (for Jade Mahjong).

## Additional
- Files stored with `create_time` metadata.
- Used by the WorkItemCommentInput.vue rich editor with `pkgName: 'work-item-comment'`.
- Handles MinIO hook events and Kafka integration (as a Rust service).

memories.abstract: hfrog is an artifact storage and presigned URL service (Rust, MySQL) used by BlockCrush, BlockBlast, Jade Mahjong, and Starlink projects. It runs on port 8001, uses MinIO/OSS backends, and provides a JSON API for presigned URLs.
memories.body:
## hfrog

- **Service**: hfrog is a Rust-based artifact storage service with a MySQL backend. It provides presigned upload and download URLs for artifacts.
- **Deployment**: Runs on `starlink-dev-all-in-one` as a container named `starlink-lhh-blockcrush-hfrog`, listening on port 8001.
- **API**: Provides a JSON API at `GET /hfrog/api/artifactory/get_object_presigned_url`, keyed by `pid` (or `name+ver+runtime`). As of 2026-08-04, it lacks a browser-accessible download redirect endpoint.
- **Backends**: Has three S3 backends (`s3_0`, `s3_1`, `s3_2`) pointing to MinIO buckets. Also supports OSS (Object Storage Service) for presigned URLs.
- **Webhooks**: Expects MinIO-style flat JSON payloads with `event_name` and `key` fields. The webhook endpoint is hosted at the `starlink-jade-mahjong` domain and looks up the `artifactory` table in the `prd_jdmj_hfrog` database.
- **Metadata**: Stores files with `create_time` metadata. For BlockBlast production, metadata is stored in the `prd_blockblast_hfrog` database.
- **Usage**:

memories.abstract: Starlink is a PM creative workflow platform and infrastructure for multiple games (BlockCrush, BlockBlast, JDMJ, MJWD, Block Bloom) with frontend SolutionHub, BBC backend, wirerope-gql, Ding gateway, and various services; uses MinIO/OSS storage, Kafka topics, and multiple environments.
memories.body:
# Starlink

Starlink (星链) is a project management (PM) creative workflow platform and infrastructure for multiple games, including BlockCrush, BlockBlast, JDMJ (Jade Mahjong), MJWD, and Block Bloom. It integrates with the cehua AI platform and handles creative ideas, star map review, and workflow events.

## Components
- **Frontend**: SolutionHub (PM UI)
- **BBC**: Python write backend (also a submodule `block_crush`)
- **wirerope-gql**: Rust GraphQL read API
- **Ding**: OpenResty gateway
- **starflow**, **vector**, **hfrog**, **pgpour**, **fakeuser** (LGH only) are additional services.
- The system includes the `hs-code-keeper` codebase.
- Repositories: solutionhub, hs-code-keeper, pm-1-frontend, pm-1-backend.

## Environments
- **Production**: `archteam-starlink-jdmj-prod-1` (internal resource), public domain `starlink.youxi123.com`
- **LGH**: `/data/starlink-lgh-jdmj/` (path), hostname `lgh-jdmj.ext.hs99.vip`
- **Dev all-in-one**: `archteam-starlink-dev-all-in-one` (hosts JDMJ LGH environment)
- **Remote environment**: `starlink.hs99.vip` (proxy target for GraphQL and passport endpoints)
- **Proxy preset target**: `https://pm-1-dev.hs99.vip`
- 6 game variants and 14 dev environments, each with ~14 services.
- Uses Host isolation (no appname field).
- CI/CD via Jenkins (instance at devops-jenkins.hs99.vip).

## Storage
- Uses MinIO (server at 10.254.3.107) and Aliyun OSS; artifacts are being migrated from MinIO to OSS.
- Two-bucket architecture per game (private and public).
- Buckets include `starlink-blockcrush-pm-artifacts`, `starlink-artifacts-prd`, `starlink-jdmj-pm-artifacts-public`.
- Credential file: `e.credentials/starlink/pm-artifacts-oss.txt`.
- RAM policy v2 covers four buckets.
- `hfrog` has an `s3.ini` template for bucket types.
- Artifact upload URLs are stored in `pm_work_item_meta` table.
- Known issue: `/download` endpoint does not redirect to presigned URL (404 in prod, error in dev).
- During PoC migration, only `task-acceptance` prefix was copied to OSS; `art-submit` prefix was not.
- Attachment paths are relative URLs like `/attachments/{key}/{filename}`; nginx/OpenResty routes `/attachments/` to the starlink-attachments service, which returns 302 with `Content-Disposition: inline; filename*` from OSS metadata. Note: Inline disposition in Chrome results in hash filenames; attachment disposition works correctly.

## Data & Databases
- Shared-services RDS: `archteam-starlink-prd-shared-services.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com`.
- Database `fework_prd_db` contains tables: `app_group`, `app_info`, `app_login`, `release`, `work`.
- `app_info` stores game registration (app_id, app_name, app_web_url, group_id, sort_order, create_time).
- `app_login` stores SSO hostname mapping (app_id, host).
- Database user `fework_prd_user` owns these tables.
- PostgreSQL RDS instance has application users `prd_blockbloom_client` and `prd_blockbloom_codekeeper`; no postgres superuser.

## Kafka
- Topic naming: `starlink.{game}.{env}.{schema}.{table}`.
- Feature config workflow topic: `biz.starlink.{game}.{env}.public.feature_config_workflow_info`.
- Production topic example: `biz.starlink.blockcrush.prd.public.feature_config_workflow_info` (3 partitions, replication factor 2, 3-day retention).
- Environment variable `KAFKA_STARLINK_UPDATE_DATA_TOPIC` uses prefix `biz.starlink.{game}.{env}.public`.

memories.abstract: Starlink is a project management platform for games, with services, environments, storage, Kafka, databases, and infrastructure details.
memories.body:
## Overview
- Starlink (星链) is a project management (PM) platform that hosts games and services, integrating with the cehua AI platform. It handles creative ideas, star map review, and workflow events for games.
- It is a creative evaluation system using a stakeholder review process with art and dev gates.
- Contains repositories: solutionhub, hs-code-keeper, pm-1-frontend, pm-1-backend. Includes PM application and attachments service.
- User is currently working on this project.

## Architecture
- Services: BBC (Python write backend), frontend (SolutionHub), wirerope-gql (Rust GraphQL read API), Ding (OpenResty gateway), starflow, vector, hfrog, pgpour, and fakeuser (LGH only).
- Uses Host isolation for projects; no appname field needed.
- Environments: 6 game variants, 14 dev environments, each with ~14 services. Production and LGH environments exist (e.g., archteam-starlink-jdmj-prod-1, /data/starlink-lgh-jdmj/).
- Hostnames: starlink-jade-mahjong.youxi123.com, lgh-jdmj.hs99.vip.

## Games
- Hosts multiple games: BlockCrush, BlockBlast, JDMJ, MJWD, N8N, pgpour, Guofeng Mahjong, Jade Mahjong, Block Bloom. Sub-projects include blockcrush and jdmj.

## Storage
- Uses MinIO for production and Alibaba Cloud OSS for development; artifacts are being migrated from MinIO to OSS.
- Two-bucket architecture per game (private and public). Buckets include starlink-blockcrush-pm-artifacts, starlink-jdmj-pm-artifacts-public, starlink-artifacts-prd.
- Artifact upload URLs are stored in the pm_work_item_meta table.
- Credential file: e.credentials/starlink/pm-artifacts-oss.txt.
- RAM policy v2 covers its four buckets.
- hfrog s3.ini template exists for bucket types.
- Known issue: /download endpoint does not redirect to presigned URL (404 in production, error in dev).

## Kafka
- Topic naming: starlink.{game}.{env}.{schema}.{table} or biz.starlink.{game}.{env}.public.feature_config_workflow_info.
- Environment variables: KAFKA_STARLINK_UPDATE_DATA_TOPIC (prefix biz.starlink.{game}.{env}.public), KAFKA_PLAN_STATE_SYNC_TOPICS (outbox topic).
- Biz topics are filtered by Lua to project only update events with a whitelist of fields; raw topics contain full CDC envelope.
- Forwarder component exists for outbox events.
- Production topic `biz.starlink.blockcrush.prd.public.feature_config_workflow_info` exists with 3 partitions, replication factor 2, and 3-day retention.

## Database
- Shared-services RDS: archteam-starlink-prd-shared-services.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com.
- Database fework_prd_db contains tables: app_group, app_info, app_login, release, work.
- app_info stores game registration (app_id, app_name, app_web_url, group_id, sort_order, create_time).
- app_login stores SSO hostname mapping (app_id, host).
- Database user fework_prd_user owns these tables.
- PostgreSQL RDS instance has application users prd_blockbloom_client and prd_blockbloom_codekeeper; no postgres superuser.
- On shared-services instance, Starlink stacks use `starlink_<slug>_client` and `starlink_<slug>_codekeeper` database naming; `prd_*` is reserved for dedicated per-game RDS.

## Infrastructure
- Deployed on Aliyun cloud; uses EventBridge and OSS.
- Jenkins for CI/CD (blockblast environments). Jenkins instance: devops-jenkins.hs99.vip.
- Runbook exists for adding new games.
- Production Docker Compose environments hosted in archteam environment.
- Starlink is a team in Aliyun caikuai-cn billing.
- In production, bbc service uses Aliyun VPC registry; frontend, gql, starflow use registry.hs99.vip.
- Starlink 3.5.0 config: pgpour uses starlink_hs99_vip_client/bbc_publication, only _pm_idea_flow_outbox_event table, topics starlink.starlinkpm.prod and biz.starlink.starlinkpm.inner.prod.

## Attachments
- Stores attachment paths as relative URLs like `/attachments/{key}/{filename}`.
- starlink-attachments 302 responses include `Content-Disposition: inline; filename*` from OSS metadata.
- Inline disposition in Chrome downloads results in hash filenames; attachment disposition works correctly.
- nginx/OpenResty routes /attachments/ to the starlink-attachments service.

## Other
- Starlink is the project prefix for BlockCrush PM and BlockBlast systems.
- The starlink dev all-in-one server (archteam-starlink-dev-all-in-one) hosts the JDMJ LGH environment.
- Remote environment at starlink.hs99.vip (proxy target for GraphQL and passport endpoints).
- Proxy preset target: https://pm-1-dev.hs99.vip.
- Production: starlink.youxi123.com, also lgh-jdmj.ext.hs99.vip.

memories.body:
# starlink-attachments

## Overview
- Go service for handling file attachments for Starlink PM (project management), related to hfrog.
- Uses Aliyun OSS as its storage backend and source of truth; **no database**.
- Provides upload/download API endpoints.

## Storage & Content Addressing
- Content-addressed using **SHA-256 hashes** for object keys.
- Upload/download via **presigned URLs** with inline and attachment disposition options.
- Client-side hashing and deduplication via `HeadObject`.
- Stores original filenames in OSS object metadata (`x-oss-meta-filename`); non-ASCII filenames are base64-encoded.
- Handles `Content-Disposition` via query parameter.

## Repository & Build
- Hosted at **git.7k7k.com/hs-devops/starlink-attachments** (not GitHub).
  - SSH: `git@git.7k7k.com:hs-devops/starlink-attachments.git`
- Local paths: `/Users/liguanghui/hs.projects/starlink/starlink-attachments` and `/Users/liguanghui/hs.projects/hs-devops/starlink-attachments`.
- Built with a **Jenkins** pipeline.
- Image: `starlink/attachments`, pushed to `registry.hs99.vip` and `starfamily-registry-vpc.cn-beijing.cr.aliyuncs.com` (also referenced as `/starlink/attachments` and `/starlink/starlink-attachments`).

## Deployment & Access
- Deployed on host **archteam-starlink-dev-all-in-one**; service port **24511**.
- Container name: `starlink-lgh-jdmj-attachments-1`.
- Accessible at:
  - `https://lgh-jdmj.hs99.vip/attachments/demo/`
  - `https://lgh-jdmj.ext.hs99.vip/attachments/`
- Inside container: listens on port **8080**, uses `APP_ENV=production` and `LISTEN_ADDR=:8080`; demo/docs routes disabled in production.
- Routed through OpenResty using docker upstream names.
- Uses environment variable `ATTACHMENTS_IMAGE_TAG` to specify image tag.
- Production deploy gated to users: `liguanghui001232`, `yangyang001233`, `duanwenbin`.

## Current Limitations (v0)
- No authentication.
- No database.
- No OSS EventBridge webhook.
- No multipart upload.
- No PM frontend integration.

memories.abstract: rmb (recall memory bank) is a Go-based client-server memory system for long-term memory, with a desktop app, CLI, agent integrations (Cursor, Claude Code, etc.), append-only versioned storage, and HTTP-based sync.
memories.body:
# rmb (Recall Memory Bank)

rmb is the user's project, a client-server CLI tool for long-term memory. It is written in Go and serves as a memory agent backend performing incremental ingestion, distillation, and retrieval. The repository is hosted at `colinleefish/rmb` and also serves as a repository for static assets of the RMB project.

## Components

- **Desktop app**: Served under `/ui/` path, bundle identifier `me.remember.rmb`, binary at `~/.rmb/bin/rmb-app`.
- **CLI tool**: Binary at `~/.rmb/bin/rmb`, configuration at `~/.rmb/config.yaml` pointing to server `https://rmb.colinleefish.com`.
- **Agent integration**: Provides detect, preview, and apply functions in the `internal/setup/` package, supporting Cursor, CC (Claude Code), Codex, OpenCode, and Pi.

## Integrations

- **Cursor**: Requires two artifacts: `hooks.json` and user rules.
- **Claude Code**: Requires two artifacts: `settings.json` and a recall file.
- **Workflow**: Requires a preview-before-apply workflow for configuration changes.

## Memory System

- Categories: Profile, Events, Preferences, Entities.
- Memories are stored in a versioned, append-only `memories` table keyed by URI, with a single active row per URI.
- Events are immutable and first-write-wins by URI.
- Corrections are stored in a separate append-only `corrections` table and synced by id.
- Skills are versioned by `bundle_sha256`.
- Sessions and turns are synced by `session_key` and turn id; `turn_count` is computed at read time.
- Uses globally unique URIs (e.g., `rmb://scenes/...`) for entities, memories, scenes, and skills.
- Provenance is used to key off distillation.

## Sync & Behavior

- Cross-instance behavior uses client-to-remote HTTP API.
- Sync resolves conflicts by syncing rows by id, unioning provenance, and re-distilling.
- No BitTorrent/DHT code in the stack.
- Not yet evaluated on the MemoryAgentBench benchmark.

memories.body:
## Overview
- rmb (recall memory bank) is the user's project, a memory system with categories Profile, Events, Preferences, and Entities.
- It is a client-server CLI tool for long-term memory, also a desktop app, a daemon (rmbd), and a web UI.
- It is a memory agent backend performing incremental ingestion, distillation, and retrieval.
- It is written in Go.

## Architecture
- Components: desktop app, daemon (rmbd), web UI, and CLI.
- The rmb application is served under the /ui/ path; the web UI is served under the /ui basePath.
- The rmb desktop web UI is served at http://127.0.0.1:19019/ui/.
- The rmb server hosts the server UI at /ui, serving an embedded static build at internal/http/static/web/ (including _next/ assets).
- The rmb app bundle identifier is me.remember.rmb.
- The rmb app binary is at ~/.rmb/bin/rmb-app; the CLI binary is at ~/.rmb/bin/rmb.
- The rmb configuration file is at ~/.rmb/config.yaml and points to the server https://rmb.colinleefish.com.
- The rmb desktop app stores its database at ~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/data/rmb.db.
- The rmb tool uses a hook mechanism where rmb-hook-dual calls rmb-desktop.
- rmb is a repository for static assets of the RMB project (separate from the main repo? unclear, but as stated).

## Storage & Sync
- Memories are stored in a versioned, append-only 'memories' table keyed by URI.
- There is a separate append-only 'corrections' table.
- RMB memories are append-only version chains with a single active row per URI.
- RMB events are immutable and first-write-wins by URI.
- RMB corrections are append-only and synced by id.
- RMB skills are versioned by bundle_sha256.
- RMB sessions and turns are synced by session_key and turn id.
- Session turn_count is computed at read time, not stored on the session row.
- RMB uses provenance to key off distillation.
- RMB sync resolves conflicts by syncing rows by id, unioning provenance, and re-distilling.
- rmb has a recall_stats table keyed by URI; recall stats are recorded server-side via rmb search/cat/meta commands.
- The rmb server requires migration 00023_recall_stats.sql for recall stats.
- rmb normalizes skill file paths to rmb://skills/<slug>.
- rmb is a system with entities memories, scenes, and skills, using globally unique URIs like rmb://scenes/...

## Integrations
- RMB integrates with Cursor and Claude Code, and also supports CC, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi via internal/setup/ package with detect, preview, and apply functions.
- Cursor integration requires two artifacts: hooks.json and user rules.
- Claude Code integration requires two artifacts: settings.json and a recall file.
- RMB requires a preview-before-apply workflow for configuration changes.

## Deployment & Hosting
- The rmb repository is hosted at github.com/colinleefish/rmb (owned by the user).
- The rmb repository is deployed via Docker only (using `make deploy`), not Vercel.
- The production service is hosted at https://rmb.colinleefish.com.
- The rmb base auth credentials are rmb:sVf3^n5ht.

## Development & Location
- The rmb project is located at /Users/liguanghui/Virginia/colinleefish/rmb.
- The rmb project has a UI component named rmb-ui.

## Other
- RMB currently has no BitTorrent/DHT code in its stack.
- RMB's cross-instance behavior uses client-to-remote HTTP API.
- rmb has not been evaluated on the MemoryAgentBench benchmark.
- The RMB app currently has no auto-update mechanism; updates are manual via DMG download, and a bootstrap refreshes ~/.rmb/bin/ sidecars on launch when bundled binaries are newer.

# rmbd Service

- **Role**: Local UI server/daemon on the user's laptop, hosting the PI agent and serving the dashboard UI.
- **Management**: Managed by launchd via a LaunchAgent.
- **Endpoint**: Runs at `http://127.0.0.1:19019`.

# Strategy A (缩量首板 + 整理)

- **Definition**: A trading strategy based on low-volume first boards followed by consolidation.

## Performance
- Based on 1,270 signals since 2024:
  - 43% 20-day loss rate
  - 18% of signals dropped over 10%
  - 6% dropped over 20%

## Bad Case Categories
1. Direct decline after first board (no second wave)
2. Bull trap (诱多)
3. Fake second wave
4. Failed Ke Chuan-style washout

## Warning Signals
- **Second wave interval < 5 days**: Indicates a fake second wave and higher failure rate.
- **First-board 5-day drop > 15%**: Warning signal for a bad case.

memories.abstract: rmb is a Go/React client-server CLI tool for long-term memory with desktop app, daemon, web UI, and agent integrations (Cursor, CC, Codex, OpenCode, Pi).
memories.body:
# rmb (Recall Memory Bank)

## Overview
- rmb is the user's project: a client-server CLI tool for long-term memory, written in Go with a React frontend.
- It is a memory system with categories: Profile, Events, Preferences, and Entities.
- It provides detect, preview, and apply functions for agent integration in the `internal/setup/` package, supporting Cursor, CC, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi.
- It has not been evaluated on the MemoryAgentBench benchmark.
- RMB is a memory layer that serves all AI agents. It is a macOS desktop app distributed as a .dmg, built with Tauri, and bundles `rmb` and `rmbd` binaries synced to `~/.rmb/bin/`.

## Components
- **Desktop app**: bundle ID `me.remember.rmb`, binary at `~/.rmb/bin/rmb-app`, database at `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/data/rmb.db`.
- **Daemon**: `rmbd`.
- **Web UI**: served under `/ui/` path; desktop web UI at `http://127.0.0.1:19019/ui/`, server UI at `/ui`. Web UI source located at `rmb-desktop/webui`.
- **CLI**: binary at `~/.rmb/bin/rmb`, config at `~/.rmb/config.yaml` pointing to server `https://rmb.colinleefish.com`. Provides recall rules via `rmb://agent` and `rmb:recall`.
- **UI component**: `rmb-ui`, includes `RecallRuleCopy`.
- **Hook mechanism**: `rmb-hook-dual` calls `rmb-desktop`.
- **Repository**: hosted at `github.com/colinleefish/rmb`, local path `/Users/liguanghui/Virginia/colinleefish/rmb`. Also serves as a repository for static assets of the RMB project.

## Integrations
- **Cursor**: requires `hooks.json` and user rules. Integration merges `rmb hook-submit` into the `hooks.stop` array of `~/.cursor/hooks.json`, preserving all other hook events. Detection checks if `hooks.stop` contains `rmb hook-submit`. Uses `./hooks/audit.sh` and adds `timeout: 15` when missing.
- **Claude Code**: requires `settings.json` and a recall file.
- **CLI integration**: provides recall rules (`rmb:recall`).
- **Workflow**: requires a preview-before-apply workflow for configuration changes.
- The rmb server repo has working integrations for OpenCode and Pi.

## Storage & Sync
- Memories are stored in a versioned, append-only `memories` table keyed by URI, with a single active row per URI.
- Events are immutable and first-write-wins by URI.
- Corrections are append-only and synced by id.
- Skills are versioned by `bundle_sha256` and normalized to `rmb://skills/<slug>`.
- Sessions and turns are synced by `session_key` and turn id.
- Session `turn_count` is computed at read time, not stored on the session row.
- Sync resolves conflicts by syncing rows by id, unioning provenance, and re-distilling.
- Provenance keys off distillation.
- Recall stats are recorded server-side via `rmb search/cat/meta` commands, requiring migration `00023_recall_stats.sql`.
- Cross-instance behavior uses client-to-remote HTTP API.
- No BitTorrent/DHT code in the stack.

## Deployment & Configuration
- Production service hosted at `https://rmb.colinleefish.com`.
- Deployed via Docker only (using `make deploy`), not Vercel.
- Server embeds its web UI static assets under `internal/http/static/web/` (including `_next/`).
- Base auth credentials: `rmb:sVf3^n5ht`.
- No auto-update mechanism; updates are manual via DMG download, and a bootstrap refreshes `~/.rmb/bin/` sidecars on launch when bundled binaries are newer.
- The rmb tool detects configuration when both `# RMB memory` and `ALWAYS RUN \`rmb\` cli` are present; old `<!-- rmb:recall:start/end -->` markers remain compatible.

## Distribution & Signing
- Distributed via re-mem-ber.me and GitHub Releases.
- Not signed with an Apple Developer certificate.
- Tauri updater is inactive (`active: false`).

## Technical Details
- `rmb` CLI version command prints `'rmb dev'` instead of a real semver.
- `/healthz` endpoint does not return the app version; it is at `127.0.0.1:19019`.
- The rmb project has a Go backend and a React frontend.

## Architecture & Services

memories.abstract: Starlink is a project management platform for multiple games, with services, Kafka, databases, storage, and CI/CD infrastructure.
memories.body:
# Starlink

Starlink is a project management platform and permission management system for hosting games and services. It integrates with the cehua AI platform and the planning side (策划). It serves multiple games: BlockCrush, BlockBlast, JDMJ, MJWD, Mahjong Wonders, and others. It is a team in the Aliyun caikuai-cn bill.

## Repositories
- Contains repositories: `solutionhub`, `hs-code-keeper`, `pm-1-frontend`, `pm-1-backend`.
- Includes the PM (Project Management) application.

## Services & Infrastructure
- **BBC**: Python write backend.
- **Frontend (SolutionHub)**: PM UI.
- **wirerope-gql**: Rust GraphQL read API.
- **Ding**: OpenResty gateway.
- **starflow**, **vector**, **hfrog**, **pgpour**, **fakeuser** (LGH only).
- Includes the **hs-code-keeper** codebase.
- Uses Host isolation for projects (no appname field).
- Jenkins instance at `devops-jenkins.hs99.vip` with jobs for services including `attachments` and `hfrog`.
- Attachments service has Jenkins pipelines.
- Nginx/OpenResty routes `/attachments/` to the `starlink-attachments` service.
- Proxy preset target: `https://pm-1-dev.hs99.vip`.
- Remote environment at `starlink.hs99.vip` serves as proxy target for GraphQL and passport endpoints.

## Environments & Hosting
- Dev all-in-one server: `archteam-starlink-dev-all-in-one` (hosts JDMJ LGH environment).
- Production environment: `archteam-starlink-jdmj-prod-1`.
- LGH environment: `/data/starlink-lgh-jdmj/`.
- Has 6 game variants and 14 dev environments, each with ~14 services.
- Uses Jenkins for CI/CD (e.g., blockblast environments).
- Production system hosted at `starlink.youxi123.com`.
- Also hosted at `lgh-jdmj.ext.hs99.vip` and `lgh-jdmj.hs99.vip`.
- Services hosted on `hs99.vip` domain.
- Production environment uses Aliyun VPC registry for BBC; frontend, gql, starflow use `registry.hs99.vip`.

## Storage
- Uses MinIO (server at 10.254.3.107) and Aliyun OSS.
- Artifacts stored in MinIO, migrating to OSS.
- Buckets: `starlink-blockcrush-pm-artifacts`, `starlink-artifacts-prd`, `starlink-jdmj-pm-artifacts-public`.
- Two-bucket architecture per game (private and public).
- Credential file: `e.credentials/starlink/pm-artifacts-oss.txt`.
- RAM policy v2 covering four buckets.
- hfrog s3.ini template for bucket types.
- `/download` endpoint does not redirect to presigned URL (404 in prod, error in dev).
- During PoC migration, only `task-acceptance` prefix was migrated; `art-submit` prefix not copied.
- Attachments store paths as relative URLs like `/attachments/{key}/{filename}`.
- `starlink-attachments` 302 responses include `Content-Disposition: inline; filename*` from OSS metadata.
- Inline disposition in Chrome downloads results in hash filenames; attachment disposition works correctly.

## Kafka
- Topic naming convention: `starlink.{game}.{env}.{schema}.{table}`.
- Feature config workflow topic: `biz.starlink.{game}.{env}.public.feature_config_workflow_info`.
- Environment variable `KAFKA_STARLINK_UPDATE_DATA_TOPIC` with prefix `biz.starlink.{game}.{env}.public`.
- Outbox topic via `KAFKA_PLAN_STATE_SYNC_TOPICS`.
- Biz topics filtered by Lua to project only update events with whitelist fields; raw topics contain full CDC envelope.
- Has a forwarder component for outbox events.
- Production topic example: `biz.starlink.blockcrush.prd.public.feature_config_workflow_info` (3 partitions, replication factor 2, 3-day retention).
- Environment suffixes: `lgh` (test) and `prd` (production) in topic names.
- Planner consumption outbox topic pattern: `biz.starlink.jdmj.{env}.public._pm_idea_flow_outbox_event`.
- Inner topics are internal and not for planners.
- Environment variable `KAFKA_PLAN_STATE_SYNC_TOPICS` used for planning state sync topics.

## Databases
- Shared-services RDS: `archteam-starlink-prd-shared-services.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com`.
- Database `fework_prd_db` with tables: `app_group`, `app_info`, `app_login`, `release`, `work`.
- `app_info` stores game registration (app_id, app_name, app_web_url, group_id, sort_order, create_time).
- `app_login` stores SSO hostname mapping (app_id, host).
- User `fework_prd_user` owns the tables.
- PostgreSQL RDS instance has application users `prd_blockbloom_client` and `prd_blockbloom_codekeeper`; no postgres superuser.
- On shared-services instance, stacks use `starlink_<slug>_client` and `starlink_<slug>_codekeeper` naming; `prd_*` reserved for dedicated per-game RDS.
- Multiple client databases: STP, BC, JDMJ, MJWD.
- Outbox event table named `_pm_idea_flow_outbox_event` (not old `pm.iceo.flow.outbox.event`).

## Permissions
- Workcodes are 6-digit zero-padded.
- Permissions stored in `avatar.role` JSONB array in each game's codekeeper database.

## Other
- Has a runbook for adding new games.
- Uses Aliyun EventBridge and OSS, with hook endpoint at `starlink-jade-mahjong.youxi123.com`.
- Hostnames include `starlink-jade-mahjong.youxi123.com` and `lgh-jdmj.hs99.vip`.
- Includes a blockcrush component.
- Includes an attachments service.

memories.abstract: rmb (Recall Memory Bank) is a Go-based client-server CLI memory system for AI agents, with desktop and server builds, supporting multiple agents, a web UI, and versioned append-only storage.
memories.body:
# rmb (Recall Memory Bank)

## Overview
- rmb is the user's project: a memory system with categories Profile, Events, Preferences, and Entities.
- It is a client-server CLI tool for long-term memory, written in Go with a React frontend.
- It provides detect, preview, and apply functions for agent integration in the `internal/setup/` package, supporting Cursor, CC, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi.
- It has not been evaluated on the MemoryAgentBench benchmark.
- RMB is a memory layer that serves all AI agents.
- It is a CLI tool that provides recall rules via `rmb://agent`.
- It captures agent sessions and provides a WebUI.

## Components
- Desktop app (bundle ID `me.remember.rmb`, binary at `~/.rmb/bin/rmb-app`), daemon (`rmbd`), and web UI.
- Desktop app stores its database at `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/data/rmb.db` and serves UI at `http://127.0.0.1:19019/ui/`.
- Server is hosted at `https://rmb.colinleefish.com`; config at `~/.rmb/config.yaml` points to that server.
- The rmb server serves its UI from an embedded static build at `internal/http/static/web/` (including `_next/` assets).
- The rmb tool uses a hook mechanism where `rmb-hook-dual` calls `rmb-desktop`.
- The rmb application is served under the `/ui/` path.
- Web UI located at `rmb-desktop/webui`.
- Integration pages for Cursor, OpenCode, and Pi.

## Storage & Sync
- Memories are stored in a versioned, append-only `memories` table keyed by URI, with a single active row per URI.
- Corrections are stored in a separate append-only `corrections` table, synced by id.
- Events are immutable and first-write-wins by URI.
- Skills are versioned by `bundle_sha256`; skill file paths are normalized to `rmb://skills/<slug>`.
- Sessions and turns are synced by `session_key` and turn id; `turn_count` is computed at read time.
- Sync resolves conflicts by syncing rows by id, unioning provenance, and re-distilling.
- Provenance keys off distillation.
- Recall stats are recorded server-side via `rmb search/cat/meta` commands, stored in a `recall_stats` table keyed by URI (requires migration `00023_recall_stats.sql`).
- Cross-instance behavior uses client-to-remote HTTP API; no BitTorrent/DHT code.

## Integrations
- Integrates with Cursor and Claude Code.
- Cursor integration requires two artifacts: `hooks.json` and user rules.
- Claude Code integration requires two artifacts: `settings.json` and a recall file.
- Cursor hook merge logic only modifies the `hooks.stop` array, preserving all other hook events and entries.
- Hook detection (`hook_status: configured`) checks whether `hooks.stop` contains `rmb hook-submit`.
- The Cursor hook uses `./hooks/audit.sh` and the `rmb hook-submit` command, adding `timeout: 15` when missing.
- Configuration changes require a preview-before-apply workflow.
- Supports session capture from five agents: Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi.
- Supports Codex as a hook source.
- Working integrations for OpenCode and Pi (server repo).

## Deployment & Repository
- Repository hosted at `github.com/colinleefish/rmb` (owned by the user).
- Deployed via Docker only (using `make deploy`), not Vercel.
- Production site: `https://rmb.colinleefish.com`.
- Local project path: `/Users/liguanghui/Virginia/colinleefish/rmb`.
- No auto-update mechanism; updates are manual via DMG download, with a bootstrap that refreshes `~/.rmb/bin/` sidecars on launch when bundled binaries are newer.
- Base auth credentials: `rmb:sVf3^n5ht`.
- Distributed via re-mem-ber.me and GitHub Releases.
- Not signed with an Apple Developer certificate.
- Tauri updater is inactive (active: false).

## UI
- Has a UI component named `rmb-ui` and a `RecallRuleCopy` UI component.
- The rmb server hosts the server UI at `/ui`.
- Web UI located at `rmb-desktop/webui`.
- Integration pages for Cursor, OpenCode, and Pi.

## Backends & CLI
- Two backends:
  - Desktop build: local SQLite at `127.0.0.1:19019`.
  - Server build: remote at `https://rmb.colinleefish.com`.
- Desktop CLI at `~/.rmb/bin/rmb`; server CLI at `rmb/bin/rmb`.
- Desktop CLI lacks the bootstrap that the server CLI has; running with no args prints usage instead of profile/agent/skills.
- Server CLI provides 20+ skills including JumpServer and humanizer.
- Local profile is in Chinese and sparse; server profile is in English and detailed.

## Configuration Detection
- Detected when both `# RMB memory` and `ALWAYS RUN \`rmb\` cli` are present.
- Old `<!-- rmb:recall:start/end -->` markers remain compatible.

## Endpoints & Versioning
- Healthz endpoint at `127.0.0.1:19019`.
- `/healthz` does not return the app version.
- `rmb` CLI version command prints `'rmb dev'` instead of a real semver.

memories.body:
# rmb-desktop

rmb-desktop is a local-first desktop application for the RMB product, under active development by the user. It is hosted at [github.com/colinleefish/rmb-desktop](https://github.com/colinleefish/rmb-desktop) and is the desktop GUI version of the RMB tool.

## Overview
- **Type**: Desktop application (Tauri-based)
- **Platform**: macOS, built for Apple Silicon (aarch64)
- **Version**: 0.1.2 (latest known)
- **Developer**: The user
- **Product name**: RMB Desktop (appears in Finder and menu bar)
- **Installed at**: `/Applications/rmb.app` with display name `rmb`

## Architecture
- Tauri-based desktop app with a tray shell (RMB.app), a CLI (`rmb`), and a daemon (`rmbd-desktop`).
- Bundles a CLI, daemon, and Tauri menubar app; binaries are synced to `~/.rmb/bin/` on startup if newer.
- First-run bootstrap copies bundled binaries to `~/.rmb/bin/` and installs a LaunchAgent for `rmbd`.
- Uses **SQLite in WAL mode** with memory layers L0–L3; stores data locally and does not send data to any server.
- Explicitly rejects iCloud or Dropbox for sync due to corruption risk.
- Daemon (`rmbd`) listens on `127.0.0.1:19019` and exposes a `/healthz` endpoint returning SQLite and vector status.
- Uses goose migrations on `rmbd` start; stop→migrate→restart orchestration is not yet built.

## UI & Web
- Embeds a Vite-built web UI via `go:embed`; assets are copied from `webui/dist` by `make webui-build`.
- `internal/http/static/web/` is generated output only; source of truth is in `webui/`.
- WebUI dev server started with `npm run dev:mock-setup`.
- Sidebar uses a Lucide Brain icon as placeholder brand mark; favicon is a purple gradient SVG at `ui/public/favicon.svg`.
- Settings page has tabs General, Models, and Advanced, with Integrations as a top-level sidebar item.
- Browser title and Tauri app name are both 'RMB Desktop'.

## Data & Privacy
- Local-first; does not report installs or heartbeats.
- Has a `recall_stats` table keyed by URI.
- Supports OpenAI-compatible API format for LLM and embedding providers.
- Integrations exist for Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi; currently writes shell hooks for OpenCode and Pi (incorrect for these agents).

## Distribution
- Currently at version 0.1.2; Tauri updater is disabled (`updater.active: false`).
- Distributed as a DMG for macOS (aarch64) via GitHub Releases and Cloudflare R2 at `releases.re-mem-ber.me`.
- Planned packaging: DMG for macOS, MSI/EXE for Windows, AppImage/DEB for Linux.
- Packaged via `make app-build` and `finish-dmg.sh`.

## Development
- Project located at `/Users/liguanghui/Virginia/colinleefish/rmb-desktop` with a `webui` subdirectory.
- CLI expected at `~/.rmb/bin/rmb`; daemon expected at `~/.rmb/bin/rmbd-desktop`.
- Uses `make webui-build` to regenerate embedded assets; these must not be edited by hand.
- Currently under development and testing by the user.

## Configuration
- Config file: `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/config.yaml`
- General settings page includes:
  - Display language
  - Distillation database path
  - Config file collection address
- Launch-at-login setting stored in `config.yaml` under `launch_at_login`; registers a LaunchAgent at `~/Library/LaunchAgents/me.remember.rmb.plist`.

## Onboarding
- Marker file: `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/onboarding.complete`
- Contains JSON with `completed_at` and `skipped_agents`.
- API endpoints:
  - `GET /api/v1/onboarding/status`
  - `POST /api/v1/onboarding/complete`
  - `POST /api/v1/onboarding/reset`

## Testing
- Tested on the quick whale VM.

memories.body:
# Starlink

Starlink is a project management platform and permission management system that hosts games and services, including BlockCrush, BlockBlast, JDMJ, MJWD, N8N, pgpour, Guofeng Mahjong, Jade Mahjong, and Block Bloom. It is the infrastructure project for Jade Mahjong and is managed by the user with sub-projects `blockcrush` and `jdmj`. The product has APP_ID `starlink_pm`.

## Architecture
- **Services**: BBC (Python write backend), frontend (SolutionHub), wirerope-gql (Rust GraphQL read API), Ding (OpenResty gateway), starflow, vector, hfrog, pgpour, and fakeuser (LGH only).
- Integrates with the cehua AI platform for creative ideas, star map review, and workflow events.
- Uses Host isolation for projects (no appname field).
- Repositories: `solutionhub`, `hs-code-keeper`, `pm-1-frontend`, `pm-1-backend`.
- Includes a PM (Project Management) application and an attachments service.
- Jenkins jobs exist for services including attachments and hfrog.

## Environments
- **Production**: `starlink.hs99.vip` (hosted on `archteam-starlink-hs99-vip-prd`, IP `10.100.116.152`, stack directory `/data/starlink-hs99-vip`). Also referenced as `starlink.youxi123.com`.
- **Test/Dev**: `pm-1-dev.hs99.vip` (hosted on `archteam-starlink-dev-all-in-one`, IP `10.100.64.132`, stack directory `/data/starlink-pm-1-dev`). Also `lgh-jdmj.ext.hs99.vip` is used.
- Dev all-in-one server: `archteam-starlink-dev-all-in-one` (hosts JDMJ LGH environment).
- Production: `archteam-starlink-jdmj-prod-1`; LGH environment at `/data/starlink-lgh-jdmj/`.
- 6 game variants and 14 dev environments, each with ~14 services.
- Production bbc service uses Aliyun VPC registry; frontend, gql, and starflow use `registry.hs99.vip`.
- Jenkins instance: `devops-jenkins.hs99.vip`.
- Proxy preset target: `https://pm-1-dev.hs99.vip`.

## Storage
- Uses MinIO (server at 10.254.3.107) and Aliyun OSS; artifacts are being migrated from MinIO to OSS.
- Two-bucket architecture per game (private and public).
- Buckets include `starlink-blockcrush-pm-artifacts`, `starlink-artifacts-prd`, `starlink-jdmj-pm-artifacts-public`.
- Credential file: `e.credentials/starlink/pm-artifacts-oss.txt`; RAM policy v2 covers four buckets.
- Artifact upload URLs stored in `pm_work_item_meta` table.
- During PoC migration, only `task-acceptance` prefix was copied to OSS; `art-submit` prefix was not.

## Messaging
- Kafka topics follow naming conventions: `biz.starlink.{game}.{env}.public.feature_config_workflow_info` and `starlink.{game}.{env}.{schema}.{table}`.
- Outbox topic configured via `KAFKA_PLAN_STATE_SYNC_TOPICS`; forwarder component handles outbox events.
- Biz topics are filtered by Lua to project only update events with a whitelist of fields; raw topics contain full CDC envelope.
- Uses Kafka topics with environment suffixes `lgh` (test) and `prd` (production).
- Example topic: `biz.starlink.blockcrush.prd.public.feature_config_workflow_info` (3 partitions, replication factor 2, 3-day retention).
- Planner consumption outbox topic pattern: `biz.starlink.jdmj.{env}.public._pm_idea_flow_outbox_event`.
- Inner topics are internal and not for planners.
- Prefixes blockbloom topics (e.g., `starlink.blockbloom.lgh.public.*`).
- Outbox event table is `_pm_idea_flow_outbox_event` (not old `pm.iceo.flow.outbox.event`).

## Database
- Shared-services RDS: `archteam-starlink-prd-shared-services.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com`.
- Database `fework_prd_db` (owned by `fework_prd_user`) contains tables: `app_group`, `app_info`, `app_login`, `release`, `work`.
- `app_info` stores game registration (app_id, app_name, app_web_url, group_id, sort_order, create_time).
- `app_login` stores SSO hostname mapping (app_id as SSO numeric ID, host as domain).
- PostgreSQL RDS instance has users `prd_blockbloom_client` and `prd_blockbloom_codekeeper`; no postgres superuser.
- On shared-services instance, naming convention: `starlink_<slug>_client` and `starlink_<slug>_codekeeper`; `prd_*` reserved for dedicated per-game RDS.
- Dev all-in-one RDS: `starlink-dev-all-in-one.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com` (Aliyun), with 41 databases and 5 pgpour containers for CDC replication.
- Dev databases: `pm1_dev_client` and `pm1_dev_codekeeper`, seeded from production.
- Production database for BlockCrush: `prd_blockcrush_client`.
- Dev RDS also hosts `mx_blockcrush_client`.
- Client databases include STP, BC, JDMJ, and MJWD.

## Attachments
- Stores attachment paths as relative URLs like `/attachments/{key}/{filename}`.
- nginx/OpenResty routes `/attachments/` to the `starlink-attachments` service.
- 302 responses include `Content-Disposition: inline; filename*` from OSS metadata.
- Inline disposition in Chrome downloads results in hash filenames; attachment disposition works correctly.

## Permissions
- Permissions stored in `avatar.role` JSONB array in each game's codekeeper database.
- Workcodes are 6-digit zero-padded.

## Additional
- Creative evaluation system with stakeholder review (art and dev gates).
- Uses Aliyun EventBridge and OSS; hook endpoint at `starlink-jade-mahjong.youxi123.com`.
- Runbook exists for adding new games.
- Hostnames include `starlink-jade-mahjong.youxi123.com` and `lgh-jdmj.hs99.vip`.
- The `/download` endpoint does not redirect to presigned URL (404 in production, error in dev).
- Cehua Kafka messages overwrite `feature_config.url_doc` with last-write-wins; no FC→PM reverse sync for the doc link.
- Starlink is the system that receives creative ideas from the planning platform.

memories.abstract: BBC is a Flask-based backend service in the Starlink platform for game backends and PM work items, handling login verification, Avatar scopes, and PM meta upserts.
memories.body:
# BBC (hs-code-keeper)

BBC is a backend service in the Starlink platform, deployed via Jenkins. It is a Python write backend (hs-code-keeper/bbc) and a Flask 3 + SQLAlchemy 2 REST API backend for PM-1. It handles building and deploying game backends keyed by APP_ID, and is part of the starlink-blockbloom project with config at `/data/starlink-blockbloom-prod/config/bbc/env.prod` and also `config/bbc/env.prod`. It runs with `uv run app.py dwb starlink_pm` and serves REST API on port 12124.

## Scope and Authentication
- Contains `EAvatarScope` enum and `Avatar.get_scope()` logic.
- Login API returns two scope lists: cookie (user_info) contains only `:v` scopes; API `data.task.scope` contains non-`:v` API permission strings.
- Verifies login tickets by calling SSO's `ADDR_SSO_VERIFY_TICKET` endpoint.

## PM Work Items
- Handles PM work item meta upsert via REST endpoint `/pm/work_item/meta/upsert` and reads via GraphQL.
- Database table: `pm_work_item_meta`.
- Shares the `codekeeper` database with the `fakeuser` service.

## Games
- BBC project includes games: BlockCrush, JDMJ, MJWD, BlockBlast, BlockMJ, SandCrush.

## Caching
- Uses Flask-Caching; caches Avatar by `avatar_cache_{avatar_id}` with default TTL 60s.

## Configuration and Environment
- Uses `envs/block_crush/.env.mx` for configuration.
- In lsx-mjwd system, healthy, connected to `lsx_mjwd_client` database on RDS.
- Running locally with `pm1_dev` database.
- v3.4.6-lite migration runs inside BBC, requires BBC image with Python migrate module.

## Team and Management
- BBC team manages backend code and DDL changes relevant to `pgpour`.

- Uses MinIO (production) and Aliyun OSS (development) for object storage.
- Two-bucket architecture per game (private and public).
- Buckets: starlink-blockcrush-pm-artifacts, starlink-artifacts-prd, starlink-jdmj-pm-artifacts-public, etc.
- Artifact upload URLs stored in pm_work_item_meta table.
- Migration from MinIO to OSS in progress; some prefixes (art-submit) not copied during PoC.
- Credential file: e.credentials/starlink/pm-artifacts-oss.txt.
- RAM policy v2 covers four buckets.
- hfrog s3.ini template for bucket types.
- Attachments stored as relative URLs: `/attachments/{key}/{filename}`; nginx/OpenResty routes `/attachments/` to the starlink-attachments service.
- 302 responses include `Content-Disposition: inline; filename*` from OSS metadata; inline disposition in Chrome results in hash filenames, attachment disposition works correctly.

## Kafka
- Topic naming: `starlink.{game}.{env}.{schema}.{table}` and `biz.starlink.{game}.{env}.public.feature_config_workflow_info`.
- Environment variable `KAFKA_STARLINK_UPDATE_DATA_TOPIC` with prefix `biz.starlink.{game}.{env}.public`.
- Outbox topic configured via `KAFKA_PLAN_STATE_SYNC_TOPICS`.
- Biz topics filtered by Lua to project only update events with whitelist of fields; raw topics contain full CDC envelope.
- Forwarder component for outbox events.
- Uses environment suffixes `lgh` (test) and `prd` (production) in topic names.
- Example topic: `biz.starlink.blockcrush.prd.public.feature_config_workflow_info` (3 partitions, replication factor 2, 3-day retention).
- Planner consumption outbox topic pattern: `biz.starlink.jdmj.{env}.public._pm_idea_flow_outbox_event`.
- Outbox event table: `_pm_idea_flow_outbox_event` (not old `pm.iceo.flow.outbox.event`).
- Inner topics are internal and not for planners.
- Prefixes blockbloom topics like `starlink.blockbloom.lgh.public.*`.

## Database
- PostgreSQL RDS instance: `archteam-starlink-prd-shared-services.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com`.
- Database `fework_prd_db` with tables: app_group, app_info, app_login, release, work.
- app_info stores game registration (app_id, app_name, app_web_url, group_id, sort_order, create_time).
- app_login stores SSO hostname mapping (app_id, host).
- User `fework_prd_user` owns tables.
- Application users: `prd_blockbloom_client`, `prd_blockbloom_codekeeper`; no postgres superuser.
- On shared-services instance: `starlink_<slug>_client` and `starlink_<slug>_codekeeper`; `prd_*` reserved for dedicated per-game RDS.
- Dev all-in-one RDS: `starlink-dev-all-in-one.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com`, with 41 databases and 5 pgpour containers for CDC replication.
- Dev databases: `pm1_dev_client` and `pm1_dev_codekeeper`, seeded from production.
- Production database for BlockCrush: `prd_blockcrush_client`.
- Also hosts `mx_blockcrush_client` on the same RDS.
- Multiple client databases: STP, BC, JDMJ, MJWD.

## Environments
- 6 game variants, 14 dev environments, each with ~14 services.
- Production and LGH environments for JDMJ.
- Production: starlink.hs99.vip (also starlink.youxi123.com), hosted on archteam-starlink-hs99-vip-prd.
- Test/Dev: pm-1-dev.hs99.vip, hosted on archteam-starlink-dev-all-in-one. Also reachable at lgh-jdmj.ext.hs99.vip.
- Proxy preset target: https://pm-1-dev.hs99.vip.

## Permissions
- Workcodes are 6-digit zero-padded.
- Permissions stored in `avatar.role` JSONB array in each game's codekeeper database.

## Other
- APP_ID: `starlink_pm`.
- Cehua Kafka messages overwrite `feature_config.url_doc` with last-write-wins; no FC→PM reverse sync for the doc link.
- BlockCrush BBC container: `starlink-mx-blockcrush-bbc-1`.
- Runbook for adding new games.
- Uses Jenkins for CI/CD (for blockblast environments).
- Uses Aliyun EventBridge and OSS with hook endpoint at starlink-jade-mahjong.youxi123.com.
- Part of Aliyun caikuai-cn billing team.

## Notable Issues
- `/download` endpoint does not redirect to presigned URL; returns 404 in production, error in dev.
- art-submit prefix objects not copied to OSS during migration.

- Single-instance lock

- Status menu item opening the browser Dashboard
- Quit item

- No Tauri window or WebView; UI is served by rmbd at /ui/ and opened in a browser.

- Binary size about 6.3MB

- Integrates with OpenCode, Pi, Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex.

memories.body:
# Starlink

Starlink (星链) is a project management, permission management, and game config platform at HungryStudio. It receives creative ideas from the planning platform and supports A/B tests, dev pipelines, and multi-env deployments for games like BlockBlast, SandCrush, CrushBlast, Mahjong variants, and ADX. It integrates with the cehua AI platform, handling creative ideas, star map review, and workflow events for games. It uses a stakeholder review process with art and dev gates.

## Components
- **Frontend**: SolutionHub
- **BBC**: Python write backend
- **wirerope-gql**: Rust GraphQL read API
- **Ding**: OpenResty gateway
- **starflow**, **vector**, **hfrog**, **pgpour**, **fakeuser** (LGH only)
- Includes the **hs-code-keeper** codebase
- Repositories: `solutionhub`, `hs-code-keeper`, `pm-1-frontend`, `pm-1-backend`
- Includes an attachments service with Jenkins pipelines

## Environments
- **Production**: `starlink.youxi123.com` and `starlink.hs99.vip` (hosted on `archteam-starlink-hs99-vip-prd` at 10.100.116.152, stack dir `/data/starlink-hs99-vip`)
- **JDMJ Production**: `archteam-starlink-jdmj-prod-1`
- **LGH**: `/data/starlink-lgh-jdmj/`, hostname `lgh-jdmj.hs99.vip` and `lgh-jdmj.ext.hs99.vip`
- **Dev all-in-one**: `archteam-starlink-dev-all-in-one` (also `starlink-dev-all-in-one`) at 10.100.64.132, stack dir `/data/starlink-pm-1-dev`, hosts JDMJ LGH
- **Test/Dev**: `pm-1-dev.hs99.vip`
- 6 game variants, 14 dev environments, each with ~14 services
- Services hosted on `hs99.vip` domain
- In production, BBC uses Aliyun VPC registry; others use `registry.hs99.vip`

## Storage
- Uses MinIO (server at `10.254.3.107`) and Aliyun OSS
- Artifacts stored in MinIO, migrating to OSS
- Two-bucket architecture per game (private and public)
- Buckets: `starlink-blockcrush-pm-artifacts`, `starlink-artifacts-prd`, `starlink-jdmj-pm-artifacts-public`
- Credential file: `e.credentials/starlink/pm-artifacts-oss.txt`
- RAM policy v2 covering four buckets
- `hfrog` s3.ini template for bucket types
- Artifact upload URLs stored in `pm_work_item_meta` table
- `/download` endpoint does not redirect to presigned URL (404 in prod, error in dev)
- `art-submit` prefix not copied to OSS during PoC migration; only `task-acceptance` migrated
- Attachment paths stored as relative URLs like `/attachments/{key}/{filename}`
- `starlink-attachments` 302 responses include `Content-Disposition: inline; filename*` from OSS metadata; inline disposition in Chrome downloads results in hash filenames, while attachment disposition works correctly

## Messaging
- Kafka topics: `biz.starlink.{game}.{env}.public.feature_config_workflow_info`
- Prefix from `KAFKA_STARLINK_UPDATE_DATA_TOPIC`
- Outbox topic via `KAFKA_PLAN_STATE_SYNC_TOPICS`
- Biz topics filtered by Lua to project only update events with whitelist fields
- Topic naming convention: `starlink.{game}.{env}.{schema}.{table}`
- Uses Host isolation, no appname field
- Has a forwarder component for outbox events
- Production topic example: `biz.starlink.blockcrush.prd.public.feature_config_workflow_info` (3 partitions, replication factor 2, 3-day retention)
- Environment suffixes: `lgh` (test) and `prd` (production) in topic names
- Planner consumption outbox topic pattern: `biz.starlink.jdmj.{env}.public._pm_idea_flow_outbox_event`
- Inner topics are internal and not for planners
- Outbox event table: `_pm_idea_flow_outbox_event` (not old `pm.iceo.flow.outbox.event`)
- `starlink.blockcrush.dwb` streams PostgreSQL CDC data to Kafka topics with names `{topic_prefix}.{schema}.{table}`
- Prefixes blockbloom's Kafka topic names (e.g., `starlink.blockbloom.lgh.public.*`)
- Environment variable `KAFKA_PLAN_STATE_SYNC_TOPICS` used for planning state sync
- Cehua Kafka messages overwrite `feature_config.url_doc` with last-write-wins; no FC→PM reverse sync for doc link

## Database
- Shared-services RDS: `archteam-starlink-prd-shared-services.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com`
- Database `fework_prd_db` with tables: `app_group`, `app_info`, `app_login`, `release`, `work`
- `app_info` stores game registration (app_id, app_name, app_web_url, group_id, sort_order, create_time)
- `app_login` stores SSO hostname mapping (app_id, host)
- User `fework_prd_user` owns tables
- PostgreSQL RDS instance has application users `prd_blockbloom_client` and `prd_blockbloom_codekeeper`, no postgres superuser
- Dev all-in-one RDS on Aliyun: `starlink-dev-all-in-one.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com:5432` (user `solutionhub_dev`, password `pbVhQ8X1g99ByM`)
- Dev all-in-one RDS has 41 databases with CDC publications and runs 5 pgpour containers for CDC replication
- Production database `prd_blockcrush_client` exists
- Dev databases: `pm1_dev_client` and `pm1_dev_codekeeper`, seeded from production
- On shared-services instance, Starlink stacks use `starlink_<slug>_client` and `starlink_<slug>_codekeeper` naming; `prd_*` reserved for dedicated per-game RDS
- Multiple client databases: STP, BC, JDMJ, MJWD, `mx_blockcrush_client`, `lhh_blockblast_client`

## Permissions & Features
- Permission management system
- Workcodes are 6-digit zero-padded
- Permissions stored in `avatar.role` JSONB array in each game's codekeeper database
- Team configuration feature under 空间配置 → 团队
- Product APP_ID: `starlink_pm`
- Mini-bundle automation workflows store results in `lhh_blockblast_client` database

## Infrastructure

memories.body:
# JumpServer Bastion: jump.hs99.vip

## Overview
- **jump.hs99.vip** is the JumpServer bastion used to access hosts (e.g., `aliyun-perf-bbc`).
- It runs **KoKo SSH gateway** on port **2222**; only this port is exposed publicly.
- The associated rmb skill **`jump-hs99-vip`** (rmb://skills/jump-hs99-vip) lists hosts and runs SSH via this bastion. It is tagged as a work/operator skill.

## PostgreSQL Support
- JumpServer supports PostgreSQL as a first-class asset type (database platform, `postgresql` type).
- The connection-token API accepts `protocol=postgresql` and returns `201 Created` for `db_client`, `db_guide`, `native_db`, and `web_cli`.
- **XPACK enterprise license is disabled** (`XPACK_LICENSE_IS_VALID: False`), so the native DB-client proxy and the `chen` component are **unavailable**.
- All native DB proxy ports (5432, 54320, 33060, 30001, 8443, 8080) are closed on the public IP; only port 2222 is open.
- The KoKo SSH gateway (port 2222) **rejects database connection tokens**.
- However, `TERMINAL_OMNIDB_ENABLED` is `true`, so the in-browser **Web SQL terminal (OmniDB)** works for PostgreSQL assets.

## Access Method
- SSH access to hosts is via the KoKo gateway on port 2222.
- Database access is limited to the OmniDB web terminal; native clients or proxies are not available due to the disabled XPACK license and closed ports.

memories.abstract: Blockcrush is a Starlink sub-project (game and PM app) with production at starlink-blockcrush.youxi123.com, using prd_blockcrush_client DB, PM architecture with hfrog/OSS, Kafka replication, and specific schema features.
memories.body:
# Blockcrush

## Overview
- Game project integrated with cehua AI platform and Starlink.
- Also a project management (PM) application with PM UI and client library.
- Sub-project of Starlink, referred to as "bc".
- Component of Starlink system (game deployed in production).
- PostgreSQL RDS system with codekeeper and client databases.
- Credentials stored at `e.credentials/starlink/blockcrush.txt`.

## Environments
- Production host: `https://starlink-blockcrush.youxi123.com`
- LGH host: `https://lgh-blockcrush.ext.hs99.vip`
- Dev (lsx): `https://lsx-blockcrush.hs99.vip`
- Production servers: `app-1` and `app-2` (also `blockcrush-app-1` and `blockcrush-app-2`).
- Production BBC container: `starlink-blockcrush-prod-bbc-1` on hosts `blockcrush-app-1` and `blockcrush-app-2`.
- Production config at `/data/starlink-blockcrush-prod/`.
- Attachments service: `starlink-blockcrush.youxi123.com/attachments/`.
- Internal ALB: `archteam-starlink-blockcrush-prod-internal`, external ALB: `archteam-starlink-blockcrush-prod-external`.
- Attachments use `starfamily-registry-vpc.cn-beijing.cr.aliyuncs.com`.

## Databases
- Production database: `prd_blockcrush_client` at `archteam-starlink-blockcrush-pg16.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com`.
- Other databases: `lhh_blockcrush_client`, `lhh_blockcrush_hfrog`, `prd_blockcrush_codekeeper`.
- Staging: `lsx_blockcrush_client`.
- Dev (MX) database at `starlink-dev-all-in-one.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com`.
- MX has 8 tables production lacks (e.g., `pm_agent`, `pm_flow_parallel_run`, `pm_work_item_review_round`).
- Production has legacy columns `bucket_id` and `test_server_id` that MX dropped.
- Blockcrush is canonical schema target for production clients.
- Dev databases: `lsx_blockcrush_client` and `lgh_blockcrush_client` (possibly different dev instances).

## Redis
- Separate recommendation Redis (`REDIS_RECOMMEND_*`) isolated from cache Redis; must not FLUSHALL recommendation data.
- Dev Redis at `starlink-dev-internal.hs99.vip:31200 DB0`.

## PM Architecture
- Four-layer: frontend, hfrog, hfrog database, object storage.
- PM UI uses BBC for meta and hfrog for uploads.
- Uses BlockBlast's hfrog and shared MinIO bucket in production.
- PM artifacts migrated from MinIO to Aliyun OSS.
- UI reads `meta_value → file.url` for task acceptance videos.
- In production attachments service, no local hfrog or `s3_1.ini`; OSS credentials manually written to `config/attachments/env` using shared RAM user `starlink-pm-artifacts-oss`.
- Aliyun ACR login configured.

## PM Details
- Tracks requirements and creative ideas.
- Document links: PM requirements use `extra.creative_doc_link`; FC creatives use `feature_config.url_doc`.
- No reverse sync from creative to requirement; creative-to-requirement conversion copies a snapshot, and creative updates via Kafka do not propagate to the bound requirement.
- Priority mapping: `pm_work_item.priority`: urgent=10, high=8, medium=5, low=2.

## Replication & Kafka
- `wal_level` set to `logical`.
- `starlink` user has `REPLICATION` privilege.
- Active replication slot: `supabase_etl_apply_87142` (pgpour running).
- Runs pgpour on `archteam-starlink-pgpour-prd-all-in-one`.
- `bbc_publication` includes 5 tables: `_kafka_message_bi_solution`, `_pm_idea_flow_outbox_event`, `feature_config`, `feature_config_workflow_info`, `pm_work_item`.
- Production Kafka environment with topic pattern `JDMJ/blockcrush`.
- LGH and JDMJ lgh publications differ: BlockCrush lgh has `solution/solution_way`, JDMJ lgh has `_kafka_message_bi_solution`.
- Production CDC pipeline (87142) consumed by `pgpour` from `prd_blockcrush_client` database.

## Schema & Features
- JDMJ and BlockCrush schema differ only on `pm_project` table (3 columns).

# JumpServer Bastion: jump.hs99.vip

## Overview
- **jump.hs99.vip** is the JumpServer bastion used to access remote hosts (e.g., aliyun-perf-bbc, starlink hosts).
- Credentials are stored at `~/.hungrystudio/jump-hs99-vip`.
- The **jump-hs99-vip** skill on rmb (`rmb://skills/jump-hs99-vip`) lists hosts and runs SSH via this bastion; it is tagged as a work/operator skill.

## Access
- SSH access is via the **KoKo gateway on port 2222** (the only exposed port on the public IP).
- The KoKo gateway **rejects database connection tokens**.

## PostgreSQL Support
- PostgreSQL is a first-class asset type (database platform, `postgresql` type).
- The connection-token API accepts `protocol=postgresql` and returns `201 Created` for `db_client`, `db_guide`, `native_db`, and `web_cli`.
- **TERMINAL_OMNIDB_ENABLED** is `true`, so the in-browser Web SQL terminal (OmniDB) works for PostgreSQL assets.

## Limitations
- **XPACK enterprise license is disabled** (`XPACK_LICENSE_IS_VALID: False`), so the native DB-client proxy and the `chen` component are unavailable.
- All native DB proxy ports (5432, 54320, 33060, 30001, 8443, 8080) are closed on the public IP; only port 2222 is exposed.
