memories.abstract: BlockCrush (BC) is a game and PM app under Starlink, with production and dev environments, PostgreSQL RDS, Kafka, Redis, and PM/creative features.
memories.body:
# BlockCrush (BC)

BlockCrush is a game and project management (PM) application under the Starlink platform. It is integrated with the cehua AI platform and uses Starlink AI platform integration. It serves as a reference for Block Bloom (BlockBloom) specifications and its app configs were templates for BlockBloom. It is referred to as `bc` and is a sub-project of Starlink, with private and public buckets under Starlink. It is an older project whose settings remain in Block Bloom compose tree.

## Infrastructure
- Production hosts: `blockcrush-app-1` and `blockcrush-app-2`.
- Production host: https://starlink-blockcrush.youxi123.com.
- LGH environment: https://lgh-blockcrush.ext.hs99.vip.
- LSX environment: https://lsx-blockcrush.hs99.vip.
- Has `.ext` subdomain configuration on `hs99.vip`.
- Internal ALB: `archteam-starlink-blockcrush-prod-internal`; external ALB: `archteam-starlink-blockcrush-prod-external`.
- Production Kafka environment with topic pattern `JDMJ/blockcrush`.
- Runs `pgpour` on `archteam-starlink-pgpour-prd-all-in-one`.
- Aliyun ACR login configured.

## Database
- Production database: `prd_blockcrush_client` (hosted at `archteam-starlink-blockcrush-pg16.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com`).
- Also has `prd_blockcrush_codekeeper` database.
- Staging environment: `lsx_blockcrush_client`.
- MX (dev) database: `starlink-dev-all-in-one.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com` (has 8 extra tables like `pm_agent`, `pm_flow_parallel_run`, `pm_work_item_review_round`; production has legacy columns `bucket_id` and `test_server_id`).
- Uses `lhh_blockcrush_client` and `lhh_blockcrush_hfrog` databases.
- Publication `bbc_publication` includes 5 tables: `_kafka_message_bi_solution`, `_pm_idea_flow_outbox_event`, `feature_config`, `feature_config_workflow_info`, `pm_work_item`.
- `wal_level` logical, `starlink` user has `REPLICATION` privilege, active replication slot `supabase_etl_apply_87142`.
- Schema differs from JDMJ only on `pm_project` table (3 columns).
- Canonical schema target for production clients.
- Credentials stored at `e.credentials/starlink/blockcrush.txt`.

## Architecture
- Four-layer architecture: frontend, hfrog, hfrog database, object storage.
- PM UI uses BBC for meta and hfrog for uploads; does not connect directly to database.
- PM uses BlockBlast's hfrog and shared MinIO bucket in production.
- PM artifacts migrated from MinIO to Aliyun OSS; attachments service at `/attachments/`.
- UI reads `meta_value → file.url` to download task acceptance videos.
- OSS credentials manually written to `config/attachments/env` using shared RAM user `starlink-pm-artifacts-oss`.
- No local hfrog or `s3_1.ini` in production attachments service.

## Features
- Feature descriptions follow format `level·tag·name`; uses enum term `底板优化` for optimization labels.
- Includes PM AI agent and parallel flow subsystem.
- Has tables `pm_agent`, `pm_agent_flow_draft`, `pm_agent_run`, `pm_flow_step_deliverable`, `pm_flow_parallel_run`, `pm_flow_parallel_branch` that MJWD lacks.
- Has `pm_work_item`, `fc_workflow_info`, and avatar tables.

## Environments
- Production: `prd_blockcrush_client`, host `starlink-blockcrush.youxi123.com`.
- LGH: https://lgh-blockcrush.ext.hs99.vip.
- LSX: https://lsx-blockcrush.hs99.vip.
- MX (dev) environment.

## Deployment
- Production config: `/data/starlink-blockcrush-prod/`.
- Attachments use `starfamily-registry-vpc.cn-beijing.cr.aliyuncs.com`.
- Prod BBC container: `starlink-blockcrush-prod-bbc-1` on hosts `blockcrush-app-1` and `blockcrush-app-2`.
- Dev Redis: `starlink-dev-internal.hs99.vip:31200` DB0.

## Redis
- Uses a separate recommendation Redis (`REDIS_RECOMMEND_*`) isolated from its cache Redis.
- **Do not FLUSHALL recommendation data**.

## Project Management (PM) & Creative (FC)
- BlockCrush has a PM module tracking requirements and creative ideas.
- DingTalk doc links are stored in:
  - PM requirements: `extra.creative_doc_link`
  - FC creatives: `feature_config.url_doc`
- **No reverse sync** from creative to requirement; creative updates via Kafka do not propagate to the bound requirement, so links can diverge.
- `feature_config` data is managed via Excel `feature_name→feature_key` mappings, stored in `lgh_blockcrush_client` and `prd_blockcrush_client`.

## Priority Mapping
- `pm_work_item.priority`: urgent=10, high=8, medium=5, low=2.

## Timezone
- BBC application containers run with `/etc/timezone` set to `Etc/UTC` on both prd and dwb environments.
- PostgreSQL sessions inherit `Asia/Shanghai` timezone; no client forces UTC on connect.

## CDC Pipeline
- Production CDC pipeline (ID 87142) is consumed by `pgpour` from `prd_blockcrush_client`.

memories.abstract: pgpour is Starlink's internal Rust CDC tool that streams PostgreSQL WAL changes via logical replication to Kafka as Debezium-style JSON, running as Docker containers with Lua transforms, deployed across environments (prod host 10.100.64.62).
memories.body:
# pgpour

pgpour is Starlink's internal **PostgreSQL CDC to Kafka** tool. It reads WAL changes via PostgreSQL logical replication and publishes Debezium-style JSON to Kafka. It is written in Rust and runs as a Docker container on each Starlink stack.

## Deployment
- Runs as a Docker container on each Starlink stack.
- Production host: `archteam-starlink-pgpour-prd-all-in-one` (10.100.64.62), running three production containers (blockcrush, mjwd, blockblast).
- Production image tag: `8e8797b7` (registry.hs99.vip/starlink/pgpour:8e8797b7, includes array conversion fix).
- Not deployed on `archteam-starlink-jdmj-prod-1`; uses a dedicated pgpour machine.
- Also runs on `archteam-starlink-dev-all-in-one` (e.g., `starlink-lgh-blockcrush-pgpour-1` with `with_init: false`).
- Deployed across multiple environments.

## Configuration
- Config path pattern: `/data/starlink-{env}-{game}/config/pgpour/config.yml`.
- Production config example: `/data/starlink-jdmj-pgpour-prod/config/pgpour/config.yml`.
- Uses a hybrid config: YAML file plus secret environment variables.
- Topic naming convention: `{topic_prefix}.{schema}.{table}`.
- Uses PostgreSQL logical replication slots (e.g., `supabase_etl_apply_75821`).
- Does not allow two targets with the same `topic_prefix` on the same brokers.

## Features
- Supports Lua transforms for filtering/cleaning CDC data.
- DLQ routing for errors.
- Built-in helpers: `keep`, `drop_nulls`, `rename`, `now_ms`.
- Supports raw and biz targets with Lua transforms.
- Streams PostgreSQL changes to Kafka (e.g., `bbc_publication` table, merged `feature_config_workflow_info` table).

## Instances / Pipelines
- **jdmj**: container `starlink-jdmj-pgpour-prod-pgpour-1`, config at `/data/starlink-jdmj-pgpour-prod/config/pgpour/config.yml`.
- **dwb-blockcrush**: defined in docker-compose.yml behind `cdc-disabled` profile, config at `/data/starlink-dwb-blockcrush/config/pgpour/config.yml`.
- **lgh-blockcrush**: container `starlink-lgh-blockcrush-pgpour-1`, config at `/data/starlink-lgh-blockcrush/config/pgpour/config.yml`.
- **dwb-mjwd**: runs on `/data/starlink-dwb-mjwd` with image `feat-with-timestamp-cdc-payload-60a58c99`.
- Used for BlockCrush, MJWD, and BlockBlast pipelines.

- **Match authoritative row** by exact `feature_name`.
- **Soft-delete** (`is_delete=true`) any other row holding the target key **without renaming** it.
- **Update** the authoritative row's `feature_key`.
- **Run a read-only preflight** before any DML.
- **Do not** rename rows to free keys or merely strip leading zeros.
- **Data is reviewed on LGH** before any production change.

memories.body:
# mjwd (Mahjong Blast / WondersMahjong)

## Identity
- mjwd stands for **Mahjong Blast** (also known as mahjong_wonders, WondersMahjong).
- It is a game under the **BBC project** and hosted on **Starlink**.
- It is the **production environment** for the Starlink project and a service in the **starlink-alpha stack**.

## Deployment
- Production servers: **prod-1** and **prod-2**.
- Runs on host **WondersMahjong-Web-01** (10.100.22.160), accessed via **JumpServer**.
- Configuration located at `/data/starlink-mjwd-prod/`.

## Infrastructure
- Prod nodes use **registry.hs99.vip** as their image registry and **lack persistent Aliyun ACR login**.
- Attachments use **starfamily-registry-vpc.cn-beijing.cr.aliyuncs.com** and are deployed at `starlink-mahjong-wonders.youxi123.com/attachments/`.

## Database & Data
- MJWD is one of the **PRD client databases** and a **Starlink client database** referenced for schema alignment patterns.
- Contains **pm_flow tables** (pm_flow_definition, pm_flow_edge, pm_flow_step, pm_flow_step_state, etc.) and is the **source system for PM flow configuration data**.
- Has a **CDC pipeline (41668)** consumed by pgpour from the `prd_mahjongwonders_client` database.
- Project has a **pgpour prod pipeline** using image tag `8e8797b7`.

## Configuration & Behavior
- Export logic treats integer `0` for `experiment_scene_type` as **empty/NULL**.

# BlockBlast

## Overview
- Casual/successful game developed by HungryStudio.
- Part of the BBC project.
- Product hosted on Starlink (Starlink is the platform).
- Game project the user works on.

## Infrastructure

### Production App Servers
- Old UCloud set: `starlink-prd-blockblast-app-1` (10.9.79.254) and `app-2` (10.9.164.112).
- New Aliyun set: `archteam-starlink-blockblast-app-1/2/3` at 10.100.30.117/118/119.
- Source host for prod deployment: 10.9.79.254 (UCloud).
- Prod .env identical across hosts: `APP_ID=block-blast`, `HOST=starlink.youxi123.com`, fixed ports 20000-20011.
- Docker-compose images from `registry.hs99.vip/starlink/bbc`; OTEL metrics to `host.docker.internal:24318`.

### Databases
- Two production PostgreSQL databases: `hs_client_db` (~14 GB) and `hs_code_keeper_db` (~9 MB).
- Migrating to Aliyun RDS (instance `pgm-2zevk26j83oa40t4`, account `caikuai-cn`):
  - Host: `archteam-starlink-blockblast-prod.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com`
  - RO host: `archteam-starlink-blockblast-prod-ro.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com`
  - Port: 5432
  - Databases: `prd_blockblast_client` and `prd_blockblast_codekeeper`
- hfrog database: `prd_blockblast_hfrog` on blockblast-prod RDS.

### Development Environment
- lsx environment at `https://lsx-blockblast.hs99.vip` with Redis at `starlink-dev-uc.hs99.vip:31000` DB0.

## Services & Integration
- Provides hfrog artifact service shared with BlockCrush; hfrog component used in `lhh-blockcrush` project.
- CDC pipeline (18977) consumed by pgpour.
- PRD BI solution: Outbox → message table → pgpour → Kafka.
- pgpour prod pipeline uses image tag `main-2ce47744`.
- `external_system` configuration includes: admarket, n8n, hfrog, user, bbc, automated_testing, mainstream_automated_testing, publish_platform_gp, publish_platform_ios.
- API access: `/api` open (no key), `/gql/` restricted to key-auth + ACL with consumers liguanghui, starorigin, bi, etc.
- Service in `starlink-alpha` stack.

## Operational Notes
- Jenkins jobs (alpha, lby, lxy) write ~1.3G DB dumps to `/tmp` on `uc-devops-jenkins` and never clean up, causing recurring disk pressure.

memories.abstract: BaoStock is a free Python SDK for Chinese A-share market data and a data source adapter in the user's pbp/sync pipelines. Key operational details: singleton global session, per-symbol queries, session expiry, unadjusted daily history, and concurrency constraints.
memories.body:
## BaoStock (baostock)

- BaoStock is a free Python SDK for Chinese market data, primarily covering Shanghai and Shenzhen stocks (A-shares). It is used as a data source in the user's data pipeline (pbp/sync pipeline), providing daily stock data and A-share financial statement metrics.
- Query interface: Uses `query_history_k_data_plus` for daily K-line data; each call takes a single symbol. `query_all_stock` returns ~7,202 rows including both indices and stocks, so the universe is not only A-share tickers; `stock_info` also includes non-equity index codes.
- Session/concurrency model: BaoStock uses a global session model where one login can serve many queries, and the Python client is a singleton — one global socket session per process, cannot be instantiated per worker. The API session expires mid-run during long full-market backfills, causing `用户未登录` errors. BaoStock caps concurrent requests, so the pbp sync execute phase uses a single worker; parallel workers only speed up BaoStock ingest when mixing other sources such as sina, tencent, or em.
- Data characteristics: Daily A-share K-line history spans 1990-12-19 to the last trading day, with each symbol's data starting at its listing date. Daily data is unadjusted (`adjustflag=3`). BaoStock also provides profit and growth data via `query_profit_data` and `query_growth_data`.

memories.abstract: Pattern B (二波涨停) definition: limit-up 8–25 days after prior limit-up + 10d coil [-8%, +5%]; backtest 2018–2026 shows no edge (-0.13%/20d, 41.2% win).
memories.body:
## Pattern B (二波涨停)

- **Definition**: A limit-up strategy requiring a limit-up occurring 8–25 days after a prior limit-up, plus a 10-day coil range within [-8%, +5%].
- **Backtest result (2018–2026)**: Average return over 20 days was **-0.13%**, with a **41.2% win rate**.
- **Conclusion**: No edge versus random limit-ups.

memories.body:
# Kong

- Kong is the API gateway used in the Starlink infrastructure.
- Kong was the read-only gateway, replaced by OpenResty.
- Kong served the main Starlink RO hostnames on :18000.
- Recent state: Kong (`kong/kong-gateway:3.10`, DB-less) serves `starlink-ro` on `ro-1`.
- Kong is the legacy `starlink-s2s-gateway` being replaced by ding; on `ro-2` it is bypassed, but `ro-1`'s Kong still serves production until DNS cutover.
- Kong is dead in the user's setup.
- As the existing gateway on `ro-1`, Kong honors `X-Forwarded-For` and trusts `172.16.0.0/12`.
- The legacy s2s-gateway `/api` route is completely open: it returns 200 even for invalid keys or non-whitelisted IPs.
- Kong's key-auth plugin uses the `X-Starlink-ApiKey` header (no hyphen between Api and Key).

# starlink-dev-all-in-one-uc

- **Type**: Old / legacy UCloud-hosted dev all-in-one host; `uc` stands for UCloud.

- **Services**: Runs PostgreSQL 16 and Docker.
  - ~33 Docker Compose projects.

memories.abstract: Memory pipeline (Go): T1 extract, T2 scene, T3 memory/L3 rollup; per-session sequential, cross-session parallel; timed polling, sqlite, design docs.
memories.body:
# Memory Pipeline

- Stages: T1 atom extraction, T2 scene building, T3 memory (global rollup, heavier prompts than T1/T2); also referred to as t1 extract, t2 scene, t3 memory.
- Sessions are processed sequentially through T1→T2→T3 per session; T1 and T2 workers run in parallel across sessions.
- Each stage is a single-lane queue: one session at a time per worker, with up to 8 candidates per cycle run sequentially in one goroutine.
- Implemented in Go using goroutines.
- T1/T2 polled every 15s; 90s wait after T1 before T2; T3/L3 rollup polled every 5min; l1_every_n: 8 with 10-minute idle gating.
- L3 rollup runs every 5 minutes and breaks on the first transient error; a timeout on the rmb://profile bucket stalls all other buckets.
- rmb://profile bucket is a global bucket aggregating all profile-class atoms.
- Uses sqlite 3.53.4.
- Design docs: #3 describes failed-session infinite retry; #7 describes atom source-index fallback.

memories.abstract: BBC (hs-code-keeper/bbc) is the Starlink Python/Flask backend project and service for game backends (BlockCrush, BlockBlast, MJWD, etc.), keyed by APP_ID, deployed via Jenkins/containers; handles auth/scopes, PM meta, DMP sync, and has known production issues.
memories.body:
# BBC (hs-code-keeper/bbc)

## Overview
- BBC is the Python write backend in the Starlink stack, deployed via Jenkins, and used for building/deploying game backends keyed by APP_ID.
- The BBC project covers multiple games: BlockCrush, JDMJ, MJWD, BlockBlast, BlockMJ, and SandCrush. MJWD stacks require APP_ID=mahjong_wonders.
- The BBC team manages backend code and DDL changes relevant to pgpour.
- Also described as BlockBlast Core and as the starlink PM backend service.

## Tech stack
- Flask 3 + SQLAlchemy 2 REST API backend for PM-1; also run under gunicorn with a create_app factory.
- Uses SQLAlchemy ORM against Alibaba Cloud RDS PostgreSQL via rwlb.rds.aliyuncs.com (10.9.177.238:5432).
- Uses Flask-Cache backed by Redis, keys prefixed `flask_cache_`; caches Avatar by `avatar_cache_{avatar_id}` with default TTL 60s.
- Makes synchronous downstream calls to Postgres, two Redis instances (10.9.169.x), n8n, Jenkins, starflow, atomkit, rustyme, DMP, and SSO.

## Deployment and configuration
- Production BlockBlast backend runs as `starlink-blockblast-prod-bbc-1` on app-1/app-2 (`prd-blockblast-app-1`, `prd-blockblast-app-2`; app-2 at 10.100.30.118).
- Production image: `registry.hs99.vip/starlink/bbc:block-blast-main-05b48f3b`; production API domain: `starlink-inner.youxi123.com`.
- Runs 9 synchronous gunicorn workers with `timeout=360` and no `max_requests` recycling.
- Config paths: `/data/starlink-blockblast-prod/config/bbc/env.prod`, `/opt/starlink-blockblast-prod/config/bbc/env.prod` (sets `ATOM_KIT_HOST=https://atomkit-internal.youxi123.com`), `/data/starlink-<user>-blockblast/config/bbc/` on dev-all-in-one with `env.dev` mounted as `/app/envs/default/.env.dev`, `/data/starlink-blockbloom-prod/config/bbc/env.prod`, and `envs/block_crush/.env.mx`.
- Local run example: `uv run app.py dwb starlink_pm`, serving REST API on port 12124; also run locally against `pm1_dev` database.
- bbc is an upstream service behind the openresty gateway, and is also used in the lsx-mjwd system connected to the `lsx_mjwd_client` RDS database.
- Shares the codekeeper database with the fakeuser service.
- The v3.4.6-lite migration runs inside BBC and requires a BBC image with the Python migrate module.

## Responsibilities and endpoints
- Handles login ticket verification by calling SSO's `ADDR_SSO_VERIFY_TICKET` endpoint.
- Contains the `EAvatarScope` enum and `Avatar.get_scope()` logic. The login API returns two scope lists: cookie `user_info` contains only `:v` scopes, while `data.task.scope` contains non-`:v` API permission strings.
- Handles PM work item meta URL upsert via GraphQL and REST `/pm/work_item/meta/upsert`; database `pm_work_item_meta`.
- `/api/fc/enum/get` requires the `get_sub_type_required_solution_types` hook; version 2.0.72+ added the `SUB_TYPE_REQUIRED_SOLUTION_TYPES` enum field read via a pluggy hook.
- Schedules `conflict.detect` jobs through rustyme via Redis.
- Exposes `/api/fc_dmp/crowd/list` and `/api/fc_dmp/rule/list`, syncing DMP data into local `dmp_crowd` and `dmp_rule` tables. Env.dev DMP block sets `DMP_HOST`, `DMP_TOKEN_CROWD_GP`, `DMP_TOKEN_CROWD_IOS`, `DMP_TOKEN_RULE_GP`, `DMP_TOKEN_RULE_IOS`.
- creative_idea_proposal add flow maps `proposal.id` to `feature_config.feature_id` and `external_id` to `feature_key`.

## Operational notes / known issues
- Had 5 production stability incidents in June 2026.
- Leaks idle-in-transaction connections by running `UPDATE solution_ai_marks SET editer_time=...` without committing.
- `http_ai_so_kafka_update_status` handler in `/app/api/fc/fc_status.py` looks up Solution rows without filtering `is_delete == False`, unlike another handler in the same file at ~line 136.
- `batch_ignore_unstar` records only SNAT'd host IPs as `remote_addr`, so real clients are hidden behind the ALB.
- Prone to worker-pool exhaustion because of synchronous workers, long timeout, and no worker recycling.

memories.body:
# hs-code-keeper

- Type: Git repository; original BBC backend (Flask + SQLAlchemy) for the starlink project, now archived; local source repository for BlockCrush BBC; content management system source code repository.
- Location: /Users/liguanghui/hs.projects/starlink/hs-code-keeper
- Project: Under the starlink project; Starlink BBC backend covering feature config, PM/workbench, and conflict detection.
- Branch: Developed on the main_ne branch; main branch also referenced for get_scope() behavior.
- Contains:
  - BBC code with role definitions.
  - BBC game spec files, e.g. bbc/spec/block_mahjong/func_fc_get_enum.py.
  - hs_code_keeper.dump, a 111K dump file.

## Scope and caching
- get_scope() reads avatar_role.scope from the database on the main branch.
- On main_ne, get_scope() returns the full EAvatarScope set without reading the DB when the user role contains 888.
- Avatar scope is cached in Redis with a sliding TTL (CACHE_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT=60).
- cache.delete is only called in post_user_set_role, so direct DB edits do not invalidate the cache.

## Environment / metrics
- Active env keys: METRICS_SERVICE_NAME and JAEGER_ADDR (OpenTelemetry OTLP export).
- Obsolete blocks: git, loki, web, n8n, DingTalk, Jenkins, Flowchart, and Atom Kit.

## Known issues
- BlockMahjong's BlockMjSpecEnumGet class lacks the get_sub_type_required_solution_types hook, causing an IndexError on /api/fc/enum/get.
- convert_creative_to_work_item (bbc/api/pm/utils.py) hardcodes priority to medium and never uses DEFAULT_CREATIVE_PRIORITY_MAP.

memories.abstract: LiteLLM is an AI gateway/proxy in the user's portfolio and under the aigateway/astra umbrella; used by StarOrigin across GKE, GCP Cloud Run, Aliyun, and Tencent Cloud; production at stargate.youxi123.com, protected by Cloud Armor IP allowlists.
memories.body:
## Identity
- LiteLLM is an AI Gateway / proxy the user works with, and part of the user's project portfolio.
- It is an AI gateway component of the astra project, forked and built into the aigateway/litellm image.
- It is a component under the aigateway umbrella (LiteLLM proxy).
- Used by StarOrigin as an AI Gateway service.
- Also used as a GPU proxy on Tencent Cloud, and for AI running on GCP Cloud Run and Aliyun.
- Deployed in the user's Kubernetes cluster, fronted by an nginx sidecar.

## Deployments
- Runs on two GKE clusters (dev and prod) in asia-northeast1 on GCP.
- The service runs as litellm-clusterip in the starorigin-aigateway-prod namespace.
- The GKE clusters have no Cloud NAT; pods egress via ephemeral node IPs.
- GKE gateway ingress IPs: 35.190.79.58 (dev), 34.149.8.200 (prod).
- LiteLLM requires idle_timeout=300 on its ALB.

## Endpoints
- Production environment: https://stargate.youxi123.com/
- Multimodal kernel endpoint (tentative): https://stargate.youxi123.com/multimodality
- Production gateway exposed at llm-gateway.afafb.com.
- GCP node production GA-accelerated domain (accelerated region Beijing): https://stargate-gcp.youxi123.com/
- GCP origin domain: https://stargate-gcp-origin.youxi123.com/
- Global accelerator: new-litellm-prod-ga, for cross-border traffic between Beijing and Tokyo.

## Security / Access
- The production gateway is protected by the litellm-prd-ip-allowlist Cloud Armor policy in GCP project starorigin-485010.
- litellm-prd-ip-allowlist has a default deny (403) at priority 2147483647 and ~50 allow rules for specific source ranges; it is attached to GKE Autopilot NEGs across asia-northeast1-a/b/c.
- A sibling dev policy, litellm-dev-ip-allowlist, protects the litellm-dev backend in asia-northeast1-b.
- All StarOrigin prod services share a single LiteLLM proxy key; there is no dedicated per-service Anthropic key.

memories.body:
# MiMo

- **Provider**: Xiaomi MiMo is the LLM provider for mypast (chat, workers, memory/T1 extraction).
- **Plan**: Xiaomi MiMo Token Plan — an individual-developer subscription with monthly tiers from ¥39 to ¥659, only MiMo's own models (mimo-v2.5 series, TTS, ASR). Supports API integration into apps/scripts; USD pricing available for international use.
- **Endpoint/Model**: The user's mypast workers use the MiMo token plan at `https://token-plan-cn.xiaomimimo.com/v1` with model `mimo-v2.5`. Quota resets every 5 hours.
- **Pricing**: Off-peak pricing during 00:00–08:00 Asia/Shanghai (Beijing night hours) costs 80% of normal (0.8x credit consumption).
- **API behavior**: In MiMo thinking mode, temperature and top_p are ignored and forced to 1.0 / 0.95. Thinking mode is disabled via the top-level field `thinking: {type: 'disabled'}` on the direct API.
- **Embeddings**: MiMo has no embedding model.
- **Usage**: mypast's T1 extraction LLM calls run against the user's MiMo quota.

memories.abstract: Memory about hs99.vip domain: game-services domain managed on Cloudflare (zone ID 2a18c9f22740da5a00a9b172076e5169), associated with user systems, hosted on hs99-vip running starlink's pgpour and forwarder; Let's Encrypt cert at /etc/nginx/ssl/hs99.vip/fullchain.cer, published to OSS bucket colin-certs; no ICP filing so external connections reset; wildcard cert does not cover 4-level subdomains; cert-renew uses Cloudflare DNS token.
memories.body:
# hs99-vip / hs99.vip

- **Domain**: hs99.vip is an active domain associated with the user's systems, used for game services.
- **Host**: The host `hs99-vip` runs starlink's `pgpour` and `forwarder`.
- **DNS / Cloudflare**:
  - hs99.vip is managed on Cloudflare; the user manages this domain in their Cloudflare account.
  - Cloudflare zone ID for hs99.vip: `2a18c9f22740da5a00a9b172076e5169`.
  - The domain is managed by the cert-renew job and hosted on Cloudflare; cert-renew uses a Cloudflare API token with DNS edit permissions for this zone.
- **TLS / Certificates**:
  - Wildcard TLS certificates for hs99.vip are stored at `/etc/nginx/ssl/hs99.vip/` (`fullchain.cer` and key).
  - The installed certificate on Nginx hosts is `/etc/nginx/ssl/hs99.vip/fullchain.cer`.
  - The TLS certificate for hs99.vip is issued by Let's Encrypt.
  - The certificate is published to the OSS bucket `colin-certs`.
  - The `*.hs99.vip` wildcard certificate does **not** cover 4-level subdomains such as `foo.ext.hs99.vip`.
- **Access / Operational Notes**:
  - hs99.vip has no ICP filing, so the cloud provider resets external connections to it; internal access works fine.
  - Nginx certificates for hs99.vip are stored under `/etc/nginx/ssl/hs99.vip/`.

memories.abstract: hfrog: Rust-based artifact/artifactory service in Starlink, presigns S3/MinIO/OSS upload/download URLs, stores metadata in hfrog DBs; prod hfrog.youxi123.com, dev hfrog-dev.hs99.vip (hfrog-dev-all-in-one, port 9898).
memories.body:
# hfrog

## Identity
- hfrog is the Starlink artifact (制品) service: a legacy Rust-based artifactory / artifact proxy service (backend `hs-artifactory-hfrog-backend`).
- It presigns upload and download URLs for artifacts on S3/MinIO/OSS, stores artifact metadata, and handles file uploads/registration.
- It is a single presign/lookup gateway for OSS attachments and serves artifacts from S3 configuration files.
- It is related to `starlink-attachments` and shares namespace/app_id choices with it; `starlink-attachments` is a greenfield alternative.

## API / behavior
- Main JSON API: `GET /hfrog/api/artifactory/get_object_presigned_url`; implemented in `hs-artifactory-hfrog-backend/src/services/api/artifactory/artifactory.rs`, delegating to `static_remote::S3Handler::action_object_url_with_presigned`.
- The presign endpoint is keyed on `pid` (or `name`+`version`+`runtime`), not on `s3Key`.
- Presigned URLs are signed for GET only; HEAD requests fail with `SignatureDoesNotMatch` (tracked as FGLM-7968).
- Health check: `GET /hfrog/health` returns `i'm working!`; `HEAD /hfrog/health` returns 404.
- OpenAPI docs: `/hfrog/apidoc/swagger/openapi.json` (OpenAPI v0.2.0).
- hfrog handles `s3_hook`/MinIO webhooks, expecting MinIO-style flat JSON with `event_name` and `key` fields.
- It is a Rust service that also handles Kafka.
- Note: as of 2026-08-04 it lacks a browser-accessible download redirect endpoint.

## Deployments / domains
- Production: served at `hfrog.youxi123.com` and `hfrog-inner.youxi123.com`; wildcard TLS cert `CN=*.youxi123.com` valid until Jan 2027.
- Dev: `hfrog-dev.hs99.vip` is the dev domain, terminated by host nginx config `/etc/nginx/conf.d/0-hfrog-dev.hs99.vip.conf`, which proxies to `127.0.0.1:9898`.
- Dev stack: `hfrog-dev-all-in-one` at `/data/hfrog-dev-all-in-one`; the container has restart policy `always` and listens on port 9898.
- Routing: `starlink.hs99.vip` proxies `/hfrog/` to `hfrog-dev.hs99.vip`, which reaches the `hfrog-dev-all-in-one` container on `starlink-dev-internal.hs99.vip` (10.100.64.132); the local hfrog container on the hs99-vip host receives no traffic.
- Also seen as a service on `starlink-dev-all-in-one`; in the lhh-blockcrush PoC the container is named `starlink-lhh-blockcrush-hfrog` and runs on port 8001, with S3 configuration pointing to OSS.
- In mjwd, blockmj and blockcrush, the hfrog service uses image tag `prd-tempbranch-from-old-env-1a30f9b`.

## Data / backends
- Reads three INI files; supports three S3 backends: `s3_0`, `s3_1`, `s3_2`, each pointing to MinIO buckets.
- Example MinIO config: `/Users/liguanghui/hungrystudio/2025/12/04.星链商业化环境/starlink-blockblast-prod/config/hfrog/s3_0.ini` with bucket `starlink-artifacts-prd`, access key `X5WpS41OGmEvCa3PSVmp`, endpoint `https://minio.hungrystudio.pp.ua`, and empty region.
- Metadata lives in hfrog databases named per environment: dev `hfrog_dev` on Aliyun dev RDS (`starlink-dev-all-in-one.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com:5432`, account `solutionhub_dev`), `prd_blockblast_hfrog`, and `prd_jdmj_hfrog`.
- hfrog stores files with `create_time` metadata. Originally it was a MySQL-backed legacy artifactory; as a service it is not a user database and does not own a dedicated PostgreSQL database—it uses shared environment-specific databases.

## Usage / integrations
- A service component of Jade Mahjong; webhook endpoint is on the `starlink-jade-mahjong` domain.
- Shared service at `hfrog-dev.hs99.vip` is used for PM artifact downloads via OpenResty proxy.
- BlockBlast production hfrog presigns uploads and registers artifacts in `prd_blockblast_hfrog`.
- The comment rich editor `WorkItemCommentInput.vue` uploads via hfrog with `pkgName` `'work-item-comment'`.
- hfrog is a component of the BlockCrush PoC (cloned from BlockBlast's production hfrog).

memories.body:
## starlink/db-migrator-client-and-code-keeper

- Jenkins job: `starlink/db-migrator-client-and-code-keeper`.
- Restores both the `code_keeper` and `client` databases.
- Migrates starlink client and codekeeper databases from **prod to dev** using `SRC_DB` and `DST_DB` parameters.
- Drops and recreates target DBs during the migrator process.
- Truncates **5 sensitive tables** post-restore; this does **not** require a TOTP token.
- Dumps are run on the **Jenkins master localhost**.
- Expects per-game `dump-starlink-db.sh` scripts to already exist on the host.

memories.abstract: db-migrator: Ansible/Jenkins PostgreSQL dump-restore migration system at starlink/ansible-playbooks/db-migrator; two Jenkins jobs, TOKEN-gated truncation of sensitive perf tables, vars.yml maps game environments to DB hosts.
memories.body:
# db-migrator

- Lives at `starlink/ansible-playbooks/db-migrator/`; orchestrates PostgreSQL dump-and-restore migrations via Ansible and Jenkins.
- Contains `vars.yml`, which maps game environments to database hosts and defines `db_host` per namespace and game.
- Jenkins jobs:
  - `db-migrator-client-and-code-keeper`: migrates both `client` and `code_keeper` databases.
  - `db-migrator-client-only`: migrates `client` only.
- Data flow: `pg_dump` on the UCloud source host → fetch to Jenkins → copy to the target ops host → `pg_restore` to the target RDS → per-table `COUNT(*)` verification.
- The playbook's `TOKEN` param gates whether 5 sensitive perf tables (`jixiao_*`, `airflow_*`) are truncated after restore:
  - Valid TOTP preserves them.
  - Empty token wipes them.
  - Wrong token fails the build.

memories.body:
# bbc_publication

bbc_publication is a PostgreSQL logical replication publication, table-list based, used for CDC in the blockcrush pipeline. It has `puballtables = false` and exists on the `starlink_hs99_vip_client` database. `pgpour` subscribes to it for CDC; on prd BlockBlast it publishes 8 tables including `_kafka_message_bi_solution`. It is also used by the Supabase ETL for the blockcrush client databases.

## Environment-specific table sets
- `dwb_blockcrush_client`: `_kafka_message_bi_solution`, `feature_config`, `fc_workflow_info`.
- `dwb_mjwd_client`: `public._kafka_message_bi_solution`.
- `lgh_blockcrush_client`: `fc_workflow_info`, `pm_work_item`.
- `alpha_blockcrush_client`: `_kafka_message_bi_solution`, `_pm_idea_flow_outbox_event`, `feature_config`, `feature_config_workflow_info`.
- BlockCrush PRD: `_kafka_message_bi_solution`, `feature_config`, `feature_config_workflow_info` (also listed as `prd_blockcrush_client`).
- Prod BlockBlast logical replication: `_kafka_message_bi_solution`, `feature_config`, `feature_config_workflow_info`, `_pm_idea_flow_outbox_event`.
- `wz_blockblast_client`: `public._kafka_message_bi_solution`, `feature_config`, `feature_config_conflict`, `feature_config_label_lv1`, `feature_config_label_lv2`, `feature_config_label_lv3`, `feature_tag_config`.
- `alpha_mjwd_client`: `feature_config`, `feature_config_workflow_info`, `solution`, `solution_outbox`, `solution_way`.
- Starlink alpha database (as of 2026-06-11): `feature_config`, `solution`, `solution_way`, `feature_config_workflow_info`, `_kafka_message_bi_solution`.
- Starlink alpha Aliyun RDS: covers 8 tables.
- Starlink alpha PostgreSQL consumed by `pgpour`: contains 10 tables including `feature_conflict_way`, `st_workflow`, and `solution_way`.
- On `hs_client_db`, it is owned by `root`.

One observation states that bbc_publication contains `_kafka_message_bi_solution`, `feature_config`, and `fc_workflow_info`, and that `feature_config_workflow_info` is not part of it; other environment-specific observations list `feature_config_workflow_info`.

memories.abstract: BlockCrush (BC) is a HungryStudio Starlink/BBC game and PM application, current Aliyun production game replacing crushblast; its prod stack is the reference architecture. Prod URLs/hosts, Postgres/RDS, Redis, hfrog/OSS attachments, pgpour/Kafka CDC, PM/flow schema, feature_config conventions, environment/database list, and known issues are captured.
memories.body:
# BlockCrush

## Overview
- BlockCrush (BC) is a HungryStudio Starlink/BBC game project and a project-management (PM) application with a PM UI and client library. It is part of the Nebula series and one of the four live games in the starlink repo.
- Integrated with the cehua AI platform and Starlink; it is one of the PRD client databases.
- It is the current production game on Aliyun, replacing retired crushblast; its production Starlink stack (archteam-starlink-blockcrush-*) is the reference architecture for new deployments. Older app settings/configs served as templates/reference baseline for BlockBloom/Starlink resource specifications.

## Environments and hosts
- Production: https://starlink-blockcrush.youxi123.com, with servers app-1 and app-2. Attachments/game path: https://starlink-blockcrush.youxi123.com/attachments/. Internal ALB archteam-starlink-blockcrush-prod-internal; external ALB archteam-starlink-blockcrush-prod-external.
- LGH: https://lgh-blockcrush.ext.hs99.vip (.ext subdomain configured on hs99.vip). LSX dev: https://lsx-blockcrush.hs99.vip.
- Environment names seen: prd, lsx/staging, lgh, lhh, mx/dev, alpha, dwb, lby, yy, yl; project family has 14 environments.
- Databases: prd_blockcrush_client, prd_blockcrush_codekeeper, lsx_blockcrush_client, lgh_blockcrush_client, lhh_blockcrush_client/lhh_blockcrush_hfrog, alpha_blockcrush_client, lby_blockcrush_client, dwb_blockcrush, and MX/dev database at starlink-dev-all-in-one.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com. PRD and DWB PostgreSQL are kept in schema sync via Atlas diffs.

## Infrastructure
- Production PostgreSQL: Aliyun RDS PostgreSQL 16 (16.13) at archteam-starlink-blockcrush-pg16.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com:5432, hosting prd_blockcrush_client and prd_blockcrush_codekeeper. Credentials in e.credentials/starlink/blockcrush.txt. wal_level=logical; starlink user has REPLICATION; wal_keep_size=2GB, max_wal_size=2GB, min_wal_size=512MB.
- Redis: Aliyun Tair archteam-starlink-blockcrush-redis.redis.rds.aliyuncs.com:6379 DB 0 (instance r-2zeo2vah2w71dtap4q, cn-beijing). Dev Redis: starlink-dev-internal.hs99.vip:31200 DB 0.
- App hosts: archteam-starlink-blockcrush-app-1 (10.100.25.26) and archteam-starlink-blockcrush-app-2 (10.100.25.25), accessed via JumpServer. Deployment dir /data/starlink-blockcrush-prod/; prod BBC container starlink-blockcrush-prod-bbc-1.
- Prod Docker Compose runs vector, bbc, frontend, starflow, and gql containers on each node. Prod config is maintained server-side at config/bbc/env.prod (bind-mounted); repo has no bbc/envs/block_crush/.env.prod.
- BBC containers use /etc/timezone = Etc/UTC on prd and dwb; PostgreSQL sessions inherit Asia/Shanghai; no client forces UTC.
- Known issue: gql service is misconfigured to run the mahjong-wonders image tag prod-mahjong-wonders-main-acd7aa54 (TODO in .env). Materialization script refuses to run with --env prod.

## Redis recommendation
- BlockCrush uses a separate recommendation Redis (REDIS_RECOMMEND_*) isolated from cache Redis; recommendation data must not be FLUSHALL'd.
- If REDIS_RECOMMEND_HOST is unset, recommendation reads/writes fall back to main cache Redis (REDIS_HOST).
- Avatar-pick scores stored in Redis ZSETs keyed recommend:{scene}:{scope}:{actor_id}.

## Database and schema notes
- BlockCrush stores PM work-item metadata in prd_blockcrush_client and is the canonical schema target for production clients.
- Tables: pm_work_item, fc_workflow_info, avatar, feature_config, feature_config_workflow_info. PM/flow tables: pm_project, pm_flow_definition, pm_flow_node, pm_flow_instance, pm_iteration, pm_work_item and related pm_* tables.
- Reported PM AI/parallel-flow table names: pm_agent, pm_agent_flow_draft, pm_agent_run, pm_flow_step_deliverable, pm_flow_parallel_run, pm_flow_parallel_branch.
- Source notes conflict on which environments have the full pm_* module: one note says alpha_blockcrush_client has pm_project/pm_work_item that prd_blockcrush_client lacks; another says production pm_project exists with only id=21; another says MX has 8 tables production lacks (including pm_agent, pm_flow_parallel_run, pm_work_item_review_round), while production still has legacy columns bucket_id and test_server_id that MX dropped.
- JDMJ and BlockCrush schemas differ only on pm_project (3 columns); BlockCrush has tables MJWD lacks.
- feature_config has a partial unique constraint on (platform, feature_id) where is_delete=false and feature_id>0.
- Prod PM/flow data observations: business logic assumes exactly one PM project id=1, but prod pm_project only contains id=21. Orphaned active rows under nonexistent project_id=1: 59 pm_flow_node, 17 pm_flow_instance, 6 soft-deleted pm_flow_definition. Under project_id=21: 2 active flow definitions, 15 active flow nodes, 2 running flow instances, 2 iterations, 8 work items. Running instances ids 18/19 belong to test work items 【测试】Other类需求 (id 3) and Gina测试1 (id 7).
- pm_flow_node unique constraint uq_pm_flow_node_project_key on (project_id, node_key). Prod pm_* tables have seven FK constraints referencing pm_project(id).
- lby_blockcrush_client restore via Ansible fails with rc=1 because pm_flow_definition, pm_flow_node, and pm_flow_instance FK constraints referencing pm_project were not created during restore.

## People and workflow data
- prd_blockcrush_codekeeper.public.avatar is BlockCrush's people directory (originally 95 rows; dingding_name unique), mapping display names to avatar id and workcode. fc_workflow_info.*_avatar_id references avatar.id rather than workcode.
- prd_blockcrush_client.public.fc_workflow_info stores workflow rows with submitter/follower text[] name arrays and parallel submitter_avatar_*/follower_avatar_* arrays (name, id, workcode) kept position-aligned.

## PM and attachments architecture
- PM UI does not connect directly to the database; it uses BBC for meta and hfrog for uploads. Four layers: frontend, hfrog, hfrog database, object storage.
- Production PM uses BlockBlast's hfrog and shared MinIO bucket.
- PM artifacts/attachments were migrated from MinIO to Aliyun OSS; task acceptance artifacts are stored in MinIO and OSS buckets. BlockCrush has private and public buckets under Starlink.
- UI downloads task acceptance videos by reading meta_value → file.url.
- Prod attachments environment has no local hfrog or s3_1.ini; OSS credentials manually written to config/attachments/env using shared RAM user starlink-pm-artifacts-oss. Aliyun ACR login is configured.

## Replication and Kafka
- Production Kafka exists; topic pattern JDMJ/blockcrush; PostgreSQL-to-Kafka topic prefix starlink.blockcrush.*.
- Active replication slot supabase_etl_apply_87142; pgpour runs on archteam-starlink-pgpour-prd-all-in-one and supports Lua transform.
- bbc_publication includes _kafka_message_bi_solution, _pm_idea_flow_outbox_event, feature_config, feature_config_workflow_info, pm_work_item.
- LGH publication difference: BlockCrush lgh has solution/solution_way; JDMJ lgh has _kafka_message_bi_solution.

## Features and configuration
- Feature descriptions follow format level·tag·name; feature config labels use feature_name and feature_desc, with feature_desc a three-part format. Optimization label uses enum term 底板优化.
- feature_config data managed via Excel feature_name to feature_key mappings, stored in lgh_blockcrush_client and prd_blockcrush_client. Feature configs are being migrated from LGH to PRD; BlockCrush is in iteration preparation.
- pm_work_item.priority mapping: urgent=10, high=8, medium=5, low=2 (another reported legacy mapping: low→3, medium→5, high→8, urgent→10); prod BBC serves PM priority as integers 1–10.
- DingTalk doc links are stored separately in PM requirements (extra.creative_doc_link) and FC creatives (feature_config.url_doc); they can diverge because creative-to-requirement conversion copies a snapshot and there is no reverse sync. Creative updates via Kafka do not propagate to the bound requirement.

memories.abstract: T3 (L3 rollup) global memory distillation: groups atoms by slug across sessions, distills one memory per bucket, serialized by GlobalLock, 5-min polling, needs per-slug locks.
memories.body:
# T3 (L3 rollup)

- T3 is a **memory distillation system** that groups atoms into buckets by slug and tracks progress in `t3/t3_done` tables.
- It is a **global memory-distillation job**: it groups all sessions' atoms by slug across sessions and distills **one memory per bucket**, not per session.

## Processing

- Uses **5-minute polling** with GlobalLock-serialized processing.
- Holds the **GlobalLock while sleeping in `distillDelay`**.
- Currently **cannot run multiple workers**: rollup is serialized by `workerlock.GlobalLock`, distilling **one bucket at a time** with a **1-second holding-lock delay**.

## Concurrency & Locking

- Per-slug memory uses an **active unique index plus versioning**.
- Concurrent distillation of the same slug conflicts; **per-slug sharded locks** are needed to avoid this.

memories.abstract: T3 (L3 rollup) is a global memory-distillation job; groups atoms by slug across sessions, serialized by GlobalLock, 5-min polling, per-slug versioning conflicts, progress tracked in t3/t3_done tables.
memories.body:
## T3 (L3 rollup)

- T3 is a global memory-distillation system that groups all sessions' atoms by slug across sessions, rather than per session, and distills one memory per slug bucket.
- It tracks progress in the `t3` / `t3_done` tables.

## Workers and locking

- The T3 worker polls on a **5-minute interval**.
- Processing is serialized by `workerlock.GlobalLock`; while holding the GlobalLock, T3 sleeps in `distillDelay`.
- T3 currently **cannot run multiple workers** because the rollup is serialized and distills one bucket at a time with a 1-second holding-lock delay.

## Concurrency and locking requirements

- T3's per-slug memory uses an **active unique index plus versioning**, so concurrent distillation of the same slug conflicts.
- To support concurrency safely, T3 needs **per-slug sharded locks**.

memories.abstract: pgpour is Starlink's internal Rust PostgreSQL-to-Kafka CDC tool built on supabase/etl. It streams WAL changes via logical replication slots/publications and publishes Debezium-style JSON (v2.23 outbox envelopes) to Kafka. Used across dev/alpha/prod stacks (blockblast, blockcrush, mjwd, mahjongwonders). Known issues: orphaned sync slots, expensive restarts, InvalidState crashes.
memories.body:
# pgpour

## Overview
- Starlink internal PostgreSQL CDC to Kafka tool, written in Rust, built on supabase/etl.
- Reads PostgreSQL WAL changes via logical replication slots and publications; publishes Debezium-style JSON to Kafka. Requires `wal_level=logical`; tables absent from the publication are not CDC'd.
- Runs as a Docker container across Starlink stacks; image `registry.hs99.vip/starlink/pgpour`.
- Used across Starlink dev/prod stacks: blockblast, blockmj, mjwd/mahjongwonders, blockcrush, and Nebula client databases.
- Used for syncing tables such as `feature_config_workflow_info` and `bbc_publication` to Kafka; also the producer application that writes Starlink Kafka topics.

## Core behavior
- Uses PostgreSQL logical replication slots like `supabase_etl_apply_*`.
- Topic naming: `{topic_prefix}.{schema}.{table}`.
- Does not auto-create Kafka topics; missing topics cause `UnknownTopicOrPartition` errors.
- Producer uses lz4 compression in code.
- Kafka message keys derive from the source table's primary key; text keys are JSON-encoded as quoted strings.
- On source DELETEs, emits tombstone-style messages with `op` = `delete`, `before` populated, `after` null.
- Postgres array/composite columns are rendered as the literal string `<array>`; genuine jsonb/array columns serialize as proper JSON.
- Supports Lua transforms for filtering/cleaning CDC data, with DLQ routing for errors and helpers such as `keep`, `drop_nulls`, `rename`, `now_ms`.
- Hybrid config: a config YAML file plus secret environment variables.
- Limit: does not allow two targets with the same `(brokers, topic_prefix)`.
- Container resource limits: CPU 2, memory 2048 MB.

## Deployment / topology
- Containers are named `starlink-*-pgpour-1`; general config path pattern: `/data/starlink-{env}-{game}/config/pgpour/config.yml`; global/default example `/data/pgpour/config.yml`.
- Example container: `starlink-jdmj-pgpour-prod-pgpour-1`, config at `/data/starlink-jdmj-pgpour-prod/config/pgpour/config.yml`.
- On alpha host `archteam-starlink-alpha`, `/data/starlink-blockblast-alpha/config/pgpour/config.yml` is mounted as `/etc/pgpour/config.yml`.
- Defined in Docker Compose stacks, generally behind a profile that disables CDC by default (`cdc-disabled`, sometimes `pgpour`); on alpha some stacks run without profile gating.
- Some deployments are profile-gated (e.g. `cdc-disabled`) and do not start by default.
- Used in pipelines: `starlink-dwb-blockcrush`, `starlink-lgh-blockcrush`, `starlink-lby-blockcrush`, `starlink-yy-blockblast`, `starlink-lhh-blockblast`.
- Containers named `starlink-*-pgpour-1` stream CDC from the Starlink dev all-in-one RDS into blockblast/blockcrush client databases (yl, dwb, lgh, lhh).

### Alpha
- Three containers on starlink-alpha: `starlink-blockblast-alpha-pgpour-1`, `starlink-blockcrush-alpha-pgpour-1`, `starlink-mjwd-alpha-pgpour-1`.
- Example alpha config: host `archteam-starlink-alpha-pg.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com`, database `alpha_blockblast_client`, publication `bbc_publication`, Kafka brokers `10.9.169.2:9092`, `10.9.131.68:9092`, `10.9.103.246:9092`, topic prefix `starlink.blockblast.alpha`.

### Blockcrush
- Config: Postgres at `starlink-dev-all-in-one.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com:5432`, database `dwb_blockcrush_client`, publication `bbc_publication`, Kafka topic prefix `starlink.blockcrush.dwb`, defined in `docker-compose.yml` under the `cdc-disabled` profile.
- Prod: container `starlink-blockcrush-prod-pgpour-1` runs on host `archteam-starlink-blockcrush-app-1`; restarting it must not touch the pipeline container in order to preserve the replication slot.
- On BlockCrush prod hosts the config remains under `config/pgpour/` but is not defined in Docker Compose.

### Production
- Production host: `archteam-starlink-pgpour-prd-all-in-one` (`10.100.64.62`); three production instances on the new server: **blockcrush**, **mjwd**, **blockblast**.
- Production image: `registry.hs99.vip/starlink/pgpour:8e8797b7` (commit `8e8797b`, includes an array conversion fix).
- MahjongWonders: the `prd-mahjongwonders` pgpour instance runs on the app-1 WondersMahjong web server.

## Replication slots & sync behavior
- Slot names are cluster-wide; default `supabase_etl_apply_1` causes collisions across Starlink stacks. An apply worker has been observed using slot `supabase_etl_apply_39786`.
- Re-enabling pgpour creates a new replication slot and attaches to existing publications.
- Initial copy may create per-table sync slots, deleted once the table reaches `sync_done`.
- Runs with `with_init=false`, so initial sync skips historical rows and only post-startup changes stream to Kafka.
- The synced-table set is frozen at first run; a full restart is required for newly added tables to be picked up.

## Message/version notes
- pgpour v2.23 routes tables via `event.table` and emits full outbox event envelopes on insert only, unlike older Debezium-style `event.source.table` routing with flat `after` rows.

## Known issues
- **Cleanup bug**: on Kafka produce failure during table sync, pgpour can leave an orphaned `table_sync` slot that is never cleaned up.
- **Restart cost**: performs a PG `table_sync_copy` on restart, causing heavy memory/disk usage; this was the root cause of the July hang.
- **InvalidState crash**: crashes with `InvalidState` when its PostgreSQL connection is terminated by an administrator command, because tables were synchronized based on a different apply worker lineage.

## Project context
- Local project path: `/Users/liguanghui/hs.projects/starlink/pgpour`.

BlockCrush has pm_agent, pm_agent_flow_draft, pm_agent_run, pm_flow_step_deliverable, pm_flow_parallel_run, pm_flow_parallel_branch that MJWD lacks. MX DB has 8 tables prod lacks (pm_agent, pm_flow_parallel_run, pm_work_item_review_round, etc.); prod has legacy columns bucket_id and test_server_id that MX dropped.
- System tables include pm_work_item, fc_workflow_info, avatar. prd_blockcrush_codekeeper.public.avatar is people directory (originally 95 rows; dingding_name unique) mapping display name -> avatar id and workcode; fc_workflow_info.*_avatar_id references avatar.id, not workcode. prd_blockcrush_client.public.fc_workflow_info stores submitter/follower `text[]` names and parallel `submitter_avatar_*`/`follower_avatar_*` arrays (name, id, workcode), kept position-aligned.

## PM module and project state
- PM UI does not connect directly to DB: BBC is used for meta, hfrog for uploads (BlockBlast's hfrog and shared MinIO bucket in production). Four-layer architecture: frontend, hfrog, hfrog DB, object storage. PM artifacts migrated MinIO -> Aliyun OSS; attachments being migrated to OSS. UI reads meta_value -> file.url for task acceptance videos.
- Prod attachments deployment has no local hfrog or s3_1.ini; OSS credentials manually written to config/attachments/env using shared RAM user starlink-pm-artifacts-oss. Private/public buckets under Starlink; Aliyun ACR login configured.
- PM/flow schema: pm_project, pm_flow_definition, pm_flow_node, pm_flow_instance, pm_iteration, pm_work_item and related pm_* tables. Business logic assumes exactly one PM project (id=1), but prod pm_project contains only id=21; pm_flow_definition/pm_flow_node/pm_flow_instance have rows referencing project_id=1.
- Orphaned active rows under nonexistent project_id=1: 59 pm_flow_node, 17 pm_flow_instance, 6 soft-deleted pm_flow_definition. Under project_id=21: 2 active flow definitions, 15 active flow nodes, 2 running flow instances, 2 iterations, 8 work items. Running instances 18 and 19 belong to test items 【测试】Other类需求 (id 3) and Gina测试1 (id 7).
- pm_flow_node unique constraint on (project_id, node_key) named uq_pm_flow_node_project_key. In prod, pm_* tables have seven FKs referencing pm_project(id).
- Known restore issue: lby_blockcrush_client restore via Ansible fails rc=1 because pm_flow_definition/pm_flow_node/pm_flow_instance FKs referencing pm_project were not created during restore.
- DingTalk doc links stored in PM requirements (extra.creative_doc_link) and FC creatives (feature_config.url_doc); they can diverge (creative-to-requirement conversion is a snapshot; no reverse sync; Kafka creative updates do not propagate to bound requirement).
- pm_work_item.priority mapping: urgent=10, high=8, medium=5, low=2; legacy enum maps low->3, medium->5, high->8, urgent->10. Prod BBC serves PM priority enum as integers 1-10.

## Kafka and feature configs
- Feature configs managed via Excel feature_name -> feature_key mappings in lgh_blockcrush_client and prd_blockcrush_client; being migrated from LGH to PRD. feature_config has partial unique constraint on (platform, feature_id) where is_delete=false and feature_id>0. Labels use feature_name/feature_desc; feature_desc format is level·tag·name; optimization label uses 底板优化.
- Kafka: production Kafka env with topic pattern JDMJ/blockcrush. BlockCrush lgh publication has solution/solution_way; JDMJ lgh has _kafka_message_bi_solution. CDC/pgpour pipeline 87142 consumes prd_blockcrush_client and replicates feature_config_workflow_info and _pm_idea_flow_outbox_event to Kafka under starlink.blockcrush.* for alpha, LGH dev, and prod.
- Materialization script refuses to run with --env prod.

## Operations notes
- BBC app containers run /etc/timezone = Etc/UTC on prd and dwb; PostgreSQL sessions inherit Asia/Shanghai; no client forces UTC on connect.
- Recommendation avatar-pick scores in Redis ZSETs keyed recommend:{scene}:{scope}:{actor_id}. Settings remain in the Block Bloom compose tree.
- BlockCrush is in iteration preparation for its next project phase.

memories.abstract: mypast is the user's personal long-term memory engine for AI agents: a Go/Postgres(pgvector) single binary with CLI, server, Next.js UI, T0→T3 memory pyramid, rmb:// URIs, corrections, hooks for Cursor/Claude, deployed at mem.colinleefish.com.
memories.body:
# mypast

mypast is the user's personal long-term memory/recall engine for AI-agent conversations, built and owned by the user. It is a Postgres-native, single Go binary with a dual-mode CLI (local tool, server, remote client), HTTP API, and embedded Next.js static web UI served at /ui.

## Stack & repo
- Go 1.26, Gin, GORM, goose migrations, PostgreSQL with pgvector (`vector(1024)` embedding columns on atoms, scenes, memories), OpenAI-compatible LLM client. Local setup uses Docker Compose, Caddy, and PostgreSQL 18; local dev Postgres is at 127.0.0.1:5432 and local server default is http://127.0.0.1:8080.
- Source: github.com/colinleefish/mypast; local repo: /Users/liguanghui/Virginia/colinleefish/mypast.
- Frontend lives in ui-next and uses pnpm; the Go binary serves the static export at /ui. API caps list endpoints at 300 rows server-side.
- Docker build is three-stage (node:22 for UI, golang:1.26 for Go, alpine runtime), embedding the static UI into the Go binary.

## Pipeline & memory model
- Pipeline: T0 ingestion (no LLM) → T1 extract → T2 scene → T3 memory rollup; T1–T3 use the chat LLM. Also described as a T1→T3 pyramid. Capture is tool-agnostic via hooks (no SDK required); sessions are ingested through an upload API into immutable `session_turns` (T0), which are ground-truth evidence and never rewritten.
- T1 extracts atoms from turns; it is append-only by design, and re-extraction requires deleting old atoms first to avoid duplicates. T1 skips skill attachments as non-durable session state.
- T2 processes one session at a time (scenes never mix atoms across sessions), groups atoms by `scene_name`, chunks into batches, and uses deterministic UUIDv5 scene URIs derived from `(session_id, scene name)` with upsert-and-prune on rebuild.
- T3 rolls up atoms globally by `(category, slug)` into versioned memory rows linked via `source_scene_uris`, using `superseded_at`; T3 is never updated in place (insert + supersede). `DistillMemory` uses temperature-0 to skip unchanged memory versions and bound churn.
- pipeline_state: one row per session tracking T1/T2/T3 worker statuses (idle/pending/running/failed), stored in Postgres so workers resume after restarts.
- Memory categories: profile, preferences, entities, events; events are insert-only. T3 currently routes preference-like and third-party facts into the profile singleton instead of `preferences/` and `entities/`.
- Memories are addressed by `rmb://` URIs (e.g. `rmb://events/...`, `rmb://corrections/...`, `rmb://profile`, `rmb://preferences/<slug>`). Inspection routes memory URIs to the memories table with active-row filtering. Memories table has partial unique indexes on `uri` and `(category, slug)`.

## Recall & quality
- Recall: hybrid vector + FTS search with RRF fusion over a flat candidate set; hierarchical score-propagation is deferred. Uses progressive disclosure: search abstracts, then drill into scene body, atoms, and raw turns.
- Scenes have two layers: a ~100-token abstract for search/filter and a full Markdown body with the narrative.
- Embed worker backfills embeddings using BigModel embedding-3 at dimensions 1024; embed worker uses a separate embedding provider from the chat LLM.
- Uses Ebbinghaus-style decay curves for forgetting.
- Eval harness: `mypast eval` runs FTS recall probes from `scripts/eval_queries.txt` and exits non-zero on regression. Human-in-the-loop assertions and corrections are central to maintaining memory quality.

## Corrections & aliases
- Corrections are human-in-the-loop sibling artifacts; CLI command is `correction add` (aliases: correct/fix), addressed as `rmb://corrections/...`.
- Entity aliases use flat-star topology: aliases point to one canonical, depth fixed at 1, cycles impossible by construction. Aliases are currently human-authored; `alias_candidates` is scaffolded for a future propose-and-confirm worker.

## CLI, config & integration
- Unified binary switches between client and server modes via `MYPAST_URL`. CLI commands `find/search/cat/tree/meta` are dual-mode: client via `MYPAST_URL`, otherwise local DB. Operational commands (`t1/t2/t3 backfill`, `embed status`, `eval`) are DB-direct by design. The `serve` command always connects to the local database regardless of `MYPAST_URL`. CLI inspect commands include `cat`, `meta`, and `tree` for sessions and atoms.
- CLI binary is built into `./bin/mypast` via `make build`; desktop install at `~/.mypast/bin/mypast`, PATH configured in `~/.zshrc`; refresh via `make build && cp bin/mypast ~/.mypast/bin/mypast`.
- Config: `~/.mypast.conf` holds `MYPAST_URL` and Basic auth credentials, including production credentials from `/opt/mypast/.env`.
- Hooks configured in `~/.cursor/hooks.json` and `~/.claude/settings.json`, both pointing at the mypast CLI; supports Cursor and Claude Code sources (`hook-submit` sends conversations to the upload API). The codex source mentioned in CLI help is not implemented. Integrates with Claude Code via a Stop hook.
- Agent instruction guide: `docs/cli-agent-guide.md`.

## Hosting & deployment
- Production: https://mem.colinleefish.com (API + UI at /ui/), Basic auth username `mypast`. Production code lives at `/opt/mypast` on a remote server; production DB name is `mypast_dev` (misleading leftover from default config). Local server default: http://127.0.0.1:8080.
- Frontend proxy injects Basic auth server-side so credentials never reach the browser. Pipeline UI displays `session_key` (first 8 characters) with click-through to session detail; UI has a Memories tab.
- Deploy: agent-driven via `make ci` and `make deploy` over SSH; no GitHub Actions. Push to main, then `make deploy`; `deploy.sh` does `git reset --hard` to the pushed SHA on production so main goes live, and sets `https_proxy=http://localhost:1080` on the production server during `git fetch`. A GitHub environment named production exists.
- CI runs `go test ./...` with no database; tests are pure unit tests. Container image is deployed to Aliyun (Alibaba Cloud) Container Registry (ACR). Production deployment uses Docker Compose (`docker-compose.prod.yml`) via `make deploy`.

## Docs & roadmap
- Design doc: `docs/design-l0-l4.zh.md`; consolidation review: `docs/memory-consolidation-review.zh.md` (cites arXiv:2605.12978); roadmap: `docs/plan.md` (phases B–E and post-pyramid backlog).
- A legacy summarizer merges turns into `sessions.overview_text`; it is to be retired in Phase E.

## Status record (dated)
- 2026-06-06: T1 atom extraction works in production; T2 scenes and T3 memories were not yet implemented. T0 raw turns remain immutable ground-truth evidence.
- 2026-06-07: ~3,800 atoms across 122 sessions.
- 2026-06-10: T0 raw turn store contained ~948 turns. Known open items: M1 (auth-env footgun), M2 (FTS index expression mismatch), M5 (slug-less atom drop). T3 profile category over-absorbs noise and the `preferences` category was empty. Eval suite passed 8/8 tests.
- Current: T1 (extract) and T2 (scene) workers run in production at mem.colinleefish.com; T3 rollups are implemented/versioned with known routing issues (see 2026-06-10).

memories.body:
# StarOrigin (星源 / 星云)

## Identity
- StarOrigin (星源) is HungryStudio's internal AI agent platform / AI Center (星源AI中心), for game designers and developers; it is also an R&D org unit 星云 (including 美术组/策划组/测试工程组/项目管理组) that develops BlockCrush, and a CostGroup/project label used for tasks; many user tickets are tagged 星源.
- It is also associated with the company behind the StarOrigin AIGC watermark project, and is a team that collaborates on Kafka topic contracts.
- The user works on StarOrigin as SRE and handles starorigin deployments; user is Owner of GCP project `starorigin-485010` (liguanghui@hungrystudio.com).
- In 星源AI中心, project `sc-starorigin` is owned by 李广慧; Wang Yan is the procurement contact for sandbox ECS resources StarOrigin will use.
- Classification: a cost group/project (StarOrigin AI agents); resources named `starorigin` belong to it.

## Infrastructure & environments
- Multi-cloud: Aliyun ACK, GCP GKE, AWS EKS, and Tencent Cloud (Tencent GPU instances are proxied via LiteLLM); also an AWS account linked to colinleefish@gmail.com.
- Uses Alibaba Cloud services including ECS, ECI, LiteLLM, AgentRun, Tair, Nacos, OSS, RDS; also has an AI gateway (星源大模型网关) and AWS US production backends.
- K8s clusters include `ack-starorigin-dev` and `ack-starorigin-prod`; two owned cluster IDs: `c2d24c874b7a74790a45566ce8bd7e12d` and `c8e7b88ff9dbe4815b3b69802d2db6051`. Jenkins kubeconfig credentials: `kubeconfig-ack-starorigin-dev`, `kubeconfig-ack-starorigin-prod`. Prod namespace: `starorigin419-prod`.
- Environments: `crab`, `dolphin`, `shark`, `squid`, `whale`, `prod`; no `turtle`; dev also has `alpha`.
- Dev all-in-one RDS: Aliyun RDS PostgreSQL `archteam-starorigin-dev-all-in-one` at `archteam-starorigin-dev-all-in-one.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com:5432` (PostgreSQL 18.2). Users: superuser `postgres`, app `starorigin`, read-only `jumpserver_readonly`, `dw_reader_starorigin_kol`. One database per service/env (`starorigin_<env>_{origin,web,agentserver,memory,toolhub,knowhowhub,eval}`), hosting crab/dolphin/shark/squid/whale/alpha DB sets; `starorigin_crab_*` lives on this instance in cluster `ack-starorigin-dev`, namespace `starorigin419-crab`.
- Dev all-in-one host `archteam-starorigin-dev-all-in-one-monkey` at 10.100.85.16 runs dockerd, alloy (Grafana telemetry agent), redis-server, and three uvicorn apps on ports 8000, 8080, and 8002.
- Production DB: PostgreSQL 18 on Aliyun RDS at `archteam-starorigin419-prd-pg18.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com`; `starorigin_prod_origin` is the production DB, plus `starorigin_prod_analytics`. Prod uses Aliyun Tair for Redis; prod includes `docproc` but no standalone memory or analytics deployment.
- Dev environments run ~9 services (including `docproc`, `starconsumer`, `valkey`); prod runs 7 (no `starconsumer`/`valkey`, but includes `docproc`). Crab env has `starconsumer` DB and in-cluster Redis `valkey`; it includes `dataanalysis-api` and `dataanalysis-worker` (FGLM-6811 data-analysis service) with no prod counterpart.
- Production data: 8 PostgreSQL DBs on Aliyun RDS, Redis/Tair, Elasticsearch, NAS, and 96+ Aliyun FC functions.
- StarOrigin stardream dev/prod VMs have static external IPs 136.110.86.243 and 136.110.123.72.

## Networking & domains
- Domains: `starorigin.youxi123.com` (service endpoint `https://starorigin.youxi123.com/`) and `starorigin-new.youxi123.com`; both tracked by Umami.
- `starorigin.youxi123.com` resolves only to public IP 106.75.17.22; no internal (`-inner`) DNS record exists; port 443 unreachable from the Airflow VPC.
- One ALB per logical edge (e.g. `starorigin-dolphin-alb`, `starorigin-public-alb`) with multiple Ingresses per ALB. Prod ALB is Intranet with 600s timeouts; whale env uses one AlbConfig/ALB shared by many Ingresses; dolphin env splits routes into `routes/private` and `routes/public`.
- Ingress files named `ingress-NNNN-<svc>.yaml`; numeric prefix determines ALB priority. `starorigin-mcps-route` ingress is deployed in both prod and staging clusters; prod namespace `starorigin-mcps-prod` uses the `starfamily-registry` ACR registry.
- Historical nginx setup and domain `starorigin-dev-monkey.hs99.vip` are outdated and replaced by ALB.

## Services & data
- Services: `web`, `origin`, `agentserver`, `toolhub`, `knowhowhub`, `eval`, `dataanalysis` (plus `memory` as a service/database); core services also described as agent-server, origin-server, memory, web/analytics.
- Service databases: `agentserver`, `analytics`, `eval`, `knowhowhub`, `memory`, `origin`, `toolhub`, `web`.
- LiteLLM production gateway is hosted in GCP project `starorigin-485010` (with Cloud Armor policies) and proxies to Tencent GPU instances; used on AWS/GCP/Aliyun.
- Origin service uses Nacos at `mse-90ac80e2-nacos-ans.mse.aliyuncs.com:8848`, namespace `starorigin-prod`, and OSS bucket `starorigin-sandbox-prod` in cn-beijing for user workspace files.
- OSS buckets follow `oss-starorigin-<role>-<env>`, except web service's `starorigin-static`.
- StarOrigin (星源平台) has an Ontology/semantic dictionary feature storing structured business concepts, relations, and constraints for AI agents.
- Report-analysis service produces Kafka topic `starlink.dwb.mjwd.experiment-analysis-reports`; StarOrigin is the source system producing experiment analysis reports consumed by the user's Vector pipeline. Kafka is reachable from the `starlink-blockblast-prod` app host via Aliyun serverless Kafka VPC endpoints.
- PV events dataset `starorigin_pv_events`: 66,735 records, 26 columns.

## Deployment & configuration
- Deployments go through Jenkins with Helm charts; CI build job is `origin-build` on the devops-jenkins server (project `star-origin-mico`).
- Configuration uses `deploy.yaml` plus `config/app.yaml` and `config/secrets.enc.yaml`; all environments use a single `config/app.enc.yaml`. Environment metadata is in `envs/<env>/env-values.yaml`; `env-values.yaml` and `versions.yaml` are treated as single source of truth (no hardcoded chart versions/image tags).
- Makefile `render`/`diff`/`apply` targets reference `helmfile.yaml.gotmpl` (not `helmfile.yaml`).
- Workspace includes `starorigin-deployments` and `starorigin-charts`; the product is deployed via `starorigin-deployments`. `starorigin` is the reference project whose charts/deployments pattern `starlink` follows; the `starorigin` repo hosts Airflow DAGs, including DingTalk document DAGs.
- Production credentials are stored at `e.credentials/starorigin/starorigin419.md`; DBeaver has dev and prd connection profiles.
- GCP: service account `hsdevops-jenkins-ar` in `starorigin-485010` has its JSON key stored as a Jenkins credential.

## Cost / dated record
- StarOrigin is the #1 cost driver in the `caikuai` account/CostGroup: ~52-58% of the monthly cloud bill.
- All StarOrigin resources were created after February 2026.
- May: ~¥50-57K cloud cost.
- June: ~¥75K cloud cost.
- July 2026: ¥100,591 monthly cost.

## Incidents / notes
- StarOrigin's public API is unreachable from the BlockBlast app network (ETIMEDOUT on port 443); port 443 is also unreachable from the Airflow VPC.
- The `starorigin` repo's pre-commit hook blocks commits while `*.enc.yaml` secrets files are left decrypted.

memories.abstract: pgpour is Starlink's internal Rust PostgreSQL-to-Kafka CDC tool, built on supabase/etl; uses logical replication slots (supabase_etl_apply_*), publishes Debezium-style JSON to {prefix}.{schema}.{table}, supports Lua transforms, and has known table_sync_copy restart, orphaned-slot, slot-collision, and <array> rendering quirks. Deployed as per-game Docker containers in dev/alpha/prod stacks.
memories.body:
# pgpour

## Identity
- Internal Starlink CDC tool: streams PostgreSQL WAL changes to Kafka via logical replication.
- Implemented in Rust, built on supabase/etl; producer app for starlink Kafka topics.
- Publishes Debezium-style JSON to Kafka; topic naming convention is `{topic_prefix}.{schema}.{table}`.
- Uses logical replication slots named `supabase_etl_apply_*` (examples: `supabase_etl_apply_75821`, `supabase_etl_apply_18977`; main apply worker slot `supabase_etl_apply_39786`).
- Requires `wal_level=logical`.
- Does not auto-create Kafka topics; missing topics produce `UnknownTopicOrPartition` errors.
- Producer uses lz4 compression.

## Deployment
- Runs as per-game Docker containers on Starlink stacks (jdmj, blockcrush, mjwd, blockblast, lgh).
- Production host: `archteam-starlink-pgpour-prd-all-in-one` (10.100.64.62), running three production containers for blockcrush, mjwd, and blockblast.
- jdmj production does not run on `archteam-starlink-jdmj-prod-1`; it runs on the dedicated pgpour machine (container `starlink-jdmj-pgpour-prod-pgpour-1`).
- Image: `registry.hs99.vip/starlink/pgpour:8e8797b7` (commit 8e8797b, includes the array conversion fix); CPU limit 2, memory limit 2048 MB.
- yl-blockblast runs the authentic version (image `main-2ce47744`, `kafka.targets` schema).
- Typical config path: `/data/starlink-{env}-{game}/config/pgpour/config.yml`; production jdmj config at `/data/starlink-jdmj-pgpour-prod/config/pgpour/config.yml`; general path: `/data/pgpour/config.yml`.
- Config is hybrid: YAML config file plus secret environment variables.
- Generally defined as a docker-compose service; in `starlink-<user>-<game>` stacks it is often behind the `cdc-disabled` profile, with configs at `/data/starlink-<user>-<game>/config/pgpour/`. A `pgpour` profile is also referenced as creating replication slots.
- On alpha stacks (blockcrush, blockblast, mjwd) it runs without profile gating.
- On BlockCrush prod it is not defined in Docker Compose; config remains under `config/pgpour/` on the host.
- Container naming examples: `starlink-blockblast-alpha-pgpour-1`, `starlink-blockcrush-alpha-pgpour-1`, `starlink-mjwd-alpha-pgpour-1`, `starlink-blockcrush-prod-pgpour-1`, `starlink-mjwd-pgpour-prod-pgpour-1`, `starlink-lgh-blockcrush-pgpour-1`, `starlink-lhh-blockblast-pgpour`.
- `starlink-*-pgpour-1` containers stream CDC from the starlink dev all-in-one RDS into blockblast/blockcrush client databases (yl, dwb, lgh, lhh).
- Other deployments: `starlink-lby-blockcrush` (profile `cdc-disabled`), `yy-blockblast` (intentionally idle, profile-gated), app-1 connected to Aliyun RDS, `lgh-jdmj` needed for Kafka message ingestion, and `prd-mahjongwonders` on the app-1 WondersMahjong web server.
- Local project path: `/Users/liguanghui/hs.projects/starlink/pgpour`.
- Production Starlink Kafka cluster is on `youxi123.com` / `prd`; production pgpour configs include MJWD, BlockCrush, JDMJ, and Block Bloom (with pgpour/Vector).
- Dated artifact: `docker-compose.yml.bak.20260527-disable-pgpour` had pgpour disabled.

## Replication and sync behavior
- Replication slot names are cluster-wide; default `supabase_etl_apply_1` is collision-prone across stacks.
- During initial copy, pgpour creates per-table sync slots and deletes them once the table reaches `sync_done`.
- Re-enabling pgpour creates a new replication slot and attaches to existing publications; it re-snapshots from current.
- With `with_init: false`, initial sync skips historical rows; only post-startup changes stream to Kafka.
- The synced-table set is frozen at first run; a full restart is required for newly added tables to be picked up.
- Tables absent from the publication (e.g. `bbc_publication`) are not CDC'd.
- pgpour performs a PG `table_sync_copy` on restart, causing heavy memory/disk usage; this was the root cause of the July hang.

## Kafka message behavior and features
- Supports Lua transforms for filtering/cleaning CDC data, with DLQ routing for errors.
- Built-in helpers: `keep`, `drop_nulls`, `rename`, `now_ms`.
- v2.23 routes tables via `event.table` and emits full outbox event envelopes on insert only, unlike older Debezium-style `event.source.table` routing with flat `after` rows.
- Kafka message keys are derived from the source table's primary key; text keys are JSON-encoded as quoted strings.
- On source DELETE, emits tombstone-style Kafka messages with `op: 'delete'`, `before` populated, and `after` null.
- Postgres array/composite columns are rendered as the literal string `<array>` in Kafka messages; genuine jsonb/array columns serialize as proper JSON.
- Known quirks: tombstone-style delete messages, `<array>` literal rendering, and lz4 producer compression.
- Used to sync tables such as merged `feature_config_workflow_info` and `bbc_publication`, and streams WAL from `bbc_publication` to Kafka (e.g. `solution_outbox` changes).

## Configuration examples
- Alpha RDS (pgpour): host `archteam-starlink-alpha-pg.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com`, database `alpha_blockblast_client`, publication `bbc_publication`, Kafka brokers `10.9.169.2:9092, 10.9.131.68:9092, 10.9.103.246:9092`, topic prefix `starlink.blockblast.alpha`.
- Blockblast alpha config: `/data/starlink-blockblast-alpha/config/pgpour/config.yml` on `archteam-starlink-alpha`, mounted as `/etc/pgpour/config.yml` in the container.
- dwb-blockcrush: streams `bbc_publication` to Kafka with topic prefix `starlink.blockcrush.dwb`; Postgres at `starlink-dev-all-in-one.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com:5432`, database `dwb_blockcrush_client`; defined in docker-compose.yml behind the `cdc-disabled` profile; config at `/data/starlink-dwb-blockcrush/config/pgpour/config.yml`.
- `starlink-lgh-blockcrush-pgpour-1` runs pipeline 63858 for the `lgh_blockcrush_client` database, with `with_init: false`, on `archteam-starlink-dev-all-in-one`.
- Blockblast deployments publish Kafka CDC for `starlink.blockblast.{env}.rustyme.*` topics from seven feature tables, including `starlink.blockblast.yy.rustyme.*`.

## Known issues and constraints
- Does not allow two targets with the same `(brokers, topic_prefix)`.
- Cleanup bug: on Kafka produce failure during table sync, can leave an orphaned `table_sync` slot that is never cleaned up.
- Crashes with `InvalidState` when its PostgreSQL connection is terminated by an administrator command, because tables were synchronized based on a different apply worker lineage.
- When re-enabled for a database, pgpour recreates fresh replication slots and re-snapshots from current.
- Operational note for blockcrush prod: restarting pgpour must not touch the pipeline container, to preserve the replication slot.

## Memory Pyramid

- Pipeline stages: T1 (atom extraction), T2 (scene building), and T3.
- The T2 stage uses the `deepseek-v4-flash` LLM via Volces.

## L2 Stage Details

- Up to 16 parallel `build_scenes` calls, backpressured to 8.
- Maximum batch size: 60 atoms.
- HTTP client timeout is hardcoded to 120 seconds, with 2 retries.
- The last L2 error text is stored in the `l2_last_error` field in SQLite.

## RMB Desktop Build / Release Preferences

- Build command: `make app-build SIGN_KEYCHAIN_PASS='rmb-sign'`
- After building, run `make notarize`.

### Release Workflow
1. Unlock the `rmb-sign` keychain.
