memories.body:
## Identity & repo
- RMB Desktop (product name and browser title; repo `rmb-desktop`): user-developed, local-first macOS desktop app for durable agent memory. Currently under development by the user.
- Repo: `colinleefish/rmb-desktop`; local checkout `/Users/liguanghui/Virginia/colinleefish/rmb-desktop`.
- Architecture: Go + Rust/Tauri, SQLite (WAL) + sqlite-vec, embedded web UI. Bundle ID `me.remember.rmb`; menu-bar app via `LSUIElement`; not sandboxed; Hardened Runtime; Tauri `exceptionDomain` empty (allows cleartext HTTP through ATS exceptions).
- Go project: rmbd daemon at `cmd/rmbd/main.go`; HTTP server in `internal/httpserver`.
- Distribution: signed/notarized aarch64 DMGs via GitHub Releases and Cloudflare R2 (`releases.re-mem-ber.me`). Planned packages: DMG (macOS), MSI/EXE (Windows), AppImage/DEB (Linux). Tauri updater disabled (`updater.active: false`).

## Version record
- Observed builds: 0.1.0, 0.1.1, 0.1.2, 0.1.9, v0.1.16 (latest as of Aug 2026), and 0.1.19 (newest observed). Personal product, license TBD.
- v0.1.18 included `llm.timeout` default 45s, T2 atom trim, and real error text in logs.
- v0.1.19 logs every LLM request to `/api/v1/debug/logs` (`op`, `attempt`, `model`, `host`, `status`, `latency_ms`, `req_bytes`, `resp_bytes`, `err`).

## Install/runtime
- Installed at `/Applications/RMB Desktop.app`; earlier observed at `/Applications/rmb.app` with display name `rmb`.
- Bundles CLI (`rmb`), daemon (`rmbd`/`rmbd-desktop`), and Tauri menubar/tray app; daemon binds `127.0.0.1:19019`.
- On startup, newer binaries sync to `~/.rmb/bin/`; first-run bootstrap installs sidecars at `~/.rmb/bin/rmb-app` and `~/.rmb/bin/rmbd-desktop` (earlier builds: `~/.rmb/bin/rmb`) and a LaunchAgent for rmbd. Launch-at-login via `launch_at_login` in config and `~/Library/LaunchAgents/me.remember.rmb.plist`.
- Config: `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/config.yaml`; SQLite DB at `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/data/rmb.db`.
- Onboarding first-run gate: `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/onboarding.complete` (`completed_at`, `skipped_agents`); endpoints `GET /api/v1/onboarding/status`, `POST /api/v1/onboarding/complete`, `POST /api/v1/onboarding/reset`.

## Memory, data, sync
- Local-first; defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:19019`; supports dual-submit to hosted `rmb.colinleefish.com` and deferred sync at `sync.re-mem-ber.me`. Does not report installs/heartbeats; explicitly rejects iCloud/Dropbox due to corruption risk.
- Memory pipeline: L0-L3 pyramid (turns, atoms, scenes, memories) addressed by `rmb://` URIs; L1/L2/L3 workers + embed worker, stages t1/t2/t3; state in SQLite `pipeline_state` table; `recall_stats` table keyed by URI. Categories: profile, entities, preferences, events, corrections, recall stats.
- Supports OpenAI-compatible API format for LLM/embedding providers; API keys stored in config.

## API/debug
- `GET /healthz` returns ok when DB opens (migrations passed); `GET /api/v1/version` reports app version, not DB schema version.
- Debug endpoints under `/debug/` and `/api/v1/debug/*`: workers, in-flight tasks, backpressure, logs, SQLite, pipeline stuck/unstick/requeue, LLM build-scenes, pipeline dry-run. They are unauthenticated.
- `pipeline_state` has `l1/l2/l3_last_error` and `l1/l2/l3_started_at`; workers expose cycle, per-session step, and backpressure via in-memory registry.

## UI / web
- Settings tabs: General, Models, Advanced; Integrations is a top-level sidebar item. General includes display language, distillation database path, config file collection address; configuration page has LLM/embedding API key fields.
- Sidebar uses a Lucide Brain icon as placeholder brand mark; favicon is purple gradient SVG at `ui/public/favicon.svg`.
- Web UI is a Vite build embedded via `go:embed`; assets copied from `webui/dist` by `make webui-build`; dev via `npm run dev:mock-setup`; `internal/http/static/web/` is generated output only, source of truth in `webui/`.

## Integrations, migrations, ops
- Supports agents: Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi. Currently writes shell hooks for OpenCode and Pi, which is incorrect for these agents.
- Schema migrations run automatically via goose on rmbd start (SQL embedded); end users don't run migration scripts; stop→migrate→restart orchestration is not built. As of 2026-08-14, README doesn't document auto-migrations and Makefile advertises a non-existent `make migrate`.
- `scripts/backfill-from-remote.py` is a data-migration/import script for remote rmb sessions, not a schema migration.
- Deployed/under test on remote box `10.254.24.7` (debug API at `10.254.24.7:19019`) and quick whale VM; rmb-desktop is the user's real database used by the pipeline daemon. Direct SQL into its memories is possible but fragile.

memories.abstract: RMB Desktop (rmb-desktop) is a local-first Tauri v1 (Rust tray) + Go daemon macOS menubar app by colinleefish (github.com/colinleefish/rmb-desktop) for durable agent memory. Bundles rmb CLI and rmbd-desktop daemon on 127.0.0.1:19019, SQLite WAL + L0-L3 memory layers, OpenAI-compatible APIs, signed DMG releases.
memories.body:
## Identity
- **RMB Desktop (rmb-desktop)** is the desktop GUI / local desktop version of the RMB product and is also described as a local-first memory CLI. The rmb-desktop repo is the repository for the RMB project and is aligned with the main rmb repository.
- Source checkout: `/Users/liguanghui/Virginia/colinleefish/rmb-desktop`; GitHub: `github.com/colinleefish/rmb-desktop`.
- Product name: **RMB Desktop** in Finder and menu bar; bundle identifier `me.remember.rmb`; installed at `/Applications/RMB Desktop.app`; tray shell is RMB.app. Tauri app name and browser title: RMB Desktop.
- Built as a Tauri v1 tray shell (Rust) + Go backend (rmbd daemon), with SQLite + sqlite-vec. On macOS it is configured as a menu-bar app via LSUIElement, is not sandboxed, runs with Hardened Runtime, and releases are signed and notarized. Tauri `exceptionDomain` is empty, allowing cleartext HTTP through ATS exceptions.
- Under development by the user, who is also working on rmb-desktop testing.

## Architecture & install
- The project bundles a CLI (`rmb`), a daemon (`rmbd-desktop`), and a Tauri menubar/tray app. The rmbd daemon is built from this repo and listens on `127.0.0.1:19019`.
- Tauri scaffold tray menu has Start/Stop rmbd and Open Dashboard.
- Binaries are installed under `~/.rmb/bin/`; observed client sidecar path/name references include `rmb`, `rmb-app`, and `rmb-desktop`, and the daemon sidecar is `rmbd-desktop`.
- First-run bootstrap copies bundled externalBin sidecars into `~/.rmb/bin/` and installs a LaunchAgent for rmbd. On startup, bundled rmb/rmbd binaries are synced to `~/.rmb/bin/` if newer.
- Runtime data and config live under `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/`: `config.yaml`, `data/rmb.db`, `onboarding.complete`. Config holds LLM and embedding API keys.
- Launch-at-login is stored in `config.yaml` under `launch_at_login` and registers `~/Library/LaunchAgents/me.remember.rmb.plist`.
- First-run/onboarding gate uses `onboarding.complete` (JSON with `completed_at` and `skipped_agents`); endpoints: `GET /api/v1/onboarding/status`, `POST /api/v1/onboarding/complete`, `POST /api/v1/onboarding/reset`.

## Data & local-first behavior
- Purpose: durable agent-memory desktop app. Captures full conversations and distills them through an L0-L1-L2-L3 pyramid (turns, atoms, scenes, memories), addressed by `rmb://` URIs.
- Local-first app: SQLite in WAL mode with memory layers L0 through L3; uses sqlite-vec. Memory categories include profile, entities, preferences, and events; supports corrections and recall stats. A `recall_stats` table is keyed by URI.
- It does not report installs or heartbeats, and iCloud/Dropbox sync is rejected due to corruption risk. Current behavior also supports dual-submit to the hosted endpoint `rmb.colinleefish.com` and deferred sync at `sync.re-mem-ber.me`.
- Exposes `/healthz`, which returns ok when the database opens (migrations passed) and reports SQLite/vector status. `GET /api/v1/version` reports app version but not DB schema version.
- HTTP API on `127.0.0.1:19019` is unauthenticated. A remote RMB Desktop instance is deployed at `10.254.24.7`, with debug API reachable at `10.254.24.7:19019`.
- Direct SQL into RMB Desktop's memories is possible but fragile.

## Web UI / frontend
- Web UI source is in `webui/`; dev server is started with `npm run dev:mock-setup`.
- Built UI is embedded via `go:embed`; assets are copied from `webui/dist` by `make webui-build`. `internal/http/static/web/` is generated output only and must not be hand-edited; regenerate with `make webui-build`.
- Sidebar uses a Lucide Brain icon as a placeholder brand mark; favicon is a purple gradient SVG at `ui/public/favicon.svg`.
- Settings page tabs: General, Models, Advanced; Integrations is a top-level sidebar item. General settings include display language, distillation database path, and config file collection address.
- Supports the OpenAI-compatible API format for LLM and embedding providers.
- Supported agents: Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi. Integrations UI includes Cursor, Claude Code, Codex; also used for AI-agent onboarding with an agent install setup flow.
- Known issue: shell hooks are currently written for OpenCode and Pi, which is incorrect for those agents.

## Packaging, release & ops
- Current macOS package is a DMG built via `make app-build` and `finish-dmg.sh`; distributed as signed and notarized aarch64 DMGs via GitHub Releases and Cloudflare R2 at `releases.re-mem-ber.me`.
- Planned distribution targets: DMG for macOS, MSI/EXE for Windows, AppImage/DEB for Linux.
- Tauri updater is disabled (`updater.active: false`).
- Schema migrations use goose on rmbd start; migration SQL files are embedded in the binary, so end users never run migration scripts manually. Stop → migrate → restart orchestration is not yet built.
- `scripts/backfill-from-remote.py` is a data-migration script for importing sessions from remote rmb instances, not a schema migration.

## Development / internals
- Go implementation: rmbd daemon at `cmd/rmbd/main.go`, HTTP server in `internal/httpserver`.
- Pipeline processes sessions through t1/t2/t3 stages via l1/l2/l3 workers plus an embed worker, backed by a SQLite `pipeline_state` table. `pipeline_state` has `l1/l2/l3_last_error` and `l1/l2/l3_started_at` columns.
- Debug API routes are under `/api/v1/debug/*`; additional `/debug/` endpoints expose workers, in-flight tasks, backpressure, logs, SQLite, pipeline stuck/unstick/requeue, LLM build-scenes, and pipeline dry-run.
- L1/L2/L3/embed workers report cycle, per-session step, and backpressure info to an in-memory registry.
- The app folder is the Tauri v1 tray shell containing only tray menu and daemon management; the shipped product includes an rmbd daemon and an embedded web UI.
- Tested on the quick whale VM.

## Version / dated record
- Version 0.1.0 was built for macOS aarch64; observed releases include 0.1.1, 0.1.2, 0.1.9, and 0.1.16. As of August 2026 it was v0.1.16, described as a personal product with license TBD, shipped as a macOS menubar app from re-mem-ber.me.
- Release 0.1.19 logs every LLM request to `/api/v1/debug/logs` with fields `op`, `attempt`, `model`, `host`, `status`, `latency_ms`, `req_bytes`, `resp_bytes`, and `err`.
- Release 0.1.19 includes 0.1.18 fixes: `llm.timeout` default 45s, T2 atom trim, and real error text in logs.
- 2026-08-14 observation: the README does not document automatic DB migrations, and the Makefile advertises a `make migrate` target that does not exist.

memories.body:
# StarOrigin (星源 / 星云)

## Identity
- StarOrigin is used across contexts as: HungryStudio's internal AI agent platform for game designers/developers; a project/system the user works on and supports as SRE; a team that collaborates on Kafka topic contracts; and a cost group/project in the Aliyun caikuai-cn account. It is also described as the company behind the StarOrigin AIGC watermark project.
- Also called 星源AI中心 (StarOrigin AI Center), the org unit that builds internal AI tools; 星云 (starorigin) is the Hungry Studio division (美术组/策划组/测试工程组/项目管理组) that develops BlockCrush.
- Workspaces/projects include starorigin-deployments, starorigin-charts, and the starorigin repo. It is a reference project whose charts/deployments pattern `starlink` follows.

## Ownership & access
- User is an Owner of GCP project `starorigin-485010`, owned by 李广慧 (liguanghui@hungrystudio.com). StarOrigin support tickets are often tagged 星源. `sc-starorigin` is a project in 星源AI中心, also owned by 李广慧.
- GCP project `starorigin-485010` hosts the LiteLLM production gateway and Cloud Armor policies; it has service account `hsdevops-jenkins-ar` (JSON key stored as a Jenkins credential).
- Main service: https://starorigin.youxi123.com/. Production domains `starorigin.youxi123.com` and `starorigin-new.youxi123.com` are tracked by Umami. `starorigin.youxi123.com` resolves only to public IP 106.75.17.22; port 443 was unreachable from the Airflow VPC, and no internal (-inner) DNS record exists. Public API was also unreachable from the blockblast app network (ETIMEDOUT on port 443).
- Production credentials are stored at `e.credentials/starorigin/starorigin419.md` in the workspace. DBeaver has `dev` and `prd` connection profiles for starorigin.

## Architecture / deployment
- Runs on Aliyun ACK, AWS EKS, and GCP GKE; uses Helm, Jenkins, Airflow, Alibaba Cloud ECS/ECI, LiteLLM, and AgentRun. Owns two Kubernetes clusters with IDs `c2d24c874b7a74790a45566ce8bd7e12d` and `c8e7b88ff9dbe4815b3b69802d2db6051`.
- Has an AI gateway (星源大模型网关) and AWS US production backends. LiteLLM gateway also runs on AWS/GCP/Aliyun and proxies to Tencent GPU instances.
- Production cluster: `ack-starorigin-prod`, namespace `starorigin419-prod`. Dev cluster: `ack-starorigin-dev` (crab namespace `starorigin419-crab`). Jenkins credentials: `kubeconfig-ack-starorigin-dev` and `kubeconfig-ack-starorigin-prod` (prod kubeconfig stored as a credential). CI build job: `origin-build` on the devops-jenkins server (project star-origin-mico).
- Production is backed by 8 PostgreSQL databases on Aliyun RDS, Redis, Elasticsearch, NAS, and 96+ Aliyun FC functions. Production runs on an AWS account linked to colinleefish@gmail.com. StarOrigin operates Aliyun infrastructure including the agentrun AI-agent sandbox fleet.
- Services: web, origin, agentserver, toolhub, knowhowhub, eval, dataanalysis. Prod runs a `docproc` service but has no standalone memory or analytics deployment; dev also runs docproc, starconsumer, and valkey, while prod does not run starconsumer/valkey. Crab has `dataanalysis-api` and `dataanalysis-worker` (FGLM-6811) with no prod counterpart.
- MCP-related prod namespace `starorigin-mcps-prod` uses the `starfamily-registry` ACR registry; the starorigin MCP route ingress (`starorigin-mcps-route`) is deployed in both prod and staging clusters.
- One ALB per logical edge (e.g. `starorigin-dolphin-alb`, `starorigin-public-alb`) with multiple Ingresses per ALB. Prod ALB is Intranet with 600s timeouts; whale env uses one AlbConfig/ALB shared by many Ingresses. Ingresses are per-service files `ingress-NNNN-<svc>.yaml`; numeric prefix determines ALB priority; the dolphin environment splits routes into routes/private and routes/public.

Environment metadata is in `envs/<env>/env-values.yaml`; `env-values.yaml` and `versions.yaml` are the source of truth for versions. Kafka StarOrigin is reachable from the starlink-blockblast-prod host via Aliyun serverless Kafka VPC endpoints.

memories.abstract: RMB (Recall Memory Bank) is the user's personal long-term memory system for AI-agent conversations: Go server (Postgres/pgvector) plus Tauri desktop app with SQLite, CLI, and web UI; T0-T3 distillation pyramid, rmb:// URIs, corrections, Cursor/Claude/Codex/OpenCode/Pi hooks; repo colinleefish/rmb, live at rmb.colinleefish.com.
memories.body:
# RMB (Recall Memory Bank)

## Identity
- RMB is the user's personal long-term memory system/product for AI-agent conversations, also serving as a personal skills system and skill registry. Former names include mem9, mem-colinleefish, mem-colinleefish-com, and mypast.
- Owned and built by the user; project source at `/Users/liguanghui/Virginia/colinleefish/rmb`; GitHub repo `github.com/colinleefish/rmb`; production site https://rmb.colinleefish.com (SSH access as root@rmb.colinleefish.com).
- Architecture: Go server (Gin, GORM, goose migrations) with PostgreSQL/pgvector; React/Next.js web UI served under `/ui`; Tauri macOS menu-bar app; Go CLI `rmb`. The server itself is a single binary that runs `/rmb serve`.

## Architecture and data model
- Distillation pyramid T0 turns -> T1 atoms -> T2 scenes -> T3 cross-session memories; categories: `profile`, `preferences`, `entities`, `events`.
- Append-first, versioned memories; events are immutable and first-write-wins by URI; human corrections outrank machine-distilled facts; separate append-only `corrections` table synced by id; newest-wins conflict resolution; no hard-delete primitive.
- Stable `rmb://` URIs, e.g. `rmb://profile`, `rmb://entities/<slug>`, `rmb://preferences/<slug>`, `rmb://events/<slug>`, `rmb://scenes/<uuid>`, `rmb://skills/<slug>`, `rmb://atoms/<uuid>`, `rmb://agent`.
- Memories stored in a versioned `memories` table keyed by URI with one active row per URI; `recall_stats` table keyed by URI; skill file paths normalize to `rmb://skills/<slug>`; skills versioned by `bundle_sha256`.
- Recall uses hybrid vector + full-text search + RRF fusion; aliases/canonical mode folds duplicate identities into canonical entities; an alias-suggest worker proposes aliases using embeddings.

## Storage and sync
- Server storage: PostgreSQL database `rmb_db` with pgvector (HNSW indexes, vector(1024)). Desktop storage: local SQLite database at `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/data/rmb.db`, served locally at `127.0.0.1:19019` (`/healthz`, `/ui/`).
- Desktop and server instances share session UUIDs. Sync resolves conflicts by syncing rows by id, unioning provenance, and re-distilling; sessions/turns sync by `session_key` and turn id; session `turn_count` is computed at read time, not stored.
- Recall stats are recorded server-side via `rmb search`, `rmb cat`, and `rmb meta` commands (requires migration `00023_recall_stats.sql`).
- Cross-device sync is a deferred paid feature (`sync.re-mem-ber.me`); syncing `rmb.db` via iCloud/Dropbox is considered unsafe.

## Deployment and hosting
- Production deployed with Docker only (`make deploy`), not Vercel; Docker image at `registry.cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/colinleefish/rmb`; server runs a minimal Docker/Caddy runtime at `/app/rmb`; `/healthz` returns the git commit SHA.
- The same server also hosts the pbp stock/sync project: Postgres database `pbp_db` (user `pbp_user_rw`), reachable at `rmb.colinleefish.com:5432` with SSL.
- HTTP basic auth for rmb: username `rmb`, password `sVf3^n5ht`. API uses snake_case JSON and server-side pagination.
- Also has a VitePress docs site with bilingual English/Chinese content under `docs/concept` and `docs/zh/concept`.

## Desktop app and distribution
- macOS menu-bar app (Tauri, no Dock icon) installed at `/Applications/rmb.app`; tray manages the `rmbd` daemon; LaunchAgents are `me.remember.rmb` and `me.remember.rmbd`; tray auto-restarts `rmbd` every ~5 s when health checks fail.
- Distributed via `re-mem-ber.me` and GitHub Releases as DMG/installer; no auto-update (Tauri updater inactive, `active: false`); `bootstrap.rs` refreshes `~/.rmb/bin/` sidecars on launch when bundled binaries are newer.
- Binaries: CLI at `~/.rmb/bin/rmb`; desktop app binary `~/.rmb/bin/rmb-app`; config at `~/.rmb/config.yaml` (also honors `~/.rmb.conf`).
- Config detection requires both `# RMB memory` and `ALWAYS RUN `rmb` cli` markers; old `<!-- rmb:recall:start/end -->` markers remain compatible.

## CLI and agent integrations
- `rmb` CLI connects to local rmbd HTTP API (desktop build) or to https://rmb.colinleefish.com (server build); `rmb --version` prints `rmb dev` instead of a real semver.
- Capture hooks/integrations for Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi, with no SDK required; `hook-submit` parsers exist for Codex, OpenCode, and Pi; Cursor hook uses `./hooks/audit.sh` and adds `timeout: 15`; hook detection checks whether `hooks.stop` contains `rmb hook-submit`.
- Integration artifacts: Cursor needs `hooks.json` + user rules; Claude Code needs `settings.json` + recall file; `internal/setup` package provides detect/preview/apply functions and requires a preview-before-apply workflow.
- CLI manages agent recall instructions (`rmb://agent`) and provides recall rules (`rmb:recall`); called with no arguments, it injects the agent guide into the agent's context at session start.
- Agent guide is bundled as `agent_guide.md`, embedded in the project and mirrored to the DB via `UpsertAgentGuide`; migration 00006 inserts `rmb://agent` and the upserter supersedes it to version 2, permanently offsetting its version counter by one.

## Embeddings and LLM configuration
- Default embedding model: OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small`, default dimension 1024; the configured dimension cannot be changed after setup because re-embedding all memories would be required.
- Some deployments have used Volces Ark (LLM `ark-code-latest`, embeddings `doubao-embedding-vision`); the server has also been described as using DeepSeek (`api.deepseek.com`, model `deepseek-v4-flash`) for LLM calls.
- Workers: T1 extract, T2 scene building, T3 global memory rollup/embed; T3 polls and distills atoms into shared memory buckets; embeddings verified to match the configured vector length exactly.

## Current status and dated record
- As of 2026-07-25, rmb lacked a knowledge base, memory promotion, an entity relationship graph, and multi-tenant sharing (gaps identified against ContextDB).
- Not yet evaluated on MemoryAgentBench; currently has no BitTorrent/DHT code in its stack; no procedural memory track yet; no auto-update mechanism.
- Go project has unit tests only; `TestWritePlist` is environment-dependent and fails when `/Applications/RMB Desktop.app` exists on the host, making `make test` red on developer machines with the app installed.

memories.abstract: rmbd is the Go backend daemon/UI server for RMB/rmb-desktop (installed ~/.rmb/bin/rmbd-desktop), served at 127.0.0.1:19019, managed by launchd/tray, SQLite+goose, memory pipeline L1/L2/L3, Basic Auth, debugging endpoints, LLM stargate.
memories.body:
**Identity / role**
- rmbd is the main service binary and Go backend daemon of the RMB / rmb-desktop project, and the application bundle distributed to users. It is the memory backend daemon on the user's laptop, hosts the PI agent, serves the embedded web UI at `/ui/`, runs a local HTTP server at `http://127.0.0.1:19019`, and handles T3 bucket distillation/rollup.
- Installed as `~/.rmb/bin/rmbd-desktop`; source/project location: `/Users/liguanghui/Virginia/colinleefish/rmb-desktop`; main entrypoint `cmd/rmbd/main.go`. Go project uses CGO + SQLite; internal packages include `db`, `config`, `worker/scene`, `cmd/rmbd`.

**Deployment & operations**
- Managed by launchd as a LaunchAgent; service label `me.remember.rmbd` (plist file also referenced as `com.remember.rmbd.plist`); also managed by the RMB tray app; single-instance lock.
- Started via `make run-rmbd` or the desktop app; built with `make build`. Desktop binary deployed at `~/.rmb/bin/rmbd-desktop`.
- Release process: `make app-build`, notarize, and `release-publish`; the code-signing keychain password is only needed for publishing signed DMG and GitHub releases, not local deployment.
- Does not auto-restart after an app upgrade; has no CLI version command; when run as a bundle, logs are discarded with no export diagnostics path.
- Manages memories and embeddings; restart via RMB Desktop, and restart after embedding configuration changes.

**Database & migrations**
- SQLite database: `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/data/rmb.db`, WAL mode, foreign_keys enabled, using `mattn/go-sqlite3`; DSN uses `_txlock=immediate` (or `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`) to avoid WAL `SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT` write contention.
- Schema migrations use goose, embedded in `internal/db/migrations/`, and run automatically on every daemon startup; agent guide seeding runs after migrations. Migrations are `00001`–`00006`.
- Schema changes ship inside the new rmbd binary and apply automatically on daemon restart; critical coupling exists between the rmbd version and schema version.
- Embeddings stored as BLOB; KNN recall uses sqlite-vec's `vec_distance_cosine` scalar function on the embedding BLOB column, returning only top-k rows (no `vec0` virtual table / MATCH).
- The rmb CLI talks to rmbd via HTTP API, not directly to the database.

**Architecture & memory pipeline**
- Memory pipeline: L1 extract, L2 scene, L3 memory workers, plus an embed step. Concurrency defaults: L1=64, L2=16. Polling: L1/L2 every 15s, L3 every 5m, embed every 30s.
- DB connection pool ceiling is derived from L1/L2 concurrency plus fixed workers and HTTP headroom; dynamic scene chunking is used.
- Memories use vector embeddings and are stored in categories `profile`, `events`, `preferences`, and `entities`.
- Serves integration setup data for the rmb platform; setup previews are computed using built-in merge logic per agent, not dynamic detection.
- Mock setup mode for the integration tab: toggled via localStorage key `rmb.mockSetup` or `npm run dev:mock-setup` in webui; when mock is disabled, rmbd is the backend used for real API testing.

**API & network**
- Defaults to `127.0.0.1:19019` (`http://127.0.0.1:19019/ui/`); can also listen on `0.0.0.0:19019`; one deployment on a remote Mac was exposed at `10.254.24.7:19019`.
- Embeds the webui frontend built from `webui/dist` into `internal/http/static/web/`.
- Uses HTTP Basic Auth for UI and API; `/healthz` is unauthenticated when bound to `0.0.0.0`. Plain HTTP means Basic Auth credentials are cleartext on LAN. Starting on `0.0.0.0` requires `USERNAME`/`PASSWORD` or `RMB_USERNAME`/`RMB_PASSWORD` env vars.
- `healthz` reports status, SQLite version, and vector version.
- Exposes `/api/v1/version`. Onboarding endpoints: `/api/v1/onboarding/status` and `/api/v1/onboarding/complete`, backed by the `onboarding.complete` file in the rmb-desktop support directory; in normal deployments onboarding can be bypassed by creating that file or calling `POST /api/v1/onboarding/complete`.
- Makes HTTPS requests to the LLM API at `stargate.youxi123.com`.

**Debugging / observability**
- `GET /api/v1/debug/logs` is backed by a 2000-line ring buffer, and all slog output is teed to stderr.
- Debug endpoints include `/debug/workers`, `/debug/in-flight`, `/debug/pipeline/stuck`, and `browse/sessions/{key}`; `pipeline_state.t2_last_error` in SQLite holds the actual L2 error text.
- Known logging gaps: `?worker=l2` log filter is broken because L2 logs use `session_id` instead of `worker`; there is no LLM request tracing (URL, status code, latency, response size are not logged); `persist.scenes` failures are not logged because dry-run skips DB writes.

memories.abstract: Jenkins CI/CD at HungryStudio: managed instances devops-jenkins.hs99.vip (uc-devops-jenkins) and archteam-starfamily-jenkins-master (10.100.27.205); builds BBC, starlink, StarOrigin; 11 build jobs dual-push images; stores kubeconfigs and SOPS age key; DB sync/backup and MinIO migration limitations; job inventory and wrapper permission bypass.
memories.body:
## Role
- Jenkins is the CI/CD tool the user manages and uses for CI builds at HungryStudio; it is also a common MCP tool.
- Used for CI/CD with Linux, Windows, and iOS agents.
- Builds and deploys the BBC service and runs CI/CD pipelines for the starlink project (currently starlink/solutionhub and starlink/hs-code-keeper).
- Has a production job `prod_starlink-pm` for starlink, but no test job for starlink.
- Used for pipeline work, including hs-devops pipelines and starorigin deployments; Jenkins holds the `nebula_app_ids` that define the full Nebula game family.

## Known instances/endpoints
- **archteam-starfamily-jenkins-master**: internal Jenkins master/CI server at 10.100.27.205, accessed via JumpServer, on a g7/hfg7 ECS instance; has PostgreSQL 16.14 tools. Used for bbc-deploy jobs, starlink pipeline scripts (e.g. lowcodegql-build), database sync/restoration, PostgreSQL dump/restore, and migration attempts.
- **devops-jenkins.hs99.vip** / **uc-devops-jenkins** (https://devops-jenkins.hs99.vip): Rocky Linux 9.7 x86_64; the user's Jenkins instance. Hosts starlink/ding jobs and starorigin419 jobs/folder; runs starlink deploy and db-migrator playbooks on its local agent; connects to starlink-dev-internal.hs99.vip as root; used for starlink BBC builds, toolhub deployments, and StarOrigin 419 CI. Jobs are organized under folders, e.g. `starorigin-mcps`.
- BlockBlast PRD uses multiple Jenkins instances: main at 10.254.144.112:8181, 中台 at 10.9.94.63:15050, 星链 at starlink-jenkins.hungrystudio.pp.ua:8181, iOS/mbh at mbhpacker1.youxi123.com:8080.

## Builds and registries
- Jenkins has 11 build jobs: bbc, frontend, lowcodegql, pgpour, rustyme, starflow, feworkgql, ding, gql, fakeuser, hfrog.
- All 11 build jobs push to both registry.hs99.vip and starfamily-registry-vpc.cn-beijing.cr.aliyuncs.com; build pipelines dual-push Starlink images to both registries with the same path and tag.
- Jenkins build pipelines (hs.projects) push all Starlink images to registry.hs99.vip.
- Starlink frontend Jenkinsfiles live at hs.projects/hs-devops/jenkins-pipeline-scripts/starlink/jenkins-jobs/frontend/frontend-build/.
- Jenkins manages image tag versions in versions.yaml files.
- **starlink folder** contains 21 `-build` jobs (one per service), e.g. `bbc-build-tiger`, `frontend-build-tiger`, `gql-build`; these build and push Docker images.
- **aigateway/astra folder** hosts StarAstra restart jobs; each job's `scriptPath` points to the corresponding `starastra` path in the repository.
- **starorigin-mcps/star-maxcompute/star-maxcompute-deploy** is hosted by Jenkins.
- **ai-diagnostics-and-notify-when-failure**: Jenkinsfile at `hs-devops/jenkins-pipeline-scripts/misc/jenkins-jobs/ai-diagnostics-and-notify-when-failure/Jenkinsfile` and contains the `jenkinsUserToDingTalkUserId` mapping.

## Credentials, secrets, cluster access
- Stores kubeconfig credentials for starlink, starorigin, and aigateway as Secret file type.
- Kubeconfigs stored as FileCredentialsImpl (Secret File): GKE clusters starorigin-prod (Autopilot) and starorigin-dev (Standard Zonal asia-northeast1-b); Alibaba ACK clusters starorigin dev/prod, starfamily devops, aigateway dev/prod. Used by the hourly ping-clusters job and deploy pipelines.
- gcloud and gke-gcloud-auth-plugin are not installed on the Jenkins host.
- Has an age key for decrypting SOPS-encrypted secrets; jobs decrypt *.enc.yaml files in-place with `sops -d -i` during deployments.
- The sync-envs job syncs deployment configs from the hs-devops repo to the ACK clusters.

## Database, backup, sync
- Used for database sync operations, database restoration tasks, PostgreSQL dump/restore, and dump-and-restore Ansible playbooks (run on the Jenkins x86_64 agent).
- PostgreSQL dump/restore runs on archteam-starfamily-jenkins-master.
- Sync logs and dumps are stored at ~/jdmj-sync-from-crush/.
- Backup scripts on Jenkins: /data/backup-postgres/prd-blockbloom/dump-starlink-db.sh and /data/backup-postgres/alpha-blockbloom/dump-starlink-db.sh; backup-all.sh auto-discovers all dump-starlink-db.sh scripts.
- The pipeline syncs data from prd to alpha but does not include schema changes.
- The Jenkins server at 10.100.27.205 performs migration from MinIO across a cross-VPC link, achieving about 47 KiB/s; migration logs show 425 unexpected EOF errors and many connection reset by peer errors when downloading from MinIO. Jenkins cannot reliably download objects cross-VPC from MinIO and could not finish large file transfers.

## Operational notes
- Jenkins caches the last parameter definitions, so parameter dropdowns only repopulate after a build runs with the updated Jenkinsfile.
- devops-jenkins runs the db-migrator playbooks on its local agent; the Jenkins x86_64 agent runs the dump-and-restore Ansible playbooks.
- In Jenkins, a wrapper job's `build` step queues the downstream job as the Jenkins controller, so a user with Job/Build on the wrapper does not need permission on the underlying job.

# Jenkins (CI/CD)

## Overview
- Jenkins is the user's managed CI/CD tool/service and a common MCP tool.
- Used for CI builds and CI/CD; supports Linux, Windows, and iOS agents.
- Jenkins is the CI system at HungryStudio and part of the user's infrastructure stack.
- Jenkins Master runs on a g7/hfg7 ECS instance.

## Instances
- **User-facing instance** (`uc-devops-jenkins`): https://devops-jenkins.hs99.vip (Rocky Linux 9.7, x86_64). Used for toolhub deployments, StarOrigin CI jobs under the `starorigin419` folder, starlink/ding jobs, starlink BBC builds. Runs starlink deploy and db-migrator playbooks on its local agent, connecting to `starlink-dev-internal.hs99.vip` as root.
- **Internal Jenkins master**: 10.100.27.205, hostname `archteam-starfamily-jenkins-master`, on the internal network, accessed via JumpServer, with PostgreSQL 16.14 tools. Runs bbc-deploy jobs, database syncs/restorations, db-migrator/dump-and-restore Ansible playbooks (x86_64 agent), and starlink pipeline scripts including the lowcodegql-build job. Used for starlink CI/CD pipelines currently pointing to starlink/solutionhub and starlink/hs-code-keeper. Has production job `prod_starlink-pm` for starlink, but no test job for starlink.
- **BlockBlast PRD Jenkins instances**: Main 10.254.144.112:8181, 中台 10.9.94.63:15050, 星链 starlink-jenkins.hungrystudio.pp.ua:8181, iOS/mbh mbhpacker1.youxi123.com:8080.

## Configuration & behavior
- Jenkins caches the last parameter definitions, so parameter dropdowns only repopulate after a build runs with the updated Jenkinsfile.
- Jenkins jobs decrypt *.enc.yaml files in-place with `sops -d -i` during deployments.
- Jenkins has an age key for decrypting SOPS-encrypted secrets.
- A Jenkins sync-envs job syncs deployment configs from the hs-devops repo to the ACK clusters.
- Jenkins manages image tag versions in versions.yaml files.
- Jenkins stores kubeconfigs as FileCredentialsImpl (Secret File) credentials for GKE clusters (starorigin-prod Autopilot, starorigin-dev Standard Zonal asia-northeast1-b) and Alibaba ACK clusters (starorigin dev/prod, starfamily devops, aigateway dev/prod), used by the hourly ping-clusters job and deploy pipelines.
- gcloud and gke-gcloud-auth-plugin are not installed on the Jenkins host.

## Job organization
- Jobs are organized under folders such as `starorigin-mcps`.
- The `starlink` folder contains 21 `-build` jobs (one per service, e.g. `bbc-build-tiger`, `frontend-build-tiger`, `gql-build`) that build and push Docker images.
- Jenkins also has 11 build jobs: `bbc`, `frontend`, `lowcodegql`, `pgpour`, `rustyme`, `starflow`, `feworkgql`, `ding`, `gql`, `fakeuser`, `hfrog`.
- All 11 build jobs push to both `registry.hs99.vip` and `starfamily-registry-vpc.cn-beijing.cr.aliyuncs.com` with the same path and tag (dual-push).
- Jenkins build pipelines (`hs.projects`) push all Starlink images to `registry.hs99.vip`.
- Starlink frontend build Jenkinsfiles live at `hs.projects/hs-devops/jenkins-pipeline-scripts/starlink/jenkins-jobs/frontend/frontend-build/`.
- StarAstra restart jobs live under the `aigateway/astra` folder; each job's `scriptPath` points to the corresponding `starastra` path in the repository.
- The `starorigin-mcps/star-maxcompute/star-maxcompute-deploy` job runs on this Jenkins.
- The `ai-diagnostics-and-notify-when-failure` job's Jenkinsfile is at `hs-devops/jenkins-pipeline-scripts/misc/jenkins-jobs/ai-diagnostics-and-notify-when-failure/Jenkinsfile` and contains the `jenkinsUserToDingTalkUserId` mapping.
- Jenkins holds the `nebula_app_ids` that define the full Nebula game family.

## Permissions behavior
- A wrapper job's `build` step queues the downstream job as the Jenkins controller, so a user with `Job/Build` on the wrapper does not need permission on the underlying job.
- This build-step permission bypass only applies when users trigger the wrapper; direct triggering of the downstream job still requires `Job/Build` on that job.

## Builds / deployments
- Jenkins is used to build and deploy the BBC service.
- Jenkins is used for database sync operations and database restoration tasks.
- The Jenkins pipeline syncs data from prd to alpha but does not include schema changes.

## Migration / MinIO issues
- Jenkins at 10.100.27.205 performed migration from MinIO across a cross-VPC link, achieving ~47 KiB/s.
- Jenkins migration logs show 425 unexpected EOF errors and many "connection reset by peer" errors when downloading from MinIO.
- Jenkins cannot reliably download objects cross-VPC from MinIO and could not finish large file transfers.

## Backup scripts (internal master)
- Backup scripts are installed at `/data/backup-postgres/prd-blockbloom/dump-starlink-db.sh` and `/data/backup-postgres/alpha-blockbloom/dump-starlink-db.sh`; `backup-all.sh` auto-discovers all `dump-starlink-db.sh` scripts.
- Stores sync logs and dumps at `~/jdmj-sync-from-crush/`.

memories.abstract: feature_config is the core feature-config/creative-idea table in the starlink BlockCrush/blockblast client DB: 54 columns, links to fc_workflow_info, unique on (platform, feature_desc), synced to feature_config_workflow_info.
memories.body:
# feature_config

- Core database table in the starlink project, specifically the BlockCrush/blockblast client database. It stores feature configurations and 创意 (creative feature ideas).
- Serves as the A source table in the feature-config merge system and in `dwb_blockcrush_client`, published to Kafka via `bbc_publication`.
- Links to `fc_workflow_info` via `workflow_info_id`; that column is nullable.
- `feature_config_workflow_info` (C) is the synced/merged target. In the alpha BlockCrush database, trigger `trg_sync_feature_config_workflow_info_from_fc` syncs rows from `feature_config` (A) into `feature_config_workflow_info`.
- `feature_config.platform` is an enum column (`efeatureplatform`), cast to text when synced into `feature_config_workflow_info`.
- The merge system inherited "fake prefix" columns from A, e.g. `fc_origin` and `fc_origin_param`.
- In Block Crush, a PM-native story creative's `is_mock` flag is cleared only when the requirement reaches the '结束' workflow node, which makes it appear in the creative dictionary.

## Schema

- 54 columns; identical between `prd-blockcrush`, `prd-mahjongwonders`, and `dwb-blockcrush`, except `idea_label` is `text` instead of `text[]` in `prd-blockcrush` and `prd-mahjongwonders`.
- Stores `feature_key` and `idea_priority` (integer 1-10, often null); links to requirements in `pm_work_item` via `feature_config.feature_key = pm_work_item.extra->>'feature_key'`.
- In `prd_mjwd_client`, `idea_label` stores comma-separated strings (e.g. 'UI专项,交互') that must be split into `text[]` during migration.
- People columns in `prd_blockcrush_client`: creator (`create_avatar_name`, `create_avatar_id`), editor (`editer_avatar_name`, `editer_avatar_id`), reviewer (`reviewer_avatar_name`, `reviewer_avatar_id`, `reviewer_workcode`), and `functional_dev`. The proposer is not on this table.

## Constraints and indexes

- Unique constraint/index on `(platform, feature_desc)`.
- Unique index on `(platform, feature_id)`.
- Single-column indexes on `platform` and `feature_id`.
- No index on `editer_time`.

## Row counts and notable data

- Reported ~2265 rows, with platform-specific rows (IOS and GP) for the same `feature_id`.
- BlockCrush prod table has 331 rows.
- In `prd_blockcrush_client`, exactly 9 feature_config rows are linked to `fc_workflow_info` rows with `expected_first_launch_batch='GP33期'`.

## ORM / performance note

- The BBC feature_config model's `fc_param_rules` relationship uses `lazy='joined'`, forcing a LEFT OUTER JOIN on every query and amplifying result sets.

It serves the dashboard at 127.0.0.1:19019/ui, is launchd-managed, runs L1/L2/L3 memory pipeline with SQLite/WAL and goose migrations, stores embeddings in BLOB, and exposes HTTP APIs for onboarding, debug logs, health, and version.
memories.body:
# rmbd

## Identity & management
- rmbd is the local backend daemon / UI server for the RMB / rmb-desktop app, developed by the user from the rmb-desktop project at `/Users/liguanghui/Virginia/colinleefish/rmb-desktop`.
- Written in Go (CGO + SQLite); it is the daemon component of RMB and serves the dashboard UI. It also runs T3 bucket distillation/rollup and acts as the user's memory backend daemon.
- Managed by launchd as a LaunchAgent. Label appears as `me.remember.rmbd` (plist `com.remember.rmbd.plist`); also referenced as managed by the RMB tray/desktop app. Uses a single-instance lock on macOS.
- Desktop binary deployed at `~/.rmb/bin/rmbd-desktop`; the application bundle is distributed to users.
- Started via `make run-rmbd`, the desktop app, or the LaunchAgent. Built with `make build`; release flow uses `make app-build`, notarize, and `release-publish`.
- No CLI version command; HTTP exposes `/api/v1/version`. Does not auto-restart after an app upgrade; it must be restarted after embedding configuration changes.

## Networking & access
- Default listen: `127.0.0.1:19019`; also listens on `0.0.0.0:19019` as a Go binary. UI accessible at `http://127.0.0.1:19019/ui/`. Remote Mac instance exposes HTTP API at `10.254.24.7:19019`.
- Serves plain HTTP (not HTTPS), so Basic Auth credentials are transmitted in cleartext on a LAN.
- Auth: HTTP Basic Auth for UI and API; `/healthz` is unauthenticated when bound to `0.0.0.0`. Requires `USERNAME`/`PASSWORD` or `RMB_USERNAME`/`RMB_PASSWORD` env vars to start on `0.0.0.0`.
- Makes HTTPS requests to LLM API at `stargate.youxi123.com`.
- Hosts the PI agent and serves integration setup data.

## Data & migrations
- SQLite DB: `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/data/rmb.db`; WAL mode, foreign_keys enabled, uses `mattn/go-sqlite3`.
- DSN uses `_txlock=immediate` to avoid WAL `SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT` write contention.
- Schema migrations via goose, embedded SQL in `internal/db/migrations/`, run automatically on every daemon startup. Migrations are numbered `00001`–`00006`.
- Schema changes ship inside the new binary and apply automatically on daemon restart. Critical coupling: rmbd version ↔ schema version.
- After migrations, rmbd runs agent guide seeding on every startup.
- The rmb CLI talks to rmbd via HTTP API, not directly to the database.

## Memory pipeline
- Pipeline: L1 extract, L2 scene, L3 memory workers, plus an embed step; main entrypoint is `cmd/rmbd/main.go`. Go backend internal packages include `db`, `config`, `worker/scene`, and `cmd/rmbd`.
- L1/L2 worker concurrency defaults are 64 and 16; poll intervals: L1/L2 every 15s, L3 every 5min, embed every 30s.
- DB connection pool ceiling derives from L1/L2 concurrency config plus fixed workers and HTTP headroom.
- Uses vector embeddings for memory; stores memories in categories: profile, events, preferences, entities.
- Embeddings are stored in a BLOB column. Vector recall uses sqlite-vec's `vec_distance_cosine` scalar function on the existing embedding BLOB column, returning only top-k rows; does not use a `vec0` virtual table with `MATCH`.
- Exposes a `healthz` endpoint reporting status, SQLite version, and vector version.

## API / UI / development
- Onboarding endpoints: `GET /api/v1/onboarding/status` and `POST /api/v1/onboarding/complete`, backed by the `onboarding.complete` file in the rmb-desktop support directory. In normal deployments onboarding can be bypassed by creating that file or calling the POST endpoint.
- Integration tab mock setup mode is toggled via the `rmb.mockSetup` localStorage key or `npm run dev:mock-setup` in webui; setup previews are computed by built-in per-agent merge logic, not dynamic detection. rmbd is used for real API testing when the mock is disabled.
- Embeds the WebUI frontend built from `webui/dist` into `internal/http/static/web/`.
- Code-signing keychain password is only needed for publishing signed DMG and GitHub releases, not local deployment.
- When run as a bundle, logs are discarded and there is no export diagnostics path.

## Observability / debugging
- Debug logging endpoint: `GET /api/v1/debug/logs`, backed by a 2000-line ring buffer, and tees all slog output to stderr.
- Debug endpoints: `/debug/workers`, `/debug/in-flight`, `/debug/pipeline/stuck`, and `browse/sessions/{key}`; `pipeline_state.t2_last_error` holds the actual L2 error text in SQLite.
- Known limitations: `?worker=l2` log filter is broken because L2 logs use `session_id` instead of `worker`; no per-call LLM tracing (URL, status, latency, response size not logged); `persist.scenes` failures are not logged because dry-run skips DB writes.

memories.body:
# RMB Desktop (rmb-desktop)

## Identity
- **Project/display name:** RMB Desktop (`rmb-desktop`); repo `github.com/colinleefish/rmb-desktop`; local checkout `/Users/liguanghui/Virginia/colinleefish/rmb-desktop`.
- Personal product from re-mem-ber.me, license TBD; Herdr workspace w7 corresponds to this project. Actively developed/tested by the user.
- Tauri v1 Rust tray/menubar app + Go backend; SQLite + sqlite-vec. Bundle id `me.remember.rmb`, installed at `/Applications/RMB Desktop.app` (earlier builds at `/Applications/rmb.app`). macOS `aarch64`, signed/notarized, Developer ID Application: GUANGHUI LI (N4YPJBRBN4); runs with Hardened Runtime, not sandboxed, LSUIElement.
- Desktop GUI version of the RMB product, aligned with the main `rmb` repository; includes bundled CLI `rmb` and daemon `rmbd`; also builds `rmbd`.
- Tool for AI-agent onboarding with a setup flow for installing agents.

## Architecture / Storage
- Menubar/tray app (`RMB.app`) plus bundled CLI (`rmb`) and daemon (`rmbd`). First-run bootstrap copies bundled binaries into `~/.rmb/bin/` (names observed: `rmb`, `rmb-app`, `rmbd-desktop`) and installs a LaunchAgent for `rmbd`; on startup it re-syncs newer bundled binaries.
- Daemon `rmbd` serves HTTP API on `127.0.0.1:19019`; Go codebase (e.g. `cmd/rmbd/main.go`, `internal/httpserver`, `internal/worker/scene`, `internal/db`). A deployed/remote debug instance is at `10.254.24.7:19019`.
- Local SQLite database: `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/data/rmb.db`, WAL mode, foreign keys enabled; config at `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/config.yaml` (also holds API keys). This is the user's real database used by the pipeline daemon; direct SQL into memories is possible but fragile.
- Local-first memory pipeline: full conversations distilled via L0–L1–L2–L3 pyramid (turns, atoms, scenes, memories) using `rmb://` URIs; sessions processed through t1/t2/t3 stages via l1/l2/l3 workers plus an embed worker, backed by SQLite `pipeline_state`.
- Memory categories: profile, entities, preferences, events, corrections, recall stats (also `recall_stats` table keyed by URI). Schema includes `scenes` and FTS5 virtual table `scenes_fts` (content='scenes', tokenize='unicode61'), populated by the L2 stage; `pipeline_state` has `l1/l2/l3_last_error` and `l1/l2/l3_started_at` columns.
- L1, L2, and embed workers report cycle, per-session step, and backpressure info to an in-memory registry; L2 scene worker at `internal/worker/scene/worker.go` manages `scenes`/`scenes_fts` writes. Daemon rebuilds `scenes_fts` on startup but only logs a warning if rebuild fails.
- DB migrations: goose migrations run automatically on `rmbd` start with SQL embedded in the binary; end users never run migration scripts manually. Stop → migrate → restart orchestration is not yet built. `scripts/backfill-from-remote.py` is a data-migration script for importing sessions from remote rmb instances, not a schema migration.

## Web UI / Settings
- Web UI source in `webui/` (Vite build), embedded via `go:embed` from `webui/dist`; regenerate with `make webui-build`; never hand-edit embedded/generated assets. `internal/http/static/web/` is generated output only. WebUI dev server: `npm run dev:mock-setup`.
- Favicon is a purple gradient SVG at `ui/public/favicon.svg`; sidebar uses a Lucide Brain icon as placeholder brand mark.
- Settings page tabs: **General**, **Models**, **Advanced**; **Integrations** is a top-level sidebar item. Supports OpenAI-compatible API format for LLM and embedding providers; config page has LLM and embedding API key fields. General settings include display language, distillation database path, and config file collection address.
- Integrations: **Cursor**, **Claude Code**, **Codex**, **OpenCode**, **Pi**. Current known issue: it writes shell hooks for OpenCode and Pi, which is incorrect for those agents.
- Launch-at-login setting stored in config.yaml under `launch_at_login`; LaunchAgent at `~/Library/LaunchAgents/me.remember.rmb.plist`.
- Onboarding first-run gate uses `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/onboarding.complete` (JSON with `completed_at` and `skipped_agents`); API endpoints `GET /api/v1/onboarding/status`, `POST /api/v1/onboarding/complete`, `POST /api/v1/onboarding/reset`.

## Distribution / Sync / Privacy
- Current packaging: signed/notarized aarch64 macOS DMG via `make app-build` and `finish-dmg.sh`; planned: Windows MSI/EXE, Linux AppImage/DEB. Distributed through GitHub Releases and Cloudflare R2 at `releases.re-mem-ber.me`.
- Tauri updater disabled (`updater.active: false`). Sync path: dual-submit to `rmb.colinleefish.com`; deferred sync at `sync.re-mem-ber.me`. Explicitly rejects iCloud/Dropbox sync due to corruption risk.
- Does not report installs or heartbeats; stores data locally. (No server-side telemetry reported.)

## HTTP / Debug
- `GET /healthz` returns ok when the DB opens (migrations passed). `GET /api/v1/version` reports the app version, not the DB schema version. Debug API routes are unauthenticated, as is the rest of desktop `rmbd`.
- Debug endpoints under `/debug/` cover workers, in-flight tasks, backpressure, logs, SQLite, pipeline stuck/unstick/requeue, LLM build-scenes, and pipeline dry-run; also exposed under `/api/v1/debug/*`. Tauri config sets `exceptionDomain` to an empty string, allowing cleartext HTTP.

## Version history / Known issues
- Version history observed: 0.1.1, 0.1.2, 0.1.9, 0.1.16 (as of Aug 2026), 0.1.18, and 0.1.19 (latest observed). Version 0.1.19 logs every LLM request to `/api/v1/debug/logs` with fields: `op`, `attempt`, `model`, `host`, `status`, `latency_ms`, `req_bytes`, `resp_bytes`, `err`.
- 0.1.19 includes 0.1.18 fixes: `llm.timeout` default 45s, T2 atom trim, and real error text in logs.
- Known issue (0.1.19): a 2KB LLM truncation bug caused `unexpected end of JSON input` errors in the L2 pipeline.
- Known issue: L2 pipeline can get stuck when sessions remain in `running` status after crashes or restarts, blocking the worker.
- As of 2026-08-14: `scenes` table was empty and `scenes_fts` index appeared missing or corrupted (rebuild failed with `no such table` while the app logged `malformed`), suspected cause of L2 persist failures. Also as of 2026-08-14 the README did not document automatic DB migrations and the Makefile advertised a `make migrate` target that does not exist.
- Tested on the "quick whale" VM. Initial scaffolding includes menu bar tray with **Start/Stop rmbd** and **Open Dashboard**. User is actively working on rmb-desktop testing.

## Pi (AI agent)

- Pi is a minimal terminal AI agent built with TypeScript and an extensions-based architecture.
- It captures chat via extensions and lifecycle events; it has **no shell hook system** / no shell hooks.
- Pi is an AI agent tool that the **rmb-desktop** project integrates with.
- Integration with the rmb platform is done via an extension at `~/.pi/agent/extensions/rmb-hook.ts`.
- The user uses pi for **blind-testing rmb skills**.

## Configuration and behavior

- Provider credentials are stored in `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` (user's PI configuration).
- Pi generates its own UUID v7 session IDs, stored in the session file header.
- Its message queue delivers: steering messages (Enter) after the current turn's tool calls, and follow-up messages (Alt+Enter) after all work.
- This behavior is configurable via `steeringMode` and `followUpMode`.
- Pi discovers skills from `~/.agents/skills` (e.g. the herdr and cmux skills).

## Agent ecosystem

- Pi is an agent kind integrated with **Herdr** (installed as v8).
- Available agent kinds alongside pi include: claude, codex, gemini, and cursor.

memories.body:
# RMB (Recall Memory Bank)

## Identity
- RMB/rmb is the user's personal long-term memory system for AI-agent conversations and coding agents; a product built and owned by the user.
- Formerly named mem9; previous names include mem-colinleefish-com, mem-colinleefish, and mypast.
- GitHub repo: github.com/colinleefish/rmb; local source: /Users/liguanghui/Virginia/colinleefish/rmb.
- Production: https://rmb.colinleefish.com (SSH root@rmb.colinleefish.com); deployed with Docker only (make deploy), not Vercel.
- Docker image: registry.cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/colinleefish/rmb, tag :main; images also tagged by git commit SHA. Production config at /opt/rmb/.env; database rmb_db; app connects as rmb_user.
- Production runtime is a minimal bundle at /app/rmb (docker-compose.yml, .env, config/Caddyfile), no git checkout on the server; deploy.sh only runs git pull and docker compose pull/up; .env is gitignored.
- Also deployed as two separate instances on 182.92.114.13, ports 18080 and 18081; also deployed on the remote rmb-desktop host, including the T2 scene-building pipeline.
- Targets macOS (arm64) and Windows (x64); Linux may come later. Distributed as a macOS .dmg via re-mem-ber.me and GitHub Releases; install.sh downloads binaries from GitHub Releases. The Docker image contains a single binary and runs /rmb serve.
- Self-hosted, single-owner, and URI-transparent: entities at rmb://entities/<slug>, skills at rmb://skills/<name>, agent instructions at rmb://agent.

## Credentials & databases
- Remote HTTP basic auth: username rmb, password sVf3^n5ht.
- Server Postgres: rmb_db at 127.0.0.1:5432, user rmb_user, password 0c2791d39900292afc7948f520bc0aa3; default DSN uses sslmode=disable.
- PBP Postgres (co-hosted): database pbp_db, user pbp_user_rw, 15-table schema, reachable at rmb.colinleefish.com:5432; remote connections require SSL using a wildcard *.colinleefish.com certificate auto-renewed weekly via cron.
- Production server has a single CPU core; database is Postgres 18.3 with pgvector 0.8.2; migrations use goose.
- Production has approximately 1,258 scenes across 314 sessions.

## Data & entities
- System data associates 刘欣欣 with system ID 62 and workcode 001971 (also present in mock data).

## Components & local paths
- CLI binary: ~/.rmb/bin/rmb (not on PATH by default); a stable, writable absolute path for agent hooks. Other binaries: ~/.rmb/bin/rmb-app; rmbd and rmbd-desktop sidecars are also stored in ~/.rmb/bin; ~/.rmb also contains skills cache and rmb-app.lock.
- Desktop backend: local SQLite at 127.0.0.1:19019; desktop web UI at http://127.0.0.1:19019/ui/; desktop DB at ~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/data/rmb.db.
- Real daemon listens on 19019; test daemon on 127.0.0.1:19097. Product assumes one daemon per DB file; two daemons on the same DB can create duplicate atoms.
- Config: ~/.rmb/config.yaml points to the production server. Resolution order: RMB_CONFIG env, RMB_CONF env, ~/.rmb.conf, then ~/.rmb/config.yaml; paths are resolved via $HOME. In the repo, .env sets RMB_CONFIG=.env, overriding ~/.rmb.conf when run from the repo directory. An empty RMB_URL env var can make the CLI appear to ignore its config.
- macOS app: menu bar app with no Dock icon at /Applications/rmb.app; bundle ID me.remember.rmb; dashboard opens in the browser; single-instance lock; managed via LaunchAgents me.remember.rmb and me.remember.rmbd. RMB Desktop is codesigned with Developer ID Application certificate GUANGHUI LI (N4YPJBRBN4); the Windows installer is unsigned.
- Tray app is Tauri (Rust): polls GET /healthz every 5 seconds, showing 🟢 RMB is running when healthy and Starting… when not; auto-restarts rmbd every 5 seconds when health checks fail.
- Start-on-login is implemented in the rmbd daemon's internal/launchatlogin package (LaunchAgent me.remember.rmb.login), independent of Tauri/systray; not supported on Windows.
- Bootstrap copies the sidecar from the bundle to ~/.rmb/bin/ on each startup. No auto-update (Tauri updater inactive); updates are manual via DMG/GitHub Release.
- Server /healthz returns the git commit SHA; local /healthz on 127.0.0.1:19019 does not return the app version. CLI version prints rmb dev, not a real semver.
- Desktop app seeds rmb://agent on first run and prints the profile when run with no arguments, matching the server version.

## Architecture & data model
- Client-server: the CLI is a pure HTTP API client that never touches the DB; server owns storage and processing. Backend is Go (Gin, GORM, goose migrations, PostgreSQL/pgvector); frontend is React/Next.js. Desktop backend uses local SQLite (mattn/go-sqlite3, goose, external-content FTS5 tables scenes_fts/atoms_fts/memories_fts with triggers, sqlite-vec, backpressure, FIFO extract, rollup concurrency).
- internal/setup provides detect, preview, and apply functions for agent integration. Server exposes GET /api/v1/browse/...; local RMB Desktop exposes POST /api/v1/sessions/{key}/upload.
- Memory pyramid T0-T3: T0 raw session turns; T1 atoms (extract); T2 scenes (session-local narrative segments; a session can have multiple scenes); T3 cross-session memories.
- T1 extracts atoms from session turns in batches of up to 8 turns per LLM call, mapping 0-based source_turn_indices to source_turn_ids; atoms store provenance in a source_turn_ids uuid array (~4% of atoms cite multiple source turns). Atoms table has Category (profile/preferences/entities/events) and Topic (scene_name · slug) columns; UUID primary key after migration 00017; uri column removed.
- T2 builds scenes by grouping atoms by scene_name and writes narrative rows; T2 overwrites the same scene row on rebuild, with no version history.
- T3 distills memories; the T3 worker polls every 5 minutes, loading all atoms across sessions into shared buckets (rmb://profile, rmb://entities/..., rmb://preferences/...).
- Unified 4-category taxonomy at both T1 and T3: profile / preferences / entities / events.
- URI scheme: profile, entities/<slug>, preferences/<slug>, events/<slug>, scenes/<uuid>, atoms/<uuid>, skills/<slug>, and rmb://agent.
- Scene URIs are deterministically derived from session_id and display_name via UUIDv5; display_name is a short human-readable title, not the primary search field (abstract is embedded). No validation that scene abstract is shorter than body; design expects abstract ~100 tokens with fuller body.
- Summaries are written at three tiers: sessions.abstract, scenes.abstract/body, memories.abstract/body. Legacy sessions.overview_text was retired in migration 00010.
- Data model is a directed graph: turns -> atoms -> scenes -> memories; append-first, versioned consolidation.
- Memories are stored in a versioned, append-only memories table keyed by URI, with one active row per URI; only active memories (superseded_at IS NULL) are embedded and used in recall. The memories table stores entity records and supports cname aliases for canonical merging; a flat-star invariant (no chains) is enforced at the memories table, with service-layer enforcement future work.
- Events are immutable and first-write-wins by URI.
- Corrections are stored in a separate append-only table and synced by id; human corrections outrank machine-distilled facts; they are additive overlays with newest-wins conflict resolution and no hard-delete; versioning uses superseded_at; facts can be ported via the corrections API.
- Aliases: aliases and alias_candidates tables exist; an alias-suggestion worker proposes aliases for duplicate preferences/entities (default cosine similarity floor 0.82) and is pair-centric; alias/canonical mode resolves duplicate identity by folding aliases into a canonical entity; the recall path does not yet resolve aliases. A separate entity aliases registry was dropped in migration 00012.
- Sessions have scope_key, title, and embedding columns (optional client-supplied metadata); the 1024-dim session-abstract embedding is planned but not yet populated, and the embed worker does not fill sessions.abstract.
- Default concurrency limits: L2 max 16, L1 max 64; default llm.timeout is 45s. The CLI is Go with a hand-rolled switch-based argument parser (no Cobra). The API uses snake_case JSON with server-side pagination for sessions, pipeline, and corrections.

## Recall, embeddings & skills
- Recall is hybrid vector + FTS + RRF; APIs are find (vector) and search (hybrid vector + FTS). Retrieval defaults to flat RRF; pyramid drill-down is manual and on-demand.
- pgvector vector(1024) columns with HNSW indexes for cosine similarity cover memories, scenes, and atoms.
- Embedding defaults: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small with 1024 dimensions; the dimension cannot be changed after it is set (changing would require re-embedding all memories). rmb sends the configured dimension without prior validation but requires the returned vector length to match exactly; all vectors must share the same fixed length. The production memory server has used DeepSeek (api.deepseek.com, model deepseek-v4-flash) for LLM calls and doubao-embedding-vision for embeddings.
- Recall stats are stored in a recall_stats table keyed by URI (migration 00023_recall_stats.sql), recorded server-side via rmb search/cat/meta.
- Skills are normalized to rmb://skills/<slug>, versioned by bundle_sha256, and synced via rmb skill pull; the CLI can upload skills to rmb://skills/. The server CLI provides 20+ skills including JumpServer and humanizer; known skills also include ascii-diagram.
- scripts/visualize_embeddings.py projects memory embeddings to 2D via UMAP and outputs Plotly HTML.

## Capture & agent integrations
- Captures memory via agent hooks with zero SDK in the agent; internal/hook parses agent output and uploads turns to the server. A hook mechanism uses rmb-hook-dual to call rmb-desktop. Hook integrations exist for Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi; sessions are captured from all five.
- Cursor integration requires two artifacts: hooks.json and user rules. Claude Code integration requires settings.json and a recall file. Configuration changes require a preview-before-apply workflow.
- Cursor hook integration merges rmb hook-submit into the hooks.stop array of ~/.cursor/hooks.json, modifying only hooks.stop and preserving other hook events/entries; hook_status: configured is detected only when hooks.stop contains rmb hook-submit; it uses ./hooks/audit.sh and adds timeout: 15 when missing; the Cursor hook skips aborted turns, so only completed turns are uploaded.
- Codex is supported as a hook source; the user's Codex and Cursor Stop-event hooks run rmb hook-submit --source=codex. The server contains hook-submit parsers for Codex, OpenCode, and Pi.
- Working integrations exist for OpenCode and Pi; their setup is guided and requires manual confirmation and apply (not fully automatic). Web UI has integration pages for Cursor, OpenCode, and Pi.
- The CLI manages agent recall instructions (rmb://agent) for Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi; called with no arguments it injects the agent guide into the agent's context at session start.
- The agent guide is embedded as agent_guide.md and mirrored into the memories database by UpsertAgentGuide; it is treated as system docs, not user memory, and excluded from browse counts and memory category overviews. The Go agent memory is served from the bundled agent_guide.md rather than a database row. On fresh databases, migration 00006 inserts rmb://agent at version 1 and UpsertAgentGuide immediately supersedes it to version 2, so the version counter is permanently off by one. Clients fetch the guide through the server's inspect cat endpoint.
- Recall-rule configuration is detected when both # RMB memory and ALWAYS RUN `rmb` cli are present; old <!-- rmb:recall:start/end --> markers remain compatible. The user has an rmb CLI integration that provides recall rules (rmb:recall).

## UI & product details
- Web UI is React/Next.js, served under /ui (basePath /ui); the Go server serves an embedded static build from internal/http/static/web/ (including _next/). It has a skill list page, memories/scenes tables, a hooks area, plus RecallRuleCopy UI component and rmb-ui. Web UI source lives at rmb-desktop/webui.
- The local desktop profile is in Chinese and sparse; the server profile is in English and detailed.
- Docs site is VitePress with bilingual English and Chinese content under docs/concept and docs/zh/concept.

## Sync & deployment limits
- No one-click server-to-desktop migration; no bulk PUT for profile/entities/preferences/events; built-in cross-device sync is a deferred paid feature (sync.re-mem-ber.me); syncing rmb.db via iCloud/Dropbox is planned as unsafe; pg_dump from the server will not load into desktop because they use different DB engines.
- Cross-instance behavior uses client-to-remote HTTP API; there is currently no BitTorrent/DHT code in the stack.
- Sessions and turns are synced by session_key and turn id; session turn_count is computed at read time, not stored on the session row; server and desktop instances share session UUIDs; uploads require UUID session IDs and are limited to 32 MiB; server default binding is 127.0.0.1:8080, and public binds require auth.
- Sync resolves conflicts by syncing rows by id, unioning provenance, and re-distilling. Without an app update, backfill preserves session keys, message content, turn order, and the re-distilled memories/skills path, but not original turn timestamps or bit-identical old T3 text; old rmb builds ignore unknown JSON fields, so sending started_at is harmless.
- The rmb server co-hosts the pbp stock sync project: app at /app/pbp running sync in Docker; its sync server runs the data ingestion pipeline (stock daily, fund daily, valuation, financials) and checkpoints progress in sync.sync_state; the user can SSH in and run sync, potentially bypassing the THS page-6 login wall.

## Known issues & limitations
- Lacks a dedicated procedural memory track (skills/cases) separate from its skills registry; has a single namespace and is not multi-tenant. Not evaluated on the MemoryAgentBench benchmark.
- scenes_fts can corrupt under concurrent L2 worker writes: persistScenes deletes the FTS entry after the content upsert and even on first-time scene creation, causing SQLITE_CORRUPT (database disk image is malformed) on an otherwise healthy database. The user's rmb.db (under ~/Downloads) was corrupted with 0 scenes and 45 zombie running sessions before the fix was applied.
- TestWritePlist is environment-dependent: it fails when /Applications/RMB Desktop.app exists on the host, making make test red on developer machines with the app installed.
- HTTP body handling by version: v0.1.18 streamed response bodies; v0.1.19 read through a 2 KiB LimitReader; v0.1.20 reads full bodies while capping error snippets at 2 KiB.
- Has Go unit tests but lacks HTTP handler, UI, and integration tests.
- Additional limitations: scenes update without version history; recall does not yet resolve aliases; session abstract embeddings are not yet populated; the agent-guide version counter is off by one.

## Dated record
- 2026-07-25: rmb lacked a knowledge base, memory promotion, an entity relationship graph, and multi-tenant sharing — gaps identified against ContextDB.
- 2026-08-14: rmb migrations were at version 9.

memories.body:
# jump-hs99-vip

- **Bastion**: JumpServer at `jump.hs99.vip` (https://jump.hs99.vip), used to list assets and SSH into managed hosts.
- **Access**: REST API plus KoKo SSH gateway on **port 2222**. SSH authentication uses username `JMS-<token_id>` and password `<token_value>`.
- **Credentials**: Stored at `~/.hungrystudio/jump-hs99-vip`.
- **Skill**: Operator skill registered in rmb as `rmb://skills/jump-hs99-vip`; canonical v7 at `~/.rmb/skills/jump-hs99-vip`; user-facing copy at `~/.claude/skills/jump-hs99-vip/SKILL.md` (also `/Users/liguanghui/.claude/skills/jump-hs99-vip`); synced via rmb CLI. Tagged `work`; used for listing hosts and running SSH commands.

## SSH sessions
- Each SSH session requires a **fresh connection token**; tokens are single-use and expire in about 5 minutes.
- Reusing a token across sessions fails with `Permission denied`.
- **SCP/SFTP do not work** through the KoKo gateway; file transfers use `tar over SSH`.
- Default account on JumpServer assets: `osadmin`.

## PostgreSQL / database access
- PostgreSQL is supported as a first-class asset type (`postgresql` database platform).
- The connection-token API accepts `protocol=postgresql` and returns `201 Created` for `db_client`, `db_guide`, `native_db`, and `web_cli`.
- However, **XPACK enterprise license is disabled** (`XPACK_LICENSE_IS_VALID: False`), so native DB-client proxy and the `chen` component are unavailable.
- KoKo SSH gateway rejects database connection tokens.
- All native DB proxy ports are closed on the public IP (5432, 54320, 33060, 30001, 8443, 8080); only port 2222 is exposed.
- `TERMINAL_OMNIDB_ENABLED` is true, so the in-browser Web SQL terminal (**OmniDB**) works for PostgreSQL assets.

## Managed hosts
- Used to reach backend/dev hosts behind the bastion, including `aliyun-perf-bbc`, `starlink-dev-all-in-one`, Starlink infrastructure hosts, and Airflow hosts.

memories.abstract: RMB Desktop (rmb-desktop) is a Tauri/Go macOS menu-bar agent-memory app at github.com/colinleefish/rmb-desktop, with local rmbd daemon on 127.0.0.1:19019, SQLite WAL + L0-L3 pipeline, signed DMG releases, currently v0.1.19; known 2026-08-14 scenes_fts issue.
memories.body:
# Identity and distribution

- RMB Desktop (rmb-desktop / RMB-Desktop) is a Tauri-based macOS desktop app, project at github.com/colinleefish/rmb-desktop, local path /Users/liguanghui/Virginia/colinleefish/rmb-desktop. Product name shown as RMB Desktop; menu-bar app via LSUIElement; bundle ID me.remember.rmb; installed at /Applications/RMB Desktop.app. Herdr workspace w7 corresponds.
- Latest known version in these facts: 0.1.19 (as of 2026-08-14). Earlier observed versions include 0.1.0, 0.1.1, 0.1.2, 0.1.9, and v0.1.16. Personal product, license TBD.
- Distributed as signed/notarized aarch64 DMG via GitHub Releases and Cloudflare R2 at releases.re-mem-ber.me. Codesigned with Developer ID Application: GUANGHUI LI (N4YPJBRBN4); not sandboxed; Hardened Runtime; ATS exceptionDomain is empty string, allowing cleartext HTTP.
- Planned targets: DMG for macOS, MSI/EXE for Windows, AppImage/DEB for Linux. Tauri updater disabled (`updater.active: false`). Packaged via `make app-build` and `finish-dmg.sh`.

# Architecture and runtime

- Stack: Go + Rust/Tauri; Tauri v1 tray shell with tray menu Start/Stop rmbd and Open Dashboard; shell layer is tray/menu only, no web UI in the shell layer. Go implements rmb system: rmbd daemon (cmd/rmbd/main.go) and HTTP server (internal/httpserver). SQLite + sqlite-vec.
- Bundles local CLI `rmb`, daemon `rmbd-desktop`, and Tauri app `RMB.app`. Daemon listens on 127.0.0.1:19019; endpoint /healthz returns ok when the database opens (migrations passed); indicates SQLite and vector status.
- Sidecar binaries are synced to ~/.rmb/bin/ if newer; reported names include ~/.rmb/bin/rmb (CLI), ~/.rmb/bin/rmb-app, and ~/.rmb/bin/rmbd-desktop (daemon). First-run bootstrap plans to install a LaunchAgent for rmbd.
- Config file: ~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/config.yaml (LLM and embedding API keys, launch_at_login). SQLite database: ~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/data/rmb.db, WAL mode and foreign keys enabled. LaunchAgent: ~/Library/LaunchAgents/me.remember.rmb.plist. Onboarding marker: ~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/onboarding.complete (JSON with completed_at and skipped_agents), exposed via GET /api/v1/onboarding/status, POST /api/v1/onboarding/complete, POST /api/v1/onboarding/reset.
- Migrations run automatically via goose on rmbd start; migration SQL embedded in binary; end users never run migration scripts manually. stop->migrate->restart orchestration is not yet built. Direct SQL into the DB is possible but fragile.

# Memory pipeline and integrations

- Purpose: durable agent-memory desktop app. Captures full conversations and distills them through an L0-L1-L2-L3 pyramid (turns, atoms, scenes, memories) addressed by rmb:// URIs. Memory model includes profile, entities, preferences, events, corrections, and recall_stats table keyed by URI.
- Pipeline processes sessions through t1/t2/t3 stages via l1/l2/l3 workers plus an embed worker, backed by SQLite pipeline_state table. L1/L2/embed workers report cycle, per-session step, and backpressure info to an in-memory registry.
- Supports five AI agents: Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi. Integrations for Cursor, Claude Code, Codex; currently writes shell hooks for OpenCode and Pi, which is incorrect for those agents.
- Local-first storage: stores local conversation data locally; does not report installs or heartbeats; supports dual-submit to hosted endpoint rmb.colinleefish.com and deferred sync at sync.re-mem-ber.me. Explicitly rejects iCloud or Dropbox sync due to corruption risk.

# Web UI and settings

- Web UI source of truth is in webui/; dev server starts with `npm run dev:mock-setup`. Vite-built web UI is embedded via go:embed with assets copied from webui/dist by `make webui-build`. internal/http/static/web/ is generated output only and must not be hand-edited.
- Sidebar uses a Lucide Brain icon as a placeholder brand mark. Favicon is a purple gradient SVG at ui/public/favicon.svg.
- Settings page has tabs General, Models, and Advanced; Integrations is a top-level sidebar item. General settings include display language, distillation database path, and config file collection address. Supports OpenAI-compatible API format for LLM and embedding providers.

# API and schema details

- HTTP API at 127.0.0.1:19019; a remote debug instance is also reachable at 10.254.24.7:19019. Routes are unauthenticated. /api/v1/version reports app version but not DB schema version.
- Debug endpoints are exposed under /api/v1/debug/* (also described as /debug/*), covering workers, in-flight tasks, backpressure, logs, SQLite, pipeline stuck/unstick/requeue, LLM build-scenes, and pipeline dry-run.
- rmb-desktop 0.1.19 logs every LLM request to /api/v1/debug/logs with fields op, attempt, model, host, status, latency_ms, req_bytes, resp_bytes, and err.
- DB schema includes scenes table and an FTS5 external-content index scenes_fts (content='scenes', tokenize='unicode61'). pipeline_state table has l1/l2/l3_last_error and l1/l2/l3_started_at.
- L2 scene worker at internal/worker/scene/worker.go manages scenes and scenes_fts writes. On startup, rmbd rebuilds scenes_fts but only logs a warning if the rebuild fails.
- scripts/backfill-from-remote.py is a data-migration script for importing sessions from remote rmb instances, not a schema migration.

# Release notes and known issues

- rmb-desktop 0.1.19 includes 0.1.18 fixes: llm.timeout default 45s, T2 atom trim, and real error text in logs.
- rmb-desktop 0.1.19 had a 2KB LLM truncation bug that caused 'unexpected end of JSON input' errors in the L2 pipeline.
- RMB Desktop's L2 pipeline can get stuck when sessions remain in 'running' status after crashes or restarts, blocking the worker.

# Dated observations (2026-08-14)

- RMB Desktop README did not document automatic DB migrations, and the Makefile advertised a `make migrate` target that did not exist.
- rmb-desktop's scenes table was empty and scenes_fts appeared missing or corrupted: rebuild failed with 'no such table' while the app logged 'malformed'; this was suspected to be the cause of L2 persist failures.

memories.abstract: starlink-deployments-dev is the Helmfile-based dev deployment repo for starlink targeting ack-starlink-dev, with environments dev-shared-services, lby-blockcrush, dwb-blockblast, dev-feworkgql, and blockcrush/cat; uses versions.yaml for image tags, SOPS secrets, env-values.yaml, and follows starorigin-deployments conventions.
memories.body:
# starlink-deployments-dev

- Dev deployment manifests repository for the starlink project, targeting `ack-starlink-dev`.
- Helmfile-based deployment repo with a `main` branch; follows the Helmfile/Go-template deployment pattern established in `starorigin-deployments`.
- Contains per-game/per-env folders with helmfile and service configs.
- Environments include:
  - `dev-shared-services` (contains the atomkit service config; route files under `envs/dev-shared-services/routes`)
  - `lby-blockcrush`
  - `dwb-blockblast`
  - `dev-feworkgql`
  - `blockcrush/cat`; a `cat-blockcrush` environment config exists with namespace `starlink-cat-blockcrush`.

## Configuration pattern
- `env-values.yaml` controls which services are enabled, which chart versions are used, and the target namespace.
- Helmfile values merge in the order: `deploy.yaml`, `app.yaml`, inline `image.tag`, then `secrets.enc.yaml`; later values override earlier ones.
- Environment manifests (`envs/<env>/app.yaml`) and service configs (`services/<svc>/config/app.yaml`) are both named `app.yaml`, creating a naming collision.
- Image tags are decoupled from Helmfile templates by reading `versions.yaml` at render time with `readFile` and `fromYaml`.
- Deploys are done by Jenkins updating the image tag in `versions.yaml`; rollback is a git revert of that `versions.yaml` change.
- Sensitive configuration is stored in SOPS-encrypted `secrets.enc.yaml` files.
