memories.body:
# rmbd

## Identity
- rmbd is the Go backend daemon and local UI server for RMB / rmb-desktop; user-developed project at `/Users/liguanghui/Virginia/colinleefish/rmb-desktop`.
- Version 0.1.20; installed at `~/.rmb/bin/rmbd-desktop`; built with CGO_ENABLED=1 and `sqlite_fts5` tag; application bundle distributed to users; built with `make build` / `make app-build`, started with `make run-rmbd` or desktop/tray app.
- Managed by macOS launchd as LaunchAgent label `me.remember.rmbd` with single-instance lock; can be restarted via RMB Desktop; must be restarted after embedding configuration changes.
- No version command; does not auto-restart after app upgrade; logs discarded when run as bundle; no export diagnostics path.

## HTTP / service roles
- Listens on `127.0.0.1:19019` by default (also observed on `0.0.0.0:19019`; remote Mac instance at `10.254.24.7:19019`); web UI at `http://127.0.0.1:19019/ui/`.
- Exposes `healthz` (status, SQLite version, vector version), `/api/v1/version`, `/api/v1/onboarding/status`, `/api/v1/onboarding/complete`.
- Hosts PI agent and serves integration setup data; computes setup previews with built-in merge logic per agent, not dynamic detection; real API testing uses rmbd as backend when mock disabled.
- Onboarding backed by `onboarding.complete` file in rmb-desktop support dir; bypass by creating file or calling complete endpoint.
- rmb CLI talks to rmbd via HTTP API, not directly to database.

## Auth/network
- HTTP Basic Auth for UI/API; `/healthz` unauthenticated when bound to `0.0.0.0`; plain HTTP means cleartext credentials on LAN.
- Starting on `0.0.0.0` requires `USERNAME`/`PASSWORD` or `RMB_USERNAME`/`RMB_PASSWORD` environment variables.
- Makes HTTPS requests to LLM API at `stargate.youxi123.com`.

## Data and storage
- SQLite database at `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/data/rmb.db`; WAL mode, `foreign_keys` enabled, `mattn/go-sqlite3`, `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` / `_txlock=immediate` to avoid WAL `SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT`.
- Embedded WebUI built from `webui/dist` into `internal/http/static/web/`.
- Goose migrations `00001`–`00006` with embedded SQL in `internal/db/migrations/`, run automatically on every startup; schema changes ship inside new rmbd binary and apply on daemon restart; critical coupling rmbd version ↔ schema version.
- After migrations, agent guide seeding runs every startup.
- Memories stored in categories: profile, events, preferences, entities; uses vector embeddings. Embeddings stored as BLOB column; vector recall uses sqlite-vec `vec_distance_cosine` on the existing BLOB and returns top-k rows; does not use a `vec0` virtual table with `MATCH`.
- Dynamic scene chunking; T3 bucket distillation/rollup.

## Pipeline/architecture
- Main entrypoint `cmd/rmbd/main.go`; internal packages `db`, `config`, `worker/scene`, `cmd/rmbd`.
- Memory pipeline: L1 extract, L2 scene, L3 memory workers plus embed step.
- Defaults L1=64, L2=16; poll intervals L1/L2 every 15s, L3 every 5min, embed every 30s.
- DB connection pool ceiling derived from L1/L2 concurrency config + fixed workers + HTTP headroom.

## Debugging endpoints / known issues
- `GET /api/v1/debug/logs` backed by 2000-line ring buffer; tees all slog output to stderr.
- Exposes `/debug/workers`, `/debug/in-flight`, `/debug/pipeline/stuck`, and `browse/sessions/{key}`; `pipeline_state.t2_last_error` holds the actual L2 error text in SQLite.
- Known issues: `?worker=l2` log filter broken because L2 logs use `session_id` instead of `worker`; no LLM request tracing (no per-call URL, status code, latency, or response size); does not log `persist.scenes` failures because dry-run skips DB writes.

## Dev/release operational notes
- Run with `make run-rmbd`.
- Release: `make app-build`, notarize, `release-publish`; code-signing keychain password needed only for signed DMG/GitHub release publishing, not local deployment.
- Integration mock setup toggled by `rmb.mockSetup` localStorage or `npm run dev:mock-setup` in webui.

memories.body:
# Jenkins

Jenkins is the CI/CD tool the user manages/uses at HungryStudio (also a common MCP tool). It is part of the user's infrastructure stack and is used to build and deploy the BBC service.

## Instances

- `archteam-starfamily-jenkins-master` at `10.100.27.205`: internal network, accessed via JumpServer; g7/hfg7 ECS; host has PostgreSQL 16.14 tools. Runs BBC deploy jobs, hosts Starlink pipeline scripts including `lowcodegql-build`, and is used for database restoration/sync tasks.
- `devops-jenkins.hs99.vip` (`https://devops-jenkins.hs99.vip`; instance name `uc-devops-jenkins`; Rocky Linux 9.7, x86_64; local agent). Used for CI/CD, toolhub deployments, StarOrigin 419 jobs under `starorigin419`, Starlink/ding jobs, Starlink BBC builds, and deploy/db-migrator playbooks. Supports Linux, Windows, iOS agents. Jobs are organized under folders such as `starorigin-mcps`.
- BlockBlast PRD uses multiple Jenkins instances: main `10.254.144.112:8181`, 中台 `10.9.94.63:15050`, 星链 `starlink-jenkins.hungrystudio.pp.ua:8181`, iOS/mbh `mbhpacker1.youxi123.com:8080`.

## Pipelines and jobs

- Starlink CI/CD pipelines point to `starlink/solutionhub` and `starlink/hs-code-keeper`; frontend build Jenkinsfiles are at `hs.projects/hs-devops/jenkins-pipeline-scripts/starlink/jenkins-jobs/frontend/frontend-build/`.
- A reported list of 11 build jobs: `bbc`, `frontend`, `lowcodegql`, `pgpour`, `rustyme`, `starflow`, `feworkgql`, `ding`, `gql`, `fakeuser`, `hfrog`.
- A separate starlink-folder report lists 21 `-build` jobs (one per service, e.g. `bbc-build-tiger`, `frontend-build-tiger`, `gql-build`) that build and push Docker images.
- Starlink has production job `prod_starlink-pm`; there is no test job for Starlink.
- Build pipelines push Starlink images to `registry.hs99.vip`; all 11 build jobs dual-push to `registry.hs99.vip` and `starfamily-registry-vpc.cn-beijing.cr.aliyuncs.com` with the same path/tag.
- Jenkins pipelines build and publish Starlink Helm charts to OCI, including a `build-charts` job.
- `starorigin-mcps/star-maxcompute/star-maxcompute-deploy` is hosted on the Jenkins at devops-jenkins.hs99.vip.
- The `aigateway/astra` folder hosts StarAstra restart jobs; each job's `scriptPath` points to the corresponding starastra path in the repository.
- `ai-diagnostics-and-notify-when-failure` Jenkinsfile is at `hs-devops/jenkins-pipeline-scripts/misc/jenkins-jobs/ai-diagnostics-and-notify-when-failure/Jenkinsfile` and contains the `jenkinsUserToDingTalkUserId` mapping.
- Jenkins holds the `nebula_app_ids` that define the full Nebula game family.
- A `sync-envs` job syncs deployment configs from the hs-devops repo to the ACK clusters.
- Jenkins manages image tag versions in `versions.yaml` files.

## Database, backups, and sync

- Database restoration and database sync operations run on the Jenkins master `archteam-starfamily-jenkins-master`; PostgreSQL dump/restore runs there.
- Backup scripts are installed at `/data/backup-postgres/prd-blockbloom/dump-starlink-db.sh` and `/data/backup-postgres/alpha-blockbloom/dump-starlink-db.sh`; `backup-all.sh` auto-discovers all `dump-starlink-db.sh` scripts.
- Sync logs and dumps are stored at `~/jdmj-sync-from-crush/`.
- The Jenkins pipeline syncs data from prd to alpha but does not include schema changes.
- devops-jenkins runs the Starlink deploy and db-migrator playbooks and connects to `starlink-dev-internal.hs99.vip` as root; the x86_64 agent runs dump-and-restore Ansible playbooks.

## Credentials and secrets

- Stores kubeconfig credentials for starlink, starorigin, and aigateway as Secret file type (`FileCredentialsImpl`), used by the hourly ping-clusters job and deploy pipelines.
- Kubeconfigs cover GKE clusters: `starorigin-prod` Autopilot, `starorigin-dev` Standard Zonal `asia-northeast1-b`; Alibaba ACK clusters: starorigin dev/prod, starfamily devops, aigateway dev/prod.
- Has an age key for decrypting SOPS-encrypted secrets; jobs decrypt `*.enc.yaml` files in-place with `sops -d -i` during deployments.
- `gcloud` and `gke-gcloud-auth-plugin` are not installed on the Jenkins host.
- The Jenkins agent has its own credentials for the `starfamily-registry`, so its builds are unaffected by local Mac keychain issues.

## Permissions

- In Jenkins, a wrapper job's build step queues the downstream job as the Jenkins controller, so a user with Job/Build on the wrapper does not need permission on the underlying job.
- This permission bypass only applies when users trigger the wrapper; direct triggering of the downstream job still requires Job/Build on that job.

## Operational notes and limitations

- The Jenkins instance at 10.100.27.205 performed migration from MinIO across a cross-VPC link achieving ~47 KiB/s; logs show 425 unexpected EOF errors and many connection reset by peer errors when downloading from MinIO; it cannot reliably download objects cross-VPC from MinIO and could not finish large file transfers.
- Jenkins caches the last parameter definitions, so parameter dropdowns only repopulate after a build runs with the updated Jenkinsfile.

memories.body:
# BlockBlast (BlockBlast!)

- Identity: successful casual game by **HungryStudio**; the user works on its data pipelines and it is part of the user's infrastructure scope at HungryStudio. Project code **BBC**; production backend is the **BBC service**.
- Hosted on **Starlink** and is the product that Starlink belongs to. It is a standalone Starlink game, not in the Nebula series, and one of four live games in the starlink repo. PRD infrastructure runs on Starlink hosts (app, ro, n8n, alpha nodes).
- Provides the **hfrog** artifact service shared with **BlockCrush**; the hfrog component is used in lhh-blockcrush. BlockBlast is the production environment hosting hfrog, with its own hfrog DB (`prd_blockblast_hfrog`) on blockblast-prod RDS.

## Environments

- 14 named dev environments: `dev, kwd, yy, yl, cyx, hyx, lxy, lby, mx, dwb, lgh, lhh, lsx, wz`.
- LSX dev env (bb): https://lsx-blockblast.hs99.vip; Redis at `starlink-dev-uc.hs99.vip:31000` DB0.
- LHH client DB environment reachable at `lhh-blockblast.hs99.vip`; production connection ID `PROD_BLOCKBLAST_CLIENT_DB`.
- Multiple envs (dwb, lby, dev, kwd, lgh, lhh, lxy, cyx, mx, hyx) use **fakeuser** for auth. The fakeuser service exposes `/fakeuser/users` since image `main-b2394645` (2.0); older image `main-6773fc85` lacks it.
- Blockblast is a service with dwb and lby instances and is also a service in the starlink-alpha stack.

## Application stack

- `blockblast` is deployed at `starlink-alpha.youxi123.com`; runs 12 containers and uses openresty as reverse proxy.

## Hosting / deployment

- PRD runs on old UCloud host pair: `starlink-prd-blockblast-app-1` (`10.9.79.254`) and `-2` (`10.9.164.112`), accessed via gg profile; egress IPs 106.75.x (UCloud, not Aliyun). Source host for deployment is `10.9.79.254` (UCloud).
- New Aliyun app servers: `archteam-starlink-blockblast-app-1/2/3` at `10.100.30.117/118/119`, also referenced as `archteam-starlink-blockblast-prod-app-1/2/3`.
- BlockBlast prod `.env` identical across the three hosts: `APP_ID=block-blast`, `HOST=starlink.youxi123.com`, image tags, fixed service ports 20000-20011.

memories.body:
## Instance overview
- Jenkins is the CI/CD service the user manages at HungryStudio, part of the user's infrastructure stack, and a common MCP tool; supports Linux, Windows, and iOS agents.
- User's Jenkins instance: `https://devops-jenkins.hs99.vip`, named **uc-devops-jenkins**; Rocky Linux 9.7 (x86_64). It runs starlink deploy and db-migrator playbooks on its local agent, connects to `starlink-dev-internal.hs99.vip` as root, hosts starlink/ding jobs and starorigin419 CI jobs, and is used for starlink BBC builds.
- Internal Jenkins master: `archteam-starfamily-jenkins-master` at `10.100.27.205` (internal network via JumpServer; g7/hfg7 ECS; PostgreSQL 16.14 tools). Used for PostgreSQL dump/restore, DB sync/restoration tasks, BBC deployment jobs, and starlink pipeline scripts including `lowcodegql-build`.
- BlockBlast PRD uses multiple Jenkins instances: main at `10.254.144.112:8181`, 中台 at `10.9.94.63:15050`, 星链 at `starlink-jenkins.hungrystudio.pp.ua:8181`, iOS/mbh at `mbhpacker1.youxi123.com:8080`.

## Jobs / pipelines
- The Jenkins starlink folder has 21 `-build` jobs (one per service, e.g. `bbc-build-tiger`, `frontend-build-tiger`, `gql-build`) that build and push Docker images.
- A set of 11 build jobs (`bbc`, `frontend`, `lowcodegql`, `pgpour`, `rustyme`, `starflow`, `feworkgql`, `ding`, `gql`, `fakeuser`, `hfrog`) push images to both `registry.hs99.vip` and `starfamily-registry-vpc.cn-beijing.cr.aliyuncs.com` with the same path/tag.
- Starlink images are dual-pushed by Jenkins build pipelines; hs.projects pipelines also push all Starlink images to `registry.hs99.vip`.
- Starlink CI/CD pipelines currently point to `starlink/solutionhub` and `starlink/hs-code-keeper`; production job `prod_starlink-pm` exists; no test job exists for starlink.
- Starlink frontend build Jenkinsfiles: `hs.projects/hs-devops/jenkins-pipeline-scripts/starlink/jenkins-jobs/frontend/frontend-build/`.
- A `sync-envs` job syncs deployment configs from the hs-devops repo to ACK clusters.
- Hosts StarAstra restart jobs under the `aigateway/astra` folder; each job's `scriptPath` points to the corresponding starastra path in the repository.
- Hosts `starorigin-mcps/star-maxcompute/star-maxcompute-deploy`.
- Runs `ai-diagnostics-and-notify-when-failure`; its Jenkinsfile is at `hs-devops/jenkins-pipeline-scripts/misc/jenkins-jobs/ai-diagnostics-and-notify-when-failure/Jenkinsfile` and contains the `jenkinsUserToDingTalkUserId` mapping.
- Pipelines build and publish starlink Helm charts to OCI, including a `build-charts` job.
- Jenkins holds the `nebula_app_ids` that define the full Nebula game family.
- Jenkins caches the last parameter definitions, so parameter dropdowns only repopulate after a build runs with the updated Jenkinsfile.

## Credentials & agents
- Kubeconfigs are stored as FileCredentialsImpl (Secret File) credentials for `starlink`, `starorigin`, and `aigateway`; they cover GKE clusters (`starorigin-prod` Autopilot, `starorigin-dev` Standard Zonal asia-northeast1-b) and Alibaba ACK clusters (starorigin dev/prod, starfamily devops, aigateway dev/prod). These are used by the hourly `ping-clusters` job and deploy pipelines.
- Registered credentials include: `kubeconfig-ack-starlink-dev`, `kubeconfig-ack-starlink-prod`, `hs-devops-infra-sops-age-key`, `liguanghui_ssh_key_at_git_7k7k_com`.
- `gcloud` and `gke-gcloud-auth-plugin` are not installed on the Jenkins host.
- The Jenkins x86_64 agent runs dump-and-restore Ansible playbooks.
- Jenkins manages image tag versions in `versions.yaml` files; it has an age key for decrypting SOPS-encrypted secrets, and jobs decrypt `*.enc.yaml` files in-place with `sops -d -i` during deployments.
- The Jenkins agent has its own credentials for the `starfamily-registry`, so its builds are unaffected by local Mac keychain issues.

## Database / backup / sync
- Backup scripts are installed at `/data/backup-postgres/prd-blockbloom/dump-starlink-db.sh` and `/data/backup-postgres/alpha-blockbloom/dump-starlink-db.sh`.
- `backup-all.sh` on Jenkins auto-discovers all `dump-starlink-db.sh` scripts.
- PostgreSQL dump/restore runs on the Jenkins master `archteam-starfamily-jenkins-master`.
- Jenkins is used for database restoration and sync operations; sync logs and dumps are stored at `~/jdmj-sync-from-crush/`.
- The Jenkins pipeline syncs data from prd to alpha but does not include schema changes.

## Permissions
- In Jenkins, a wrapper job's `build` step queues the downstream job as the Jenkins controller, so a user with Job/Build on the wrapper does not need permission on the underlying job.
- This permission bypass only applies when users trigger the wrapper; direct triggering of the downstream job still requires Job/Build on that job.

## MinIO migration issues
- Jenkins at `10.100.27.205` was used for MinIO migration attempts across a cross-VPC link, achieving ~47 KiB/s.
- Migration logs showed 425 unexpected EOF errors and many connection reset by peer errors when downloading from MinIO; Jenkins cannot reliably download objects cross-VPC from MinIO and could not finish large file transfers.

# Stargate LLM Gateway

- **Endpoint**: `https://stargate.youxi123.com`
- **Type**: LiteLLM-based, OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway.
- **Model support**: Exposes `/v1/models`, including `deepseek-v4-flash`; total of 27 models listed.

## Usage

- Serves as the LLM gateway for RMB systems and `rmb-desktop`.
- Used by the `rmbd` binary, the memory pipeline, L2 `build_scenes` calls, and the memory worker's L3 rollup.
- Faster than Volces for small-session probes.
- Its capacity limits how high `l3Concurrency` can be raised.

## Timeout history

- Requests awaiting response headers can time out at 45 seconds.
- In RMB Desktop 0.1.19, this caused `context deadline exceeded` errors.
- The default 45s `llm.timeout` was noted as likely too short for L2 `build_scenes` calls and could stall scene distillation.

memories.abstract: RMB Desktop (rmb-desktop): user's local-first macOS memory desktop app, Tauri tray shell + pure-Go rmbd daemon, SQLite WAL/sqlite-vec, L0-L3 distillation pipeline, OpenAI-compatible LLM/embedding providers, agents (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi), repo colinleefish/rmb-desktop; latest observed v0.1.19.
memories.body:
## Identity
- `rmb-desktop` / `RMB Desktop` / `RMB-Desktop`: a local-first desktop app, GUI, and local CLI/tool for RMB memory; under active development by the user; personal product, license TBD, shipped from re-mem-ber.me.
- Repo: `github.com/colinleefish/rmb-desktop`; local path `/Users/liguanghui/Virginia/colinleefish/rmb-desktop`; Herdr workspace w7 corresponds to this project.
- macOS menu-bar app, bundle ID `me.remember.rmb`, LSUIElement, installed at `/Applications/RMB Desktop.app`; earlier install observed at `/Applications/rmb.app` with display name `rmb`.
- Known versions: v0.1.0, v0.1.1/v0.1.2 (aarch64), v0.1.9 observed, v0.1.16 release as of August 2026, and v0.1.19 observed.

## Architecture & runtime
- Tauri-based tray/menu-bar shell manages the daemon (Start/Stop `rmbd`, Open Dashboard); backend is a pure-Go `rmbd` daemon; HTTP API at `127.0.0.1:19019`; a remote instance is reachable at `10.254.24.7:19019`.
- Bundles CLI `rmb` (also observed as sidecar `rmb-app`) and daemon `rmbd-desktop` under `~/.rmb/bin/`; first-run bootstrap copies bundled binaries/sidecars there if newer and installs LaunchAgent `me.remember.rmb.plist`; startup syncs newer bundled binaries to `~/.rmb/bin/`.
- Data: local SQLite at `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/data/rmb.db`, WAL mode, foreign keys enabled, with `sqlite-vec`; memory layers L0-L3.
- Config: `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/config.yaml`; API keys kept in config; launch-at-login stored under `launch_at_login`.
- Onboarding marker: `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/onboarding.complete` with `completed_at` and `skipped_agents`; endpoints `GET /api/v1/onboarding/status`, `POST /api/v1/onboarding/complete`, `POST /api/v1/onboarding/reset`.
- Local-first: no installs/heartbeats reported; rejects iCloud/Dropbox sync due to corruption risk; supports optional dual-submit to `rmb.colinleefish.com` and deferred sync at `sync.re-mem-ber.me`.
- Supports OpenAI-compatible API format for LLM and embedding providers.

## UI / build
- Web UI source lives in `webui/`; Vite-built and embedded via `go:embed`; `internal/http/static/web/` is generated output only and must not be edited; built with `make webui-build`; dev server via `npm run dev:mock-setup`.
- Browser title and Tauri app name: `RMB Desktop`; favicon is a purple gradient SVG at `ui/public/favicon.svg`; sidebar uses a Lucide Brain icon as placeholder brand mark.
- Settings tabs: General, Models, Advanced; Integrations is a top-level sidebar item; includes a setup flow for installing agents.
- General settings include display language, distillation database path, and config file collection address.

## Memory & agents
- Pipeline distills conversations through L0-L1-L2-L3: turns -> atoms -> scenes -> memories; addressed by `rmb://` URIs.
- Memory categories include profile, entities, preferences, events; also corrections and recall stats; `recall_stats` table keyed by URI.
- Workers: l1/l2/l3 plus embed worker; `pipeline_state` table; scenes table and FTS5 virtual table `scenes_fts` (content=`scenes`, tokenize=`unicode61`), populated by L2 stage, rebuilt on startup with only a warning on failure.
- Agents supported: Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi. Currently writes shell hooks for OpenCode and Pi, which is incorrect for those agents.
- Direct SQL into RMB Desktop memories is possible but fragile; `rmb-desktop` is the user's real database used by the pipeline daemon.

## Distribution / release
- Signed/notarized aarch64 DMGs via GitHub Releases and Quick Whale; also distributed via Cloudflare R2 at `releases.re-mem-ber.me`; packaged via `make app-build` and `finish-dmg.sh`.
- Not sandboxed; uses macOS Hardened Runtime; codesigned with Developer ID Application: GUANGHUI LI (N4YPJBRBN4); Tauri `exceptionDomain` set to empty string, allowing cleartext HTTP through ATS exceptions.
- Tauri updater disabled (`updater.active: false`); planned distribution: DMG for macOS, MSI/EXE for Windows, AppImage/DEB for Linux.

## Migrations & known issues
- Goose migrations run automatically on `rmbd` start; migration SQL is embedded, so users never run migration scripts manually; stop -> migrate -> restart orchestration is not yet built.

# Cursor

- Cursor is an AI agent tool that the rmb-desktop project integrates with; the user uses Cursor as their code editor and one of their primary coding tools.

- Cursor natively loads skills from ~/.cursor/skills-cursor/* and plugin skills.
- Cursor uses MCP config at ~/.cursor/mcp.json.

## Behavior / Limitations
- Cursor's agent mode terminates background processes tied to the agent shell when the turn ends.
- Cursor stores User Rules internally and does not expose them to the backend; the rmbd backend cannot read Cursor User Rules. apply_mode is copy_only.

memories.body:
# feature_config

- Database table in the starlink project; main feature configuration table in the starlink blockblast client database; also described as the BlockCrush table for 创意 (ideas).
- Observed row counts: ~2265 rows in one source; 54 columns and 331 rows in prod BlockCrush.
- Has 54 columns identical to dwb-blockcrush in prd-blockcrush and prd-mahjongwonders, except `idea_label` is type `text` instead of `text[]`.
  - In `prd_mjwd_client`, `feature_config.idea_label` stores comma-separated strings (e.g. 'UI专项,交互') that must be split into `text[]` during migration.

## Key columns / relationships
- Stores 创意 with `feature_key` and `idea_priority` (int 1–10, often null).
- `feature_config.workflow_info_id` is nullable and links to `fc_workflow_info`.
- Links to 需求 in `pm_work_item` via `feature_config.feature_key = pm_work_item.extra->>'feature_key'`.
- People columns: creator (`create_avatar_name/id`), editor (`editer_avatar_name/id`), reviewer (`reviewer_avatar_name/id/workcode`), and `functional_dev`; the proposer is not on this table.

## Indexes / constraints
- Unique index/constraint on `(platform, feature_desc)`.
- Unique index on `(platform, feature_id)`.
- Single-column indexes on `platform` and `feature_id`.
- No index on `editer_time`.
- `platform` is an enum column (`efeatureplatform`), cast to text when synced.

## Model / performance
- The BBC feature_config model's `fc_param_rules` relationship uses `lazy='joined'`, forcing a LEFT OUTER JOIN on every query and amplifying result sets.

## Sync / publication
- `feature_config` (table A) is a source table whose columns are synced into `feature_config_workflow_info` (C).
- Trigger `trg_sync_feature_config_workflow_info_from_fc` in the alpha BlockCrush database syncs rows to `feature_config_workflow_info`.
- Source table A in the feature-config merge system; contains 'fake prefix' columns like `fc_origin` and `fc_origin_param`, whose names were inherited into the merged table.
- Source table A in `dwb_blockcrush_client`, published to Kafka via `bbc_publication`.

## Workflow / people
- In Block Crush, a PM-native story creative's `is_mock` flag is cleared only when the requirement reaches the '结束' workflow node, which makes it appear in the creative dictionary.
- In `prd_blockcrush_client`, exactly 9 feature_config rows are linked to `fc_workflow_info` rows with `expected_first_launch_batch='GP33期'`.
- 吴绪鹏 (Wu Xupeng) reviews and follows up on items; 刘欣欣 proposes, creates, and follows up on items.

memories.body:
# BlockBlast

## Identity
- BlockBlast (also Blockblast, shorthand "bb") is a successful casual game by HungryStudio; the user works on it and it is in the user's infrastructure scope.
- It is a game under the BBC project; its production backend is the BBC service.
- Hosted on Starlink / part of the Starlink repo; one of the four live games there. Standalone Starlink game, not part of the Nebula series.
- Provides the hfrog artifact service shared with BlockCrush; hfrog is used in the lhh-blockcrush project. BlockBlast also has its own hfrog database (prd_blockblast_hfrog) on blockblast-prod RDS.
- external_system config services: admarket, n8n, hfrog, user, bbc, automated_testing, mainstream_automated_testing, publish_platform_gp, publish_platform_ios.

## Environments
- 14 named dev environments: dev, kwd, yy, yl, cyx, hyx, lxy, lby, mx, dwb, lgh, lhh, lsx, wz.
- BlockBlast is a service in the starlink-alpha stack, with dwb and lby instances; the application stack is deployed at starlink-alpha.youxi123.com, runs 12 containers, and uses OpenResty as reverse proxy.
- Environments dwb, lby, dev, kwd, lgh, lhh, lxy, cyx, mx, hyx use fakeuser for user auth.
- fakeuser exposes /fakeuser/users since image main-b2394645 (2.0); older image main-6773fc85 lacks it.
- lsx dev environment: https://lsx-blockblast.hs99.vip, with Redis at starlink-dev-uc.hs99.vip:31000 DB0.
- lhh environment: lhh-blockblast.hs99.vip; the client database has production connection ID PROD_BLOCKBLAST_CLIENT_DB.

## Production infrastructure
- PRD runs on UCloud hosts starlink-prd-blockblast-app-1 (10.9.79.254) and app-2 (10.9.164.112), accessed via the gg profile; the starlink-prd-blockblast app pair has egress IPs 106.75.x.
- New Aliyun production app servers: archteam-starlink-blockblast-app-1/2/3 at 10.100.30.117/118/119 (also referenced as archteam-starlink-blockblast-prod-app-1/2/3).
- Production is being migrated from UCloud to Aliyun; the Starflow service is part of this migration. SSH access during migration uses UCloud jumpserver 106.75.24.230.
- BlockBlast prod .env is identical across hosts: APP_ID=block-blast, HOST=starlink.youxi123.com, image tags, and fixed service ports 20000-20011.
- docker-compose uses images from registry.hs99.vip/starlink/bbc and sends OTEL metrics to host.docker.internal:24318; deployment source host is 10.9.79.254.

## Databases
- Production PostgreSQL databases on UCloud: hs_client_db (~14 GB) and hs_code_keeper_db (~9 MB), being migrated to Aliyun RDS.
- Aliyun RDS migration target: instance pgm-2zevk26j83oa40t4, account caikuai-cn, host archteam-starlink-blockblast-prod.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com, RO host archteam-starlink-blockblast-prod-ro.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com, port 5432, databases prd_blockblast_client and prd_blockblast_codekeeper.
- PRD uses Aliyun RDS databases prd_blockblast_client, prd_blockblast_codekeeper, and prd_blockblast_hfrog. PRD client db on hs_client_db is at 10.9.177.238.
- BlockBlast is a separate game database with a different schema (~120 tables); it is not part of the Nebula 5-DB set.
- Schema fact: in BlockBlast client databases (PRD prd_blockblast_client, alpha alpha_blockblast_client, and dev lgh/lhh/lsx/wz clones), public.solution.solution_ai_mark_id is integer (INT4), nullable, with a foreign key to solution_ai_marks(id); solution_ai_marks.id is serial, and the BBC flow writes integer IDs back into solution.solution_ai_mark_id.
- Employee DingTalk ID lookup uses prd_blockblast_codekeeper.avatar (username and DingTalk staffId) and falls back to prd_blockblast_client.uums.yunxiao_member_bind.

## Production RO nodes
- BlockBlast production has 4 read-only nodes:
  - archteam-starlink-blockblast-prod-ro-1 (10.100.0.31)
  - archteam-starlink-blockblast-prod-ro-2 (10.100.0.56)
  - archteam-starlink-blockblast-prod-ro-3 (10.100.116.171)
  - archteam-starlink-blockblast-prod-ro-4 (10.100.0.37)
- Prod RO tier runs only bbc and gql services; no starflow/hfrog/OTLP. Data path: /data/starlink-blockblast-prod.

## Data / pipelines / security
- blockblast production CDC pipeline (18977) is consumed by pgpour; the PRD BI solution uses an Outbox → message table → pgpour → Kafka pipeline. The pgpour prod pipeline uses image tag main-2ce47744.
- BlockBlast keeps /api open (no key required) and restricts /gql/ to key-auth + ACL with consumers liguanghui, starorigin, bi, etc.

## Ops observations
- BlockBlast Jenkins jobs (alpha, lby, lxy) write ~1.3 GB DB dumps to /tmp on uc-devops-jenkins and never clean them up, causing recurring disk pressure.
- BlockBlast prod BBC logs are shipped from 5 hosts: archteam-starlink-blockblast-prod-app-1/2/3, archteam-starlink-blockblast-prd-ro-1, and starlink-prd-blockblast-ro-1. BBC RO hosts have OTEL exporter connection failures to localhost:4318/v1/metrics.

memories.body:
# RMB Desktop (rmb-desktop)

## Identity
- Product/display name: **RMB Desktop** (also RMB-Desktop). Desktop/local GUI version of the user's rmb memory product; repo: `github.com/colinleefish/rmb-desktop`; local checkout: `/Users/liguanghui/Virginia/colinleefish/rmb-desktop`. Herdr workspace w7 corresponds to this project.
- Installed app: `/Applications/RMB Desktop.app`; bundle id `me.remember.rmb`. Older `/Applications/rmb.app` path is superseded. Site: re-mem-ber.me; license TBD.
- Observed/referenced versions include 0.1.0, 0.1.1, 0.1.2, 0.1.9, 0.1.16 (latest known as of Aug 2026), and 0.1.19. Apple Silicon (aarch64).

## Architecture & binaries
- Formerly Tauri-based; current build is a pure-Go tray app shell (`rmb-app`) plus a Go backend daemon (`rmbd`; `cmd/rmbd/main.go`, `internal/httpserver`). The app shell is a minimal tray/daemon-management shell; the daemon serves the embedded web UI/settings page. Go packages include `internal/worker/scene` and `internal/db`.
- Binaries: `rmb` (CLI with ls/pull/put subcommands) and `rmbd` (daemon); there is a sidecar self-updater. Runtime sidecars live under `~/.rmb/bin/`; referenced names include `rmb-desktop` (older) and `rmb-app` (later) for the app, `rmbd-desktop` for the daemon, and `~/.rmb/bin/rmb` for the CLI.
- rmbd listens on `127.0.0.1:19019`; an instance is also deployed on remote box `10.254.24.7`, where the debug API is reachable at `10.254.24.7:19019`.
- Schema migrations run automatically via goose on startup with migration SQL embedded in the binary; end users do not run migration scripts. Stop→migrate→restart orchestration is not yet built.

## Data & privacy
- Local-first. App data/config/onboarding live under `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/`; config at `.../config.yaml`; SQLite DB at `.../data/rmb.db`. SQLite uses WAL journal mode and foreign keys are enabled.
- No install/heartbeat reporting. iCloud and Dropbox sync are explicitly rejected due to corruption risk.
- Sync: dual-submit to hosted endpoint `rmb.colinleefish.com`; deferred sync at `sync.re-mem-ber.me`.
- Memory system: captures full conversations and distills through an L0-L1-L2-L3 pyramid (turns, atoms, scenes, memories) addressed by `rmb://` URIs. Categories include profile, entities, preferences, events; supports corrections and recall stats. Workers include l1/l2/l3 and an embed worker; `pipeline_state` tracks l1/l2/l3 started times and last errors. `recall_stats` is keyed by URI.

## UI / settings
- Web UI source of truth is `webui/` at `/Users/liguanghui/Virginia/colinleefish/rmb-desktop/webui`; dev server starts with `npm run dev:mock-setup`. Embedded web assets are generated by `make webui-build`; `internal/http/static/web/` is generated output and must not be edited by hand.
- Settings tabs: General, Models, Advanced; Integrations is a top-level sidebar item. General includes display language, distillation database path, and config file collection address. Configuration page has LLM and embedding API key fields; API keys are kept in config.
- Launch-at-login writes `launch_at_login` to config.yaml and updates LaunchAgent at `~/Library/LaunchAgents/me.remember.rmb.plist`.
- rmb-desktop supports the OpenAI-compatible API format for LLM and embedding providers.
- Agents supported: Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi. Currently writes shell hooks for OpenCode and Pi, which is incorrect for those agents.

## Packaging & distribution
- macOS DMG built via `make app-build` and `finish-dmg.sh`; signed with Developer ID GUANGHUI LI (N4YPJBRBN4), hardened runtime, timestamp; nested sidecar rmb/rmbd binaries are individually codesigned; released DMGs are notarized and stapled. App is not sandboxed.
- Distributed via GitHub Releases, Cloudflare R2 (`https://releases.re-mem-ber.me/latest.json`), and Quick Whale. Release assets include `RMB.Desktop_<ver>_aarch64.dmg`, `darwin_arm64` tarball, `windows_amd64` zip, and `manifest.json`. Planned packaging: MSI/EXE for Windows, AppImage/DEB for Linux.
- Build tooling: `build-sidecar-bundles.sh`, `release.sh`, Makefile with sidecar-bundles target.

## API / onboarding / debug
- Onboarding first-run gate: marker `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/onboarding.complete` (JSON with `completed_at` and `skipped_agents`). Endpoints: `GET /api/v1/onboarding/status`, `POST /api/v1/onboarding/complete`, `POST /api/v1/onboarding/reset`.
- `GET /healthz` returns ok when the database opens and reports SQLite/vector status. `GET /api/v1/version` reports app version but not DB schema version.
- Debug endpoints are exposed under `/api/v1/debug/*` (also described as `/debug/`) and cover workers, in-flight tasks, backpressure, logs, SQLite, pipeline stuck/unstick/requeue, LLM build-scenes, and pipeline dry-run. These routes are unauthenticated, as is the rest of the desktop rmbd.
- In 0.1.19, every LLM request is logged to `/api/v1/debug/logs` with fields op, attempt, model, host, status, latency_ms, req_bytes, resp_bytes, and err.

## Database & known issues
- Schema includes a `scenes` table and an FTS5 external-content index `scenes_fts` over scenes (`content='scenes'`, `tokenize='unicode61'`), populated by the L2 pipeline. The L2 scene worker is at `internal/worker/scene/worker.go`; rmbd rebuilds `scenes_fts` on startup but only warns if the rebuild fails.
- `scripts/backfill-from-remote.py` is a data-migration script for importing sessions from remote rmb instances, not a schema migration.
- Known issues: L2 pipeline can get stuck when sessions remain in running status after crashes/restarts; 0.1.19 had a 2KB LLM truncation bug causing unexpected end of JSON input errors in the L2 pipeline. 0.1.19 includes 0.1.18 fixes: `llm.timeout` default 45s, T2 atom trim, and real error text in logs. Direct SQL into RMB Desktop memories is possible but fragile.

## Events (dated record)
- 2026-08-14: RMB Desktop README did not document automatic DB migrations, and the Makefile advertised a `make migrate` target that does not exist.
- 2026-08-14: The `scenes` table was empty; the `scenes_fts` FTS index appeared missing or corrupted (rebuild failed with "no such table" while the app logged malformed), suspected to be the cause of L2 persist failures.

memories.body:
# RMB (Recall Memory Bank)

## Identity & Access
- RMB (`rmb`) is the user's personal long-term memory system for AI-agent conversations, built and owned by the user. Former names: `mem9`, `mypast`, `mem-colinleefish`, `mem-colinleefish-com`. It is a client-server CLI tool, memory agent backend, and desktop app (menu bar, no Dock icon).
- Source: GitHub repo `colinleefish/rmb`; local clone at `/Users/liguanghui/Virginia/colinleefish/rmb`. Remote server SSH: `root@rmb.colinleefish.com`.
- Production: https://rmb.colinleefish.com. Basic auth: user `rmb`, password `sVf3^n5ht`.
- Docs site: built with VitePress, bilingual EN/zh under `docs/concept` and `docs/zh/concept`.
- RMB has not been evaluated on MemoryAgentBench.

## Architecture & Data Model
- Single-binary Go app serving as server and CLI (Gin, GORM, goose migrations); the CLI is a pure HTTP API client and never touches the database. CLI uses a hand-rolled switch-based argument parser (no Cobra). Server defaults to 127.0.0.1:8080, requires auth for public binds, enforces 32 MiB upload limit and UUID session IDs.
- Memory pyramid: T0 session_turns → T1 atoms → T2 scenes → T3 memories; full pipeline is L0 capture, L1 extract, L2 scene, L3 memory, L4 embeddings. T3 polls every 5 min and distills atoms across sessions into shared buckets (`rmb://profile`, `rmb://entities/...`, `rmb://preferences/...`, `rmb://events/...`). T1 extracts atoms in batches of up to 8 turns per LLM call; T2 builds session-local scenes (scene URI is UUIDv5 derived from session_id + display_name); T2 overwrites a scene row on rebuild with no version history. A session can have multiple scenes; `display_name` is a short human-readable topic title.
- URI space is deliberately flat (architecture decision D1): type/tier is the first segment — `rmb://turns/<uuid>`, `rmb://atoms/<uuid>`, `rmb://scenes/<uuid>`, `rmb://sessions/<uuid>`, `rmb://entities/<slug>`, `rmb://preferences/<slug>`, `rmb://events/<slug>`, `rmb://skills/<slug>`. `rmb://sessions/<key>/` is only a navigation view. Atoms use UUID primary key; the atom `uri` column was removed.
- Memories table is versioned and append-only, keyed by URI with one active row per URI. Separate append-only corrections table synced by id; corrections are additive overlays, newest-wins, human authority, no hard-delete primitive. Events are immutable and first-write-wins by URI. Skills are versioned by `bundle_sha256`; skill paths normalize to `rmb://skills/<slug>`. Sessions and turns sync by `session_key` + turn id; `turn_count` is computed at read time. Sync resolves conflicts by syncing rows by id, unioning provenance, then re-distilling.
- Alias/canonical mode folds aliases into a canonical entity (`aliases`, `alias_candidates` tables); flat-star invariant means no alias chains, with service-layer enforcement future work; recall does not yet resolve aliases. Alias suggestion uses embeddings with default cosine floor 0.82. Agent guide (`agent_guide.md`) is system docs, not user memory, and is injected into every agent context at session start; it is mirrored into the memories DB by UpsertAgentGuide.
- Storage: desktop uses SQLite (mattn/go-sqlite3, FTS5 external-content tables `scenes_fts`, `atoms_fts`, `memories_fts`); server uses PostgreSQL/pgvector with `vector(1024)` and HNSW cosine indexes. Only active memories (`superseded_at IS NULL`) are embedded/recalled. Recall is hybrid vector + Postgres FTS + RRF fusion (`find` = vector, `search` = hybrid); SQLite search similarly uses FTSMemories + VectorMemories. `recall_stats` table (migration `00023_recall_stats.sql`) records stats server-side via `rmb search/cat/meta`.
- LLM provider: DeepSeek (`api.deepseek.com`), model `deepseek-v4-flash`, configured via `llm.api_base` in config.yaml; default LLM timeout is 300s (changed from 45s in 0.1.22). LLM failures are tracked in `pipeline_state` as `l1_last_error` with self-healing retries. Default embedding model: OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small`, dimension 1024; the dimension is fixed after set and returned vector length must exactly match the configured dimension.
- Default concurrency: L2 max 16, L1 max 64. Sessions table has optional `scope_key`/`title`; a session-abstract embedding is planned but not yet populated (embed worker does not fill `sessions.abstract`).

## Components, Paths & Desktop
- Binaries in `~/.rmb/bin/`: `rmb` (CLI), `rmb-app`, `rmbd`, `rmbd-desktop`. CLI binary: `~/.rmb/bin/rmb`; app bundle ID `me.remember.rmb`.
- RMB Desktop: macOS app at `/Applications/RMB Desktop.app` (also seen as `/Applications/rmb.app`), codesigned with Developer ID Application cert GUANGHUI LI (N4YPJBRBN4), distributed as `.dmg`; no auto-update (Tauri updater `active: false`); releases are manual via GitHub Release. Desktop app managed via LaunchAgents `me.remember.rmb`, `me.remember.rmbd`, and `me.remember.rmb.login`; single-instance lock prevents duplicate menu bar instances; tray polls `/healthz` every 5s and auto-restarts the daemon on failure. Desktop/tray was Tauri (Rust) and is being migrated from Tauri to a Go shell; start-on-login is already a Go daemon feature (`internal/launchatlogin`), independent of Tauri/systray.
- Desktop data: `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/data/rmb.db`; config `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/config.yaml`; logs at `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/logs/rmbd.log` (auto-rotate at 5 MB). Local daemon HTTP API on 127.0.0.1:19019 (e.g. `GET /api/v1/version`, `GET /healthz`; healthz does not return app version). Test daemon uses 127.0.0.1:19097. Desktop web UI: `http://127.0.0.1:19019/ui/`; web UI basePath `/ui`; server embeds Next.js static assets at `internal/http/static/web/`.
- Bootstrap self-heals sidecars in `~/.rmb/bin/` by checking executable magic numbers (Mach-O/MZ/ELF), even if a clobbered file's mtime is newer; it cannot detect a sidecar replaced with a different-but-valid Mach-O binary.

## CLI, Config & Integrations
- CLI commands: `search`, `cat`, `ls`, `meta`, `pull`, `put`, `setup`, `hook-submit`, `version`; `tree` and `skill` subcommands were removed (use `ls` and generic `pull`/`put` on `rmb://skills/`). `rmb version` currently prints `rmb dev`. On first run / with no args, the CLI bootstraps profile, agent guide, and skills catalog (20+ skills incl. JumpServer, humanizer, ascii-diagram) and prints profile.
- Config resolution: `RMB_CONFIG` env, `RMB_CONF` env, `~/.rmb.conf`, then `~/.rmb/config.yaml` (points to `https://rmb.colinleefish.com`). Server deployment config: `/opt/rmb/.env`; repo `.env` sets `RMB_CONFIG=.env`, which overrides `~/.rmb.conf` when run from the repo. An empty `RMB_URL` env var can make the CLI ignore its config file. `rmb search` ranks purely by semantic relevance (vector + FTS, RRF 70/30), no time weighting; timeline queries use `rmb ls rmb://events/` (formerly `rmb tree`), ordered by `updated_at DESC`, cap 200.
- Integrations: Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi. `internal/setup/` provides detect/preview/apply for Cursor, CC, Codex, OpenCode, Pi; config changes require preview-before-apply. Cursor hook install merges `rmb hook-submit` into the `hooks.stop` array of `~/.cursor/hooks.json`, preserves other hook events, adds `timeout: 15` if missing; detection only checks `hooks.stop` contains `rmb hook-submit`; uses `./hooks/audit.sh`. Configuration is detected by presence of `# RMB memory` + `ALWAYS RUN` + backticked `rmb` + `cli`; old `<!-- rmb:recall:start/end -->` markers remain compatible. Codex is supported via `rmb hook-submit --source=codex`; Cursor hook skips aborted turns. `rmb setup --agent=opencode/pi` installs hooks. Agent recall rules are at `rmb://agent`; `~/.rmb/bin/rmb` is the stable path for agent hooks. Server has hook-submit parsers for Codex/OpenCode/Pi; web UI has integration pages for Cursor, OpenCode, Pi; OpenCode/Pi guided setup requires manual confirmation/apply.
- API uses snake_case JSON with server-side pagination for sessions, pipeline, corrections; desktop exposes `POST /api/v1/sessions/{key}/upload`; server exposes `GET /api/v1/browse/...`. No bulk PUT for profile/entities/preferences/events. Backfill preserves session keys, message content, turn order, and re-distilled memories/skills path, but not original turn timestamps or bit-identical old T3 text.

## Deployment & Operations
- Production deployed via Docker only (not Vercel) using Aliyun ACR image `registry.cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/colinleefish/rmb:main`; `make deploy` / `deploy.sh` runs git pull + docker compose pull/up; `.env` is gitignored. Images tagged by git commit SHA and run `/rmb serve`; `install.sh` downloads binaries from GitHub Releases. Server runs as a minimal bundle at `/app/rmb` (docker-compose.yml, .env, config/Caddyfile) with no git checkout on the server. Database `rmb_db`, user `rmb_user`, password `0c2791d39900292afc7948f520bc0aa3`, Postgres 18.3 with pgvector 0.8.2 at 127.0.0.1:5432 (default DSN sslmode=disable); `/healthz` returns git commit SHA.
- The same host also runs the pbp (stock sync) project at `/app/pbp` (Docker, `pbp_db`, user `pbp_user_rw`, 15 tables, reachable at rmb.colinleefish.com:5432, remote SSL via `*.colinleefish.com` cert auto-renewed weekly; network_mode host; single CPU core). The pbp pipeline (stock daily, fund daily, valuation, financials) runs there with progress in `sync.sync_state`. Also deployed as two separate server instances on 182.92.114.13, ports 18080 and 18081.
- Targets: macOS arm64 and Windows x64 (Windows not supported for start-on-login — returns 'only supported on macOS'); Windows installer is unsigned. No one-click server-to-desktop migration (pg_dump won't load into desktop SQLite); built-in cross-device sync is a deferred paid feature (sync.re-mem-ber.me); syncing rmb.db via iCloud/Dropbox is considered unsafe. Cross-instance behavior uses client-to-remote HTTP API; no BitTorrent/DHT. Product assumes one daemon per DB file; two daemons on the same DB can create duplicate atoms.

## Dated Record & Known Limitations
- Events (immutable):
  - Migration 00006 inserts `rmb://agent` v1, then UpsertAgentGuide supersedes to v2, making the version counter permanently off by one.
  - 2026-07-25: RMB lacked knowledge base, memory promotion, entity relationship graph, and multi-tenant sharing (gaps vs ContextDB).
  - 2026-08-14: goose migrations were at version 9.
  - 2026-08-16: RMB Desktop was hand-packed version 0.2.0, commit b93641c; rmb 0.1.22 stack included RMB Desktop.app, rmbd on 127.0.0.1:19019, and rmb CLI; default LLM timeout changed to 300s.
  - Observed scale: ~1,258 scenes across 314 sessions. Mock/test data includes 刘欣欣 (system ID 62, workcode 001971).
- Limitations/bugs: `persistScenes` deletes the FTS entry after content upsert (even first-time creation), causing SQLITE_CORRUPT on otherwise healthy DBs; `scenes_fts` can corrupt under concurrent L2 writer writes. A corrupted `rmb.db` had 0 scenes and 45 zombie 'running' sessions before the fix. Go unit tests exist but no HTTP handler/UI/integration tests; `TestWritePlist` fails when `/Applications/RMB Desktop.app` exists. No procedural memory track yet; single namespace, not multi-tenant; no auto-update.

memories.body:
# PBP

PBP (Print Baby Print) is the user's Chinese A-share quantitative data sync service and stock data pipeline. It is a personal project authored by and owned by the user.

## Locations / Deployment
- Local checkout: `/Users/liguanghui/Virginia/colinleefish/pbp`
- GitHub: `github.com/colinleefish/pbp`
- Deployed on: `rmb.colinleefish.com`; code lives at `/app/pbp` on the rmb server
- Deployed via Docker Compose; ofelia schedules `pbp-sync` daily at 18:00 CST
- Database: connects to `pbp_db` on the shared Postgres 18 instance at `rmb.colinleefish.com:5432` as `pbp_user_rw`

## Stack / Architecture
- Uses PostgreSQL and SQLAlchemy; Python dependency management and script execution via `uv`
- Database schemas: `catalog`, `history`, `landing`, `sync`
- Sync worker count is configurable via `--workers` CLI flag or `SYNC_WORKERS` env var (default 4)

## Data Sources
- Supports multiple A-share data sources with fallback: BaoStock, AKShare, Sina, Tencent, Eastmoney (East Money), THS, Shenwan
- BaoStock sync stores daily K-line/daily stock data in `landing.baostock_stock_daily`
- PBP syncs A-share market data from AKShare into PostgreSQL

## Sync Behavior
- Sync is idempotent and resumable; resumes from checkpoints after failure
- Gap-driven planner with merge-all batching: fetches each symbol's missing days in one API call
- BaoStock sync default start date: 2018-01-01
- General sync default date range: 2024-01-01 to last trading day

## Domain Detail
- PBP has two Shenwan SW2021 code systems: classify codes (e.g. 110101) and index codes (e.g. 850111); they do not join directly

## Refactor / Issues
- PBP is being refactored into waves W1–W9 with 44 tasks
- Known deployment mismatch: deployed `pbp:main` image still runs old `ingest_stock_valuation` task referencing the dropped `landing.valuation_spot` table, while local repo uses `ingest_em_valuation_daily` and `ingest_sina_valuation_spot`

memories.body:
# JumpServer (Bastion Host)

- **Instance:** `jump.hs99.vip` / `https://jump.hs99.vip`, running **JumpServer v4.10.16**.
- **Role:** Primary jump host / bastion for the user's work hosts and day-to-day infrastructure access at HungryStudio. Used to access Starlink alpha infrastructure and HungryStudio systems, including database operations, server access, VM access control, and account management. Operated by the user as part of Starlink infrastructure.
- **Access methods:** REST API and KoKo SSH gateway on port **2222**.
- **SSH auth:** Usernames in the form `JMS-<token_id>` with one-time token passwords. Each token is valid for effectively one SSH session; a fresh token is required for every new connection. Previously used SSH credentials cannot be reused. Tokens come from `conn_token.py`.
- **File transfer:** SCP/SFTP do not work through the KoKo SSH gateway; transfer files by piping `tar` over SSH.
- **Credentials:** Stored at `~/.hungrystudio/jump-hs99-vip`.
- **Password strategy:** Set to **email**.
- **Access restriction:** The instance is restricted to work hosts only. It is required to reach `caikuai-cn` Aliyun VPC resources from outside networks such as the company network or AWS.
- **Administration:** Administered by the operator skill `jump-hs99-vip` and the admin skill `manage-jumpserver`.

## Assets & organization

- Assets are organized by **cloud provider and network**, under the `/DEFAULT` tree; the `admin-all` permission rule covers all assets.
- **Default account on assets:** `osadmin`.
- **Account templates available:** `osadmin` and `ubuntu`; there is **no `wy.workcode` template**.
- JumpServer usernames generally follow **pinyin initials + workcode**, e.g., `wj.002616`.
- Manages/accesses: `prd-cloud-agent-app-platform`, StarLink assets, archteam assets, Airflow hosts (UCloud dev under `archteam-ucloud`; Aliyun dev under `ArchitectureTeam-HSDEVOPS-Airflow-Dev`), `mjwd`, `blockmj`, `blockcrush`, Nginx hosts, the `starlink-dev-all-in-one` RDS instance, and hosts under `hs99.vip`.
- **Hosted nodes:** Hosts the Starlink BlockBlast and BlockMJ production read-only nodes.

memories.abstract: Jenkins CI/CD at HungryStudio: instances (devops-jenkins.hs99.vip/uc-devops-jenkins, master 10.100.27.205/111.200.218.82, BlockBlast PRD instances), build/deploy jobs, starlink pipelines, credentials, kubeconfigs, SOPS age key, migration/network issues, permission behavior.
memories.body:
# Jenkins

## Instances
- **devops-jenkins.hs99.vip** (https://devops-jenkins.hs99.vip), instance name `uc-devops-jenkins`, Rocky Linux 9.7 x86_64. Also known as the StarOrigin 419 Jenkins server. Used for toolhub deployments, starlink BBC builds, starorigin419 CI jobs, starlink/ding jobs, db-migrator playbooks on its local agent, dump-and-restore Ansible playbooks, sync-envs job, deploy pipelines, and starlink deploy/db-migrator playbooks (connects to `starlink-dev-internal.hs99.vip` as root).
- **archteam-starfamily-jenkins-master** at `10.100.27.205` (internal network), also reachable at `111.200.218.82`; accessed via JumpServer; runs on a g7/hfg7 ECS instance with PostgreSQL 16.14 tools. Used for migration attempts, database syncs/restores, bbc-deploy jobs, starlink pipeline scripts (e.g., lowcodegql-build), and backup scripts. PostgreSQL dump/restore runs on this master.
- **BlockBlast PRD** uses multiple Jenkins instances: main at `10.254.144.112:8181`, 中台 at `10.9.94.63:15050`, 星链 at `starlink-jenkins.hungrystudio.pp.ua:8181`, iOS/mbh at `mbhpacker1.youxi123.com:8080`.
- Jenkins is the CI/CD tool the user manages/uses, with Linux, Windows, and iOS agents; part of HungryStudio's infrastructure stack and production infrastructure.

## Build jobs
- Jenkins has 11 build jobs: `bbc`, `frontend`, `lowcodegql`, `pgpour`, `rustyme`, `starflow`, `feworkgql`, `ding`, `gql`, `fakeuser`, `hfrog`.
- All 11 build jobs push to both `registry.hs99.vip` and `starfamily-registry-vpc.cn-beijing.cr.aliyuncs.com` with the same path and tag.
- Build pipelines (hs.projects) push all Starlink images to `registry.hs99.vip`; pipelines dual-push Starlink images to the new ACR as well.
- The `starlink` folder contains 21 `-build` jobs (one per service, e.g. `bbc-build-tiger`, `frontend-build-tiger`, `gql-build`) that build and push Docker images.
- Jenkins has a production job `prod_starlink-pm` for starlink, but no test job for starlink.
- Starlink frontend build Jenkinsfiles live at `hs.projects/hs-devops/jenkins-pipeline-scripts/starlink/jenkins-jobs/frontend/frontend-build/`.
- Jenkins manages image tag versions in `versions.yaml` files.
- Jenkins caches the last parameter definitions, so parameter dropdowns only repopulate after a build runs with the updated Jenkinsfile.
- Jobs are organized under folders like `starorigin-mcps`; `starorigin-mcps/star-maxcompute/star-maxcompute-deploy` is hosted on Jenkins.
- StarAstra restart jobs are under the `aigateway/astra` folder; each job's `scriptPath` points to the corresponding starastra path in the repository.
- The `ai-diagnostics-and-notify-when-failure` job runs on Jenkins; its Jenkinsfile at `hs-devops/jenkins-pipeline-scripts/misc/jenkins-jobs/ai-diagnostics-and-notify-when-failure/Jenkinsfile` contains the `jenkinsUserToDingTalkUserId` mapping.
- Jenkins has database dump/restore folders.
- Jenkins separates build and deploy jobs; NEBULA builds can deploy to multiple games.
- Jenkins has 60+ near-identical deploy Jenkinsfiles, including `bbc-deploy` and `bbc-deploy-next`.
- Jenkins holds `nebula_app_ids` that define the full Nebula game family.

## CI/CD usage
- Used for CI/CD pipelines in the starlink project, currently pointing to `starlink/solutionhub` and `starlink/hs-code-keeper`.
- Used to build and deploy the BBC service; also deploys BBC, frontend, and GQL to production environments.
- Used for the deployment pipeline for the merge and TapTile apps.
- Pipelines build and publish starlink Helm charts to OCI, including a `build-charts` job.
- Runs deploy jobs `bff-deploy`, `attachments-deploy-k8s`, and `feworkgql-deploy-k8s` against the `ack-starlink-prod` cluster.
- Starlink's execution layer with TOTP protection, running jobs such as `db-migrator`, `deploy-multiapp`, and `env-sync`.
- Used for database restoration tasks and database sync operations; stores sync logs and dumps at `~/jdmj-sync-from-crush/`.
- The Jenkins pipeline syncs data from prd to alpha but does not include schema changes.
- The Jenkins x86_64 agent runs the dump-and-restore Ansible playbooks.
- Backup scripts are installed at `/data/backup-postgres/prd-blockbloom/dump-starlink-db.sh` and `/data/backup-postgres/alpha-blockbloom/dump-starlink-db.sh` on Jenkins; `backup-all.sh` auto-discovers all `dump-starlink-db.sh` scripts.
- Jenkins is the build executor, running on host `mbhpacker1`, using a shared Groovy library to report job state to Starlink.
- Jenkins sends package-update callbacks to Starlink from egress IP `111.200.218.82`.

## Credentials and secrets
- Registered credentials: `kubeconfig-ack-starlink-dev`, `kubeconfig-ack-starlink-prod`, `hs-devops-infra-sops-age-key`, and `liguanghui_ssh_key_at_git_7k7k_com`.
- Jenkins stores kubeconfig credentials for starlink, starorigin, and aigateway as Secret file type (`FileCredentialsImpl`).
- Kubeconfigs cover GKE clusters (starorigin-prod Autopilot, starorigin-dev Standard Zonal asia-northeast1-b) and Alibaba ACK clusters (starorigin dev/prod, starfamily devops, aigateway dev/prod), used by the hourly ping-clusters job and deploy pipelines.
- Jenkins uses the `kubeconfig-ack-starlink-prod` credential for the `ack-starlink-prod` cluster, mapped from `cluster: ack-starlink-prod` in `env-values.yaml`.
- Jenkins has an age key for decrypting SOPS-encrypted secrets; jobs decrypt `*.enc.yaml` files in-place with `sops -d -i` during deployments. The age key is a SOPS recipient for starlink deployments, alongside the admin key.
- The Jenkins agent has its own credentials for the `starfamily-registry`, so its builds are unaffected by local Mac keychain issues.
- `gcloud` and `gke-gcloud-auth-plugin` are not installed on the Jenkins host.

## Migration and network issues
- Jenkins at `10.100.27.205` performs migration from MinIO across a cross-VPC link, achieving ~47 KiB/s.
- Migration logs show 425 unexpected EOF errors and many connection reset by peer errors when downloading from MinIO.
- Jenkins is a CI server that cannot reliably download objects cross-VPC from MinIO and could not finish large file transfers.

## Permission behavior
- In Jenkins, a wrapper job's `build` step queues the downstream job as the Jenkins controller, so a user with Job/Build on the wrapper does not need permission on the underlying job.
- This build-step permission bypass only applies when users trigger the wrapper; direct triggering of the downstream job still requires Job/Build on that job.

memories.body:
# starflow

## Identity
- Workflow orchestration service for the Starlink game configuration platform; also described as a workflow system used by the starlink project.
- Written in Go, built with the Kratos microservice framework.
- Component/service in the starlink stack; also present in lsx-mjwd, yy-blockblast, and jade-mahjong (jdmj) stacks.
- Docker container image `starlink/starflow`, listening on HTTP port 8000.
- Runs two app instances: app-1 and app-2.

## Deployment
- Production: Aliyun Beijing ECS `archteam-starlink-blockblast-prod-app` (Intel Xeon 6982P-C 8-core, 32GB RAM, 200GB SSD), multi-node Docker Compose, Rocky Linux 9 x86_64.
- Production config on host 10.9.79.254; configs at `/data/starlink-blockblast-prod/config/starflow/` on `archteam-starlink-blockblast-prod-app-1`.
- Dev/test: `archteam-starlink-dev-all-in-one` (24 cores, 96GB RAM, 300GB SSD); also referenced as `starlink-dev-all-in-one`.
- Dev hardware: Aliyun ECS Intel Xeon 8-core, 32GB RAM, 500GB SSD for CI builds.
- Dev OS: macOS 14+ and Rocky Linux 9 (CI build server). Runtime: Rocky Linux 9 x86_64.
- Dev tools: Go 1.24, Kratos, Docker, Git, Visual Studio Code/GoLand, Jenkins.
- Runtime support software: Docker, PostgreSQL 16, Redis, Apache Kafka, OpenTelemetry.
- jade-mahjong production: hosts `archteam-starlink-jdmj-prod-1` and `archteam-starlink-jdmj-prod-2`, service_name `starflow`.
- yy-blockblast stack uses image `starflow:UNIVERSAL-block-blast-main-7ec95b35` and Postgres database `yy_blockblast_client`.

## Configuration
- Config in `config/starflow/config.yaml`; container config mounted from `./config/starflow/` to `/data/conf/`.
- Reads a directory of 5 structured YAML config files.
- Per-stack config.yaml points Postgres to Aliyun RDS and Redis to local per-stack containers.
- Required config fields: `data.bbc_kafka`, `external_system.publish_platform_gp`, `external_system.publish_platform_ios`, `yunxiao.solution_platform_2_0_33_security_token`, `yunxiao.solution_mini_bundle_auto_solution_platform`, `pipeline.layer_base_upgrade` (including `default_branch`), `media`, `external_system.automated_testing`, `aws`, and `testing_platform_auth_token`.
- Missing required fields cause startup panic `配置缺失`.
- `testing_platform_auth_token` is defined in the four blockblast stacks (lby, lhh, wz, yy) with shared dev value `d6b6c83e-3c49-46ed-9445-2bc587b928e6`.
- Stack deployed with docker-compose, uses openresty as reverse proxy, configured via `.env`.
- `kafka.yaml` has `bbc_kafka.enabled: false`, which disables KafkaBbcSubscriberService and prevents consumption of `feature_conflict_way` CDC events.

## Endpoints / access
- Public HTTP endpoint: `starlink.youxi123.com`; it is the HTTP sync API called by Vector on app-1 for solution and mini-bundle events.
- Inner HTTPS endpoint: `starlink-inner.youxi123.com`, reachable from the starlink-blockblast-prod app host.
- Public endpoint is not reachable from the prod app host (resolves to host-gateway 172.17.0.1 with no listener on port 80).
- Also hosted at `https://pm-1-dev.hs99.vip/`.
- Proxied by openresty; receives HTTP callbacks; receives package build callbacks from Jenkins.
- Image `main-9794c425` does not expose the `/flow/metrics` Prometheus endpoint (returns 404).

## Dependencies / integrations
- Calls downstream services via HTTP APIs: bbc, hfrog, user.
- Downstream dependencies include Postgres, Redis, Kafka, Jenkins, publish platforms, S3, OTLP, and Yunxiao.
- Consumes BlockBlast prd CDC Kafka topics; consumes `feature_conflict_way` via KafkaBbcSubscriberService.
- `st_workflow` table stores workflow data with a `list_result_layer` JSONB column.
- Loki logs record `PackageUpdateCallback` failures.

## Images / versions
- Prod image tag: `UNIVERSAL-mahjong-wonders-main-177320c3`; previous working dev tag: `feat-middle-1.0-94908c6e`.
- yy-blockblast image: `starflow:UNIVERSAL-block-blast-main-7ec95b35`.
- jade-mahjong image `main-9794c425` lacks `/flow/metrics`.

## Misc
- Planned Go Kratos service that ding will proxy to.
- Config requires keys `data.bbc_kafka`, `external_system.automated_testing`, `aws`, `media`, and `pipeline.layer_base_upgrade`.

memories.body:
# RMB (Recall Memory Bank)

## Identity
- RMB is the user's personal long-term memory system / memory agent backend / skills registry for AI-agent conversations: self-hosted, single-owner, URI-transparent, serving all AI agents. Previously named mem9, mem-colinleefish-com, mem-colinleefish, mypast.
- Source: GitHub `colinleefish/rmb`; local checkout `/Users/liguanghui/Virginia/colinleefish/rmb` (also written `.../colinleefish-rmb`). The repo also serves as static assets repository.
- Production: `https://rmb.colinleefish.com`; Docker-only deployment (`make deploy`), not Vercel. Docker image `registry.cn-beijing.aliyuncs.com/colinleefish/rmb:main` (tagged by git SHA). Also distributed via re-mem-ber.me, GitHub Releases, and R2.
- HTTP basic auth: `rmb:sVf3^n5ht`. Server Postgres: `rmb_db` at `127.0.0.1:5432`, user `rmb_user`, password `0c2791d39900292afc7948f520bc0aa3`.
- Docs: VitePress site, bilingual English/Chinese under `docs/concept` and `docs/zh/concept`.
- Person association in rmb data: 刘欣欣, system ID 62, workcode 001971 (also appears in rmb mock data).

## Components & install paths
- Stack: Go (Gin, GORM) backend/CLI; web UI is Next.js/React served from embedded static build under `internal/http/static/web/` (assets under `_next/`, UI also at `/ui`); server uses PostgreSQL + pgvector (Postgres 18.3, pgvector 0.8.2); desktop uses SQLite via mattn/go-sqlite3 with external-content FTS5 tables `scenes_fts`, `atoms_fts`, `memories_fts`.
- Targets macOS (arm64) and Windows (x64); Linux possibly later.
- Binaries: `rmb` (CLI), `rmbd`/`rmbd-desktop` (daemon), `rmb-app` (desktop app), under `~/.rmb/bin`; `~/.rmb/bin/rmb` is the stable absolute path used by agent hooks. Client config: `~/.rmb/config.yaml` or `~/.rmb.conf`; desktop config at `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/config.yaml`; desktop DB at `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/data/rmb.db`; daemon log at `.../logs/rmbd.log` (auto-rotates at 5 MB). `install.sh` installs binary and writes client config.
- Desktop app: RMB Desktop 0.2.0, hand-packed macOS app, installed at `/Applications/RMB Desktop.app`, bundle id `me.remember.rmb`; menu-bar app (no Dock icon), single-instance lock; codesigned/notarized with Developer ID Application certificate GUANGHUI LI (N4YPJBRBN4). LaunchAgents: `me.remember.rmb`, `me.remember.rmbd`, `me.remember.rmb.login`, `me.remember.rmbd-e2e`.
- The project is being migrated from Tauri to a Go shell; tray/daemon management via Go + launchd. Start-on-login uses `internal/launchatlogin` (not Tauri); Windows start-on-login returns 'only supported on macOS'. Tray polls `/healthz` every 5s and auto-restarts failed daemon.
- No auto-update (Tauri updater inactive); manual DMG/GitHub Release updates. Bootstrap self-heals sidecars by checking executable magic (Mach-O/MZ/ELF); cannot detect a replaced-but-valid Mach-O binary.
- Web UI: `http://127.0.0.1:19019/ui/`; skills list page and memories page exist; UI component `rmb-ui` exists (includes `RecallRuleCopy`).

## Architecture, pipeline & data model
- Full pipeline: L0 capture -> L1 atoms -> L2 scenes -> L3 memories -> L4 embeddings (also called T0 turns -> T1 atoms -> T2 scenes -> T3 memories). Summaries: `sessions.abstract`, `scenes.abstract/body`, `memories.abstract/body`. T3 worker polls every 5 minutes and distills atoms across sessions into shared buckets (`rmb://profile`, `rmb://entities/...`, `rmb://preferences/...`, and events).
- Unified taxonomy categories: profile, preferences, entities, events. URI space is flat: `rmb://turns/<uuid>`, `rmb://atoms/<uuid>`, `rmb://scenes/<uuid>`, `rmb://sessions/<uuid>`, `rmb://entities/<slug>`, `rmb://preferences/<slug>`, `rmb://events/<slug>`, `rmb://skills/<slug>`, `rmb://profile`, `rmb://agent`. `rmb://sessions/<key>/` is only a navigation view, not a path prefix. Skills normalize to `rmb://skills/<slug>`, versioned by `bundle_sha256`.
- Turns belong to sessions in `session_turns` (session_id FK) while the URI layer stays flat; `rmb meta` on a turn returns its session_id. Sessions and turns sync by `session_key` and turn id; `turn_count` is computed at read time, not stored on the session row. Server requires UUID session IDs for uploads.
- Atoms: flat URIs `rmb://atoms/<uuid>` (after migration 00017, atoms.id is UUID PK, `uri` column removed). Atoms table has Category (`profile`/`preferences`/`entities`/`events`) and Topic (`scene_name · slug`); provenance in `source_turn_ids` UUID array (~4% cite multiple source turns). T1 extract batches up to 8 turns per LLM call, mapping 0-based `source_turn_indices` to IDs.
- Scenes: URI deterministic UUIDv5 from `session_id` + `display_name`; T2 overwrites same row on rebuild (no version history); a session can have multiple scenes. `display_name` is a short human-readable title; abstract is the embedded search field (design expects abstract ~100 tokens).
- Memories: append-first/versioned, keyed by URI, single active row (`superseded_at IS NULL`); `persistMemory` supersedes old rows with same URI, version+1. Events are immutable and first-write-wins. Human corrections are additive overlays (corrections table) and outrank machine facts; newest-wins, no hard-delete.
- Aliases: alias/canonical entity resolution via `aliases` and `alias_candidates`; alias-suggest worker is pair-centric, default cosine floor 0.82; `cname` aliases merge into canonical entities with flat-star invariant (no alias chains). Dedicated entity aliases registry was dropped in migration 00012. The recall path does not yet resolve aliases.
- Recall: hybrid vector + FTS + RRF; `rmb search` is purely semantic (RRF 70/30) with no time weighting, so it must not be used to determine 'the latest'. Default retrieval is flat RRF; pyramid drill-down is manual/on-demand. Timeline queries use `rmb ls rmb://events/` (formerly `rmb tree`): orders by `updated_at DESC`, cap 200. Only active memories are embedded and used in recall. Recall stats are keyed by version-less URI and persist across versions; slug drift creates a new URI and resets counters. Server-side stats recorded via `rmb search/cat/meta` (migration `00023_recall_stats.sql`). Scene stats are per-incarnation (scenes are UUID-keyed, never versioned); skills share slug-keyed URI stats across versions.
- Embeddings: fixed 1024-dim vectors (vector(1024), HNSW cosine); dimension locked after onboarding and cannot be changed without re-embedding all memories. Models seen: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small and Volces Ark doubao-embedding-vision.
- LLM: current provider DeepSeek (`api.deepseek.com`, model `deepseek-v4-flash`) via `llm.api_base`; default LLM timeout 300s (changed from 45s in 0.1.22). Volces Ark (`ark-code-latest`) has also been reported. Pipeline has self-healing retries; LLM failures tracked in `pipeline_state.l1_last_error`. No procedural memory track yet; skills exist but are not procedural memory.
- API: snake_case JSON, server-side pagination for sessions/pipeline/corrections. Default concurrency limits: L2 max 16, L1 max 64. Two daemons on same DB file can create duplicate atoms (assume one daemon per DB).
- Sync: rows synced by id, provenance unioned, then re-distilled. Cross-instance behavior uses client-to-remote HTTP API; no BitTorrent/DHT code.

## Deployment & ops
- Production host: SSH `root@rmb.colinleefish.com`, config `/opt/rmb/.env`, runtime bundle `/app/rmb` (docker-compose, .env, config/Caddyfile; no git checkout). Caddy is configured; server daemon runs on port 19019 (test daemon on 127.0.0.1:19097); desktop daemon at 127.0.0.1:19019; health endpoint `/healthz`. Earlier server default bind was 127.0.0.1:8080; public binds require auth; 32 MiB upload limit.
- Also deployed on remote host `rmb-desktop`; previously reported as two instances on `182.92.114.13:18080/18081`.
- Server exposes GET `/api/v1/browse/...`; desktop exposes POST `/api/v1/sessions/{key}/upload`; desktop and server share session UUIDs. Production metrics from one point: ~1,258 scenes across 314 sessions.
- rmb.colinleefish.com also hosts the pbp stock sync project: `/app/pbp` in Docker, Postgres 18 with network_mode host on 127.0.0.1:5432; pbp_db, user pbp_user_rw, 15-table schema at rmb.colinleefish.com:5432; remote connections require SSL with wildcard `*.colinleefish.com` cert auto-renewed weekly via cron. The server also runs stock/fund/valuation/financials ingestion with checkpointing in `sync.sync_state`.
- No one-click server<->desktop migration; pg_dump from server won't load into SQLite desktop. Cross-device sync is a deferred paid feature (`sync.re-mem-ber.me`); syncing rmb.db via iCloud/Dropbox is planned as unsafe. Without an app update, backfill preserves session keys, content, turn order, and re-distilled memories/skills, but not original turn timestamps or bit-identical old T3 text.
- Default Postgres DSN uses sslmode=disable.

## CLI & integrations
- CLI commands: `search`, `cat`, `ls`, `meta`, `pull`, `put`, `setup`, `hook-submit`, `version`. `tree` was removed in favor of `ls`; skills sync via `rmb pull/put` on `rmb://skills/` (replaces `rmb skill pull`). CLI is not on PATH by default; `version` prints `rmb dev` instead of a real semver. The CLI is a pure HTTP API client and does not touch the database directly.
- Config resolution order: `RMB_CONFIG`, `RMB_CONF`, `~/.rmb.conf`, `~/.rmb/config.yaml`. Empty `RMB_URL` env var can make the CLI appear to ignore config; repo `.env` sets `RMB_CONFIG=.env` and overrides when run from the repo directory.
- No-args run: seeds/injects agent guide (`rmb://agent`) into every agent context at session start and prints profile. Server CLI no-args bootstraps profile, agent guide, and skills catalog (20+ skills, e.g. ascii-diagram, humanizer, JumpServer).
- `rmb setup --agent=opencode/pi` installs capture hooks; setup supports detect/preview/apply for Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi; preview-before-apply required for config changes.
- Agent guide is embedded `agent_guide.md`, mirrored into DB by `UpsertAgentGuide`; treated as system docs (excluded from browse counts and memory category overviews). On fresh DB, migration 00006 inserts `rmb://agent` v1 and UpsertAgentGuide immediately supersedes to v2, so the version counter is permanently off by one.
- Hook specifics: Cursor hook mechanism is `rmb-hook-dual` calling `rmb-desktop`; it merges `rmb hook-submit` into `hooks.stop` of `~/.cursor/hooks.json` (only `hooks.stop` modified; `timeout: 15` added when missing); hook status is configured only when `hooks.stop` contains it. Cursor/Codex stop-event hooks run `rmb hook-submit` (`--source=cursor` / `--source=codex`); Cursor skips aborted turns. Claude Code integration needs `settings.json` + a recall file. Server has hook-submit parsers for Codex, OpenCode, Pi.
- Agent guide is fetched by Cursor, Claude, Codex, Pi via the server's inspect cat endpoint. Session capture supported from five agents (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi); working integrations named for OpenCode and Pi; integration pages exist for Cursor, OpenCode, Pi.

## Known issues
- Go unit tests only; lacks HTTP handler, UI, and integration tests.
- `scenes_fts` FTS5 external-content table can corrupt under concurrent L2 writes (`persistScenes` deletes the FTS entry after content upsert, even on first-time creation), causing SQLITE_CORRUPT; user's `~/Downloads` rmb.db was once corrupted (0 scenes, 45 zombie running sessions) before the fix was applied.
- TestWritePlist is environment-dependent and fails when `/Applications/RMB Desktop.app` exists, making `make test` red.
- HTTP body handling: v0.1.18 streamed response bodies; v0.1.19 read through 2 KiB LimitReader; v0.1.20 reads full bodies while capping error snippets at 2 KiB.

memories.body:
# Codekeeper

- Codekeeper is a database used by the fakeuser service and also by BBC.
- Codekeeper is the dedicated database for user accounts; it stores avatar IDs and roles.
- User accounts live in the `avatar` table of each project's codekeeper database, e.g.:
  - Starlink: `prd_taptile_codekeeper.avatar`
  - Block Crush: `prd_blockcrush_codekeeper.avatar`
  - Dev/backfill: `lby_blockcrush_codekeeper` on the `starlink-dev-all-in-one` RDS instance, `avatar` table.

## Avatar backfill
- Missing art accounts are created by INSERTing into each project's `*_codekeeper.avatar` table, comparing JDMJ's 143 art personnel workcodes.
- New avatar rows:
  - copy `dingding_name` and `workcode` from JDMJ
  - set `role`/`dept_info` to empty JSONB
  - leave `email`, `username`, `avatar` empty
  - set `create_avatar_id=1`, `update_avatar_id=0`, `status=0`
  - auto-increment `id`
- Personal info (`email`, `username`) on new avatar rows is filled after the user's first SSO login.

## Authority sync / lookups
- Authority sync looks up the target project's `avatar.id` by `workcode`, because avatar IDs differ per project.
- In Block Crush, the `codekeeper.avatar` table has no unique constraint on `workcode` or `dingding_name`, so duplicate user rows are possible.
