memories.abstract: Starlink is HungryStudio's game configuration and A/B testing platform, supporting multiple games across dev, alpha, and prod environments on Alibaba Cloud, with services like BBC, GQL, and Starflow, using PostgreSQL, Kafka, and Docker/K8s.
memories.body:
# Starlink (星链)

Starlink is a game configuration management and A/B testing platform at HungryStudio. It hosts multiple games (blockcrush, jdmj, blockbloom, gogoblast, merge, tap-tile, stp, blockblast, blockmj, mjwd, sandcrush, pm-1-dev) and provides services for creative workflows, feature configuration, and release pipelines.

## Infrastructure

- **Cloud**: Alibaba Cloud (Aliyun) and UCloud; production on Alibaba Cloud ACK (Kubernetes) clusters `ack-starlink-dev` and `ack-starlink-prod`.
- **Hosts**: Dev all-in-one host `archteam-starlink-dev-all-in-one` (10.100.48.251 / 10.100.64.132), production hosts for merge/taptile (`archteam-starlink-merge-prod-1/2`, `archteam-starlink-taptile-prod-1/2`), BlockBlast app hosts (`archteam-starlink-prd-blockblast-app-1/2/3` at 10.100.30.117-119), and JDMJ prod hosts (`archteam-starlink-jdmj-prod-1/2`).
- **Networking**: Public gateway `starlink.youxi123.com` (also `starlink.hs99.vip`), inner gateway `starlink-inner.youxi123.com`, read-only domains `starlink-ro.youxi123.com` and `starlink-ro-internal.youxi123.com`. ALBs and SLBs used for load balancing.
- **Deployment**: Two paradigms: Docker Compose (~95% of environments, under `/data/starlink-{ns}-{game}/`) and Kubernetes/Helmfile (growing, namespaces `starlink-{game}-{env}`). CI/CD via Jenkins (jobs for gql, bbc, frontend, db-migrator) and Ansible playbooks.

## Environments

- Matrix of games × environments × services (14+ services per cell).
- 14 dev environments (dev, kwd, yy, yl, cyx, hyx, lxy, lby, mx, dwb, lgh, lhh, lsx, wz) and 6 game variants.
- Environments: dev, alpha, prod, LGH (test). Production per game (e.g., `starlink-prd-blockblast`).
- URL conventions: `https://{env}-{game}.hs99.vip` for Compose, `https://{game}-{env}.t.hs99.vip` for K8s, `*.d.hs99.vip` for dev.

## Services & Components

- Core services: `bbc` (Python backend), `gql` (GraphQL), `frontend` (SolutionHub), `starflow`, `ding` (OpenResty gateway), `hfrog` (artifact storage), `pgpour` (CDC), `vector` (log shipper), `fakeuser`, `starlai`, `rustyme`, `staroriginweb`, `attachments`, `lowcodegql`, `bff`.
- Frontend apps: block-blast, block-mahjong, mahjong-wonders, block-crush.
- Container images from `registry.hs99.vip/starlink/*` and `starfamily-registry-vpc.cn-beijing.cr.aliyuncs.com/starlink/*`.

## Databases (PostgreSQL)

- **Dev RDS**: `starlink-dev-all-in-one.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com` (PostgreSQL 16), hosts databases like `lgh_blockcrush_client`, `dwb_blockcrush_client`, `pm1_dev_client`, `dev_blockblast_client`. User `solutionhub_dev`.
- **Alpha RDS**: `archteam-starlink-alpha-pg.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com` (contains `alpha_blockblast_client`, `alpha_mjwd_client`, etc.).
- **Production RDS**: Per-game instances, e.g., `archteam-starlink-blockcrush-pg16.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com` (prd_blockcrush_client), `archteam-starlink-blockblast-prod.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com` (hs_client_db, hs_code_keeper_db), `archteam-starlink-gogoblast-prd.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com`, `archteam-starlink-prd-shared-services.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com` (fework_prd_db).
- **Naming**: Each cell has `{env}_{game}_client` and `{env}_{game}_codekeeper` databases. Shared-services RDS hosts `fework_prd_db` (app_info, app_login tables).
- **Access**: Application user `starlink_user` owns many databases; superuser `postgres` on some instances. Credentials stored in `e.credentials/starlink/`.

## Kafka

- **Brokers**: Production: 10.9.73.159:9092, 10.9.7.152:9092, 10.9.136.40:9092. Dev: 10.9.169.2:9092, 10.9.131.68:9092, 10.9.103.246:9092 (plaintext).
- **Topic naming**: `biz.starlink.{game}.{env}.public.{table}` or `starlink.{game}.{env}.{schema}.{table}`. Uses `prd` (not `prod`) and `lgh` for test.
- **CDC**: pgpour streams PostgreSQL changes to Kafka topics (e.g., `starlink.blockcrush.lgh.public._pm_idea_details_enriched`).
- **Outbox**: `_pm_idea_flow_outbox_event` table; topics configured via `KAFKA_PLAN_STATE_SYNC_TOPICS`.

## Storage

- **MinIO**: Server at 10.254.3.107; artifacts stored in buckets like `starlink-blockcrush-pm-artifacts`, `starlink-artifacts-prd`, `starlink-jdmj-pm-artifacts-public`.
- **Aliyun OSS**: Migration target; two-bucket architecture per game (private and public). Credentials in `e.credentials/starlink/pm-artifacts-oss.txt`.
- **Attachments**: Served via `/attachments/` path, with presigned URLs from hfrog.

## Other

- **Identity**: SSO via HungryStudio accounts; app ID `starlink_pm`; permissions stored in `avatar.role` JSONB.
- **Runbooks**: Manual onboarding for new games (schema seed, env config, Kafka topics, DNS/SSO).
- **Cost**: Starlink is a cost group in Aliyun `caikuai-cn` account; monthly spend ~¥12.9K–13.2K.
- **Project location**: `/Users/liguanghui/hs.projects/starlink`; includes `hs-code-keeper` repo with `bbc` directory.
- **Security note**: `db-migrator vars.yml` contains plaintext DB passwords (risk).

memories.body:
# starlink-dev-all-in-one

## Overview
- Consolidated dev environment for the Starlink project, comprising a host (ECS) and an Aliyun RDS PostgreSQL instance.
- Serves as the single target database for all Starlink dev-environment game databases.

## Host (archteam-starlink-dev-all-in-one)
- **IPs**: Public `39.106.98.1`, private `10.100.48.251` (also reachable at `10.100.64.132`).
- **OS**: Rocky Linux 9.
- **Docker**: 29.5.2 with containerd snapshotter (overlayfs storage driver).
- **Resources**: 60 GB RAM, 189 GB free disk (total disk 300 GB).
- **Containers**: Runs 383 Docker containers named `starlink-<user>-<game>-<service>-1` for many team members.
- **PostgreSQL tools**: 16.14 client tools (pg_dump, pg_restore, psql) at `/usr/bin`, package root `/usr/pgsql-16`.
- **Key containers**: `starlink-dwb-blockcrush-pgpour-1` (pgpour CDC), `starlink-hyx-blockblast-starflow-1`, and mx-blockcrush services (frontend, bbc, gql, swagger) plus an openresty gateway.
- **Images**: Has `confluentinc/cp-kafka:7.6.0` Docker image.
- **Network**: Sits on the 10.9 network (also on 10.100 network).
- **Vector configs**: Hosts at `/data/starlink-dwb-blockblast/config/vector/` and `/data/starlink-dwb-mjwd/config/vector/`.
- **Credentials**: Holds Aliyun ACR credentials.
- **Repos**: Uses Grafana RPM repo via Aliyun mirror.
- **Config files**: `env.yaml` is minified (based on 2026-07-29 BBC env cleanup); `secrets.enc.yaml` contains `DING_ACCESS_SEC`, `GIT_TOKEN`, `JENKINS_API_TOKEN`.
- **JumpServer**: Asset name `archteam-starlink-dev-all-in-one`, reachable at `10.100.48.251` via `jump.hs99.vip`; account `osadmin` (also `root` on Linux).
- **ECS instance ID**: `i-2ze0hhr20hyun2jo06y0`; DNS alias `lby-blockcrush.hs99.vip`.

## RDS Instance (starlink-dev-all-in-one.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com)
- **Type**: Aliyun RDS PostgreSQL 16.13, region cn-beijing, account `caikuai-cn`.
- **Endpoint**: `starlink-dev-all-in-one.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com:5432` (internal address `10.100.48.255:5432`).
- **Databases**: Hosts 133 databases totaling 136 GB after the 2026-05-26 migration (initially 100 GB storage, exhausted during restore).
- **Ownership**: Databases owned by `solutionhub_dev` role.
- **Replication**: `wal_level=logical` (required by pgpour); `max_replication_slots=16`, `max_wal_senders=64`, `max_logical_replication_workers=32`; `pglogical` extension available.
- **Specific DBs**: Includes `dwb_blockcrush_client`, `dwb_blockcrush_codekeeper`, and hosts both DWB and MX blockcrush environments.
- **Credentials**: Stored in `hungrystudio/e.credentials/starlink/shared.txt`; JumpServer account `starlink_readonly`.

## Databases
- Naming convention: `{namespace}_{game}_{role}` or `{initials}_{game}_{service}`.
- Games: `blockblast`, `blockcrush`, `blockmj`, `mjwd`, `sandcrush`.
- Services/roles: `client`, `codekeeper`, `hfrog`, `starflow`.
- Developer namespaces (16): `cyx`, `dev`, `dwb`, `hyx`, `kwd`, `lby`, `lgh`, `lhh`, `lsx`, `lxy`, `mx`, `ro`, `wz`, `yl`, `yy` (and possibly others).
- Example databases: `pm1_dev_client`, `pm1_dev_codekeeper`, `dwb_blockcrush_client`, `lgh_blockcrush_client`, `yl_blockcrush_client`.

## Host Services & Configuration
- Runs many Docker Compose stacks (approx. 57–68 stacks, 300+ containers; actual 383 containers).
- Services include: `gql`, `hfrog`, `starflow`, `pgpour`, `nginx`, `Alloy`, `Vector`, `Prometheus`, `Loki`.
- Observability: Alloy with business labels, `loki.process`, Prometheus scrape for gql/hfrog/starflow; metrics carry host label.
- Deploy script substitutes `__HOSTNAME__` with hostname at apply time.
- Nginx with per-user vhost configs for blockblast.
- Hosts personal dev environments: lby (220xx), lgh (240xx), lhh (280xx), dwb (210xx), yy (230xx).
- Deployments under `/data/` as `starlink-<initials>-<game>/` Docker Compose stacks sharing external network `starlink_network`.
- Specific paths:
  - `/data/starlink-lby-blockblast`
  - `/data/starlink-lgh-blockcrush/config/bbc/env.dev`
  - `/data/starlink-lhh-blockcrush/config/bbc/env.dev`
  - `/data/starlink-<ns>-<game>/config/bbc/env.dev` (BBC env config)
  - `/data/locallogin-*` (locallogin stacks)
- Hosts the environment allocation matrix.
- Automated CI/Ansible deploy host: `10.254.20.143`.

## Notes
- The host and RDS are distinct entities but share the same logical name `starlink-dev-all-in-one`.
- The RDS is the consolidated target for all Starlink dev game databases.
- The host is also used for restoring target databases.

# prd_blockblast_client

## Overview
- **prd_blockblast_client** is the production PostgreSQL database for the Block Blast (blockblast) game.
- It is labeled `prd_blockblast_client` in the repo; the actual database name is `hs_client_db`.
- It is the user's main PostgreSQL database and is used in Starlink Blockblast.
- It is hosted on Aliyun RDS (target database for Starlink blockblast client data).

## Schema
- Contains **120 tables**.
- Has **4 schemas**: `public`, `uums`, `yunxiao`, `starorigin`.
- Approximate data size: **10GB**.
- The `public.estwftype` enum has an extra value `RELEASE_SHUTTLE_BUS_FLOW` compared to `prd_blockmahjong_client`.
- No PM tables exist, so `sea-orm-cli` does not generate PM entities for this database.

## Hosting & Endpoints
- Primary endpoint: `archteam-starlink-blockblast-prod.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com`
- Read-only replica endpoint: `archteam-starlink-blockblast-prod-ro.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com`
- Also referenced as hosted on `starlink-dev-all-in-one`.

## Features
- In `feature_config`, the same `feature_id` exists for multiple platforms (GP and IOS).
- Includes the **release shuttle bus flow** (发版班车流) feature with tables `st_wf_release_shuttle_bus_flow` and `st_wf_rsbf_period`.

## Notes
- This is a production database; treat with care.

memories.abstract: mypast (mem9) is the user's personal long-term memory system for AI agents: a Go/Postgres/pgvector app with a CLI, HTTP API, and embedded Next.js UI, deployed at mem.colinleefish.com, using a T0-T3 distillation pyramid.
memories.body:
# mypast (mem9)

mypast is the user's personal long-term memory system for AI-agent conversations. It is a Go project hosted at [github.com/colinleefish/mypast](https://github.com/colinleefish/mypast) and deployed in production at [https://mem.colinleefish.com](https://mem.colinleefish.com) (UI at `/ui/`). It is also referred to as **mem9**.

## Architecture

- **Tech stack**: Go 1.26, Gin, GORM, goose migrations, PostgreSQL/pgvector, Docker Compose, Caddy, PostgreSQL 18. Uses an OpenAI-compatible LLM client.
- **Build**: Three-stage Docker build (node:22 for UI, golang:1.26 for Go, alpine runtime) that embeds the static Next.js UI into the Go binary. Frontend lives in `ui-next` and uses pnpm.
- **Deployment**: Container image pushed to Aliyun (Alibaba Cloud) Container Registry (ACR). Production uses basic auth with username `mypast`. `deploy.sh` does `git reset --hard <pushed-SHA>` on production, so whatever lands on main goes live. GitHub environment named `production`. Deploy workflow: `make ci`, push to main, then `make deploy`; deploy script sets `https_proxy=http://localhost:1080` during git fetch. No GitHub Actions; agent-driven CI/deploy over SSH.
- **Local dev**: Local Postgres at `127.0.0.1:5432`. Repo on user's machine at `/Users/liguanghui/Virginia/colinleefish/mypast`. Server defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:8080`, overridable via `MYPAST_URL` or `~/.mypast.conf`.

## Pipeline

Four-tier distillation pyramid:
- **T0** – Ingestion (no LLM), raw turns. Immutable `session_turns`; ingests from Cursor and Claude Code hooks via an upload API.
- **T1** – Extraction (atoms). Uses chat LLM; explicitly skips skill attachments as non-durable session state. Append-only (re-extraction requires deleting old atoms).
- **T2** – Scene construction (scenes). Processes one session at a time; groups atoms by `scene_name` into batches; scene URIs are deterministic UUIDv5 from (session_id, scene name), with upsert-and-prune on rebuild.
- **T3** – Memory rollup (long-term memories). Rolls up atoms globally by (category, slug) into versioned memory rows (`superseded_at`), linking scenes via `source_scene_uris`. Uses temperature-0 to skip unchanged versions.

All stages except T0 use the chat LLM. The embed worker uses a separate embedding provider (BigModel embedding-3 at dimensions:1024). `pipeline_state` keeps one row per session tracking t1/t2/t3 worker statuses (idle/pending/running/failed).

## Data Model

- **Memory categories**: profile, preferences, entities, events.
- **Addressing**: `rmb://` URIs (e.g., `rmb://events/...`, `rmb://corrections/...`). Logical URIs like `rmb://profile` and `rmb://preferences/<slug>`; inspection routes these to the memories table with active-row filtering.
- **Corrections**: Sibling artifacts; CLI supports attaching via `correction add` (aliases: `correct`/`fix`).
- **Aliases**: Flat-star topology – any number of aliases point to one canonical, depth fixed at 1, cycles impossible by construction. Alias generation is human-authored for the current milestone; a scaffolded `alias_candidates` table is reserved for a future propose-and-confirm worker.
- **Versioning**: Memories are versioned; each rollup supersedes the previous row and inserts a new version. T3 memories are versioned by insert + supersede, never updated in place.
- **Raw turns**: T0 raw turns are never rewritten; they remain the ground-truth evidence chain.
- **Storage**: Postgres database named `mypast_dev` (misleading leftover from default config) holds all production data. Memories table (migration 00003) stores versioned rows with `superseded_at` and partial unique indexes on `uri` and `(category, slug)`. Pipeline state stored in Postgres for resume after restarts.

## Retrieval

Progressive disclosure: search abstracts, then drill into scene body, atoms, and raw turns. Scenes have two layers: a ~100-token abstract for search/filter and a full Markdown body with the narrative. Recall uses hybrid vector + FTS search with RRF fusion over a flat candidate set; hierarchical score-propagation deferred. Uses Ebbinghaus decay curves for forgetting.

## CLI & Configuration

- Installed at `~/.mypast/bin/mypast` (also referenced as `~/.mypast/mypast`). Built into `./bin/mypast` via `make build`. PATH in `~/.zshrc`; refreshed via `make build && cp bin/mypast ~/.mypast/bin/mypast`.
- Config at `~/.mypast.conf` holds production credentials from `/opt/mypast/.env` (contains `MYPAST_URL` and basic auth credentials).
- Hooks configured in `~/.cursor/hooks.json` and `~/.claude/settings.json`, both pointing at the mypast CLI. Integrates with Claude Code via a Stop hook. `hook-submit` feature submits agent conversations to the mypast upload API.
- CLI subcommands never connect to the local database; they use the HTTP client when `MYPAST_URL` is set and error out when it is absent. The `serve` command always connects to the local database regardless of `MYPAST_URL`.
- Inspect commands: `cat`, `meta`, `tree` for sessions and atoms.
- API caps list endpoints at 300 rows server-side.

## Status & Tooling

- As of 2026-06-10: T1, T2, and T3 are implemented and running in production. T1 extraction works; T2 and T3 are active. ~3,800 atoms across 122 sessions (2026-06-07); T0 raw turns ~948 (2026-06-10).
- Known open items: M1 (auth-env footgun), M2 (FTS index expression mismatch), M5 (slug-less atom drop).
- T3 profile category over-absorbs noise; preferences category empty. T3 distillation currently routes preference-like and third-party facts into the profile singleton instead of `preferences/` and `entities/`.
- CI runs `go test ./...` with no database; tests are pure unit tests.
- Eval harness exists to measure recall quality; `scripts/eval_queries.txt` contains placeholder eval queries. `mypast eval` runs FTS recall probes, exits non-zero on regression; currently passes 8/8.
- Legacy summarizer writes `overview_text`, to be retired in Phase E.
- Locked consolidation policy: append-first T1 with opt-in merge, versioned T3 memories (superseded_at), insert-only events, and `mypast eval` for drift detection.

## Documentation

- Design: `docs/design-l0-l4.zh.md`; consolidation review: `docs/memory-consolidation-review.zh.md` (cites arXiv:2605.12978).
- Roadmap: `docs/plan.md` (phases B–E and post-pyramid backlog).
- Agent guide: `docs/cli-agent-guide.md`.

memories.abstract: rmbd is the Go backend daemon for RMB Desktop, managing memories/embeddings, serving UI/API on 127.0.0.1:19019, with SQLite storage and a memory pipeline.
memories.body:
# rmbd

## Overview
- rmbd is the Go backend daemon of RMB Desktop (rmb-desktop), serving as the memory backend daemon and UI server on the user's laptop.
- It runs locally at `http://127.0.0.1:19019` and is managed by launchd on macOS (LaunchAgent `com.remember.rmbd.plist` or `me.remember.rmbd`).
- It hosts the PI agent and serves the dashboard UI; the web UI is embedded in the daemon (built from `webui/dist` into `internal/http/static/web/`).
- It is the daemon component of RMB, managing memories and embeddings.
- Current version: v0.2.2 (built with CGO_ENABLED=1 and the `sqlite_fts5` tag).

## Architecture
- Written in Go, built with CGO and sqlite.
- Internal packages: `db`, `config`, `worker/scene`, and `cmd/rmbd`.
- Stateless-restart-safe daemon; all state is stored in SQLite on disk.
- Main entrypoint is `cmd/rmbd/main.go`.
- Configurable pipeline (L1/L2 concurrency) and a local HTTP server.

## Storage
- Uses SQLite with WAL mode and `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transactions.
- Uses `mattn/go-sqlite3`; DSN uses `_txlock=immediate` to avoid WAL `SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT` write contention.
- SQLite database stored at `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/data/rmb.db`.
- Uses goose for SQLite schema migrations (00001–00006), run on every daemon startup; migrations are embedded SQL in `internal/db/migrations/`.
- Schema changes ship inside the new rmbd binary and apply automatically on daemon restart; critical coupling between rmbd version and schema version.
- Embeddings stored as a BLOB column.
- Vector recall uses sqlite-vec's `vec_distance_cosine` scalar function on the existing embedding BLOB column (not a vec0 virtual table with MATCH); returns only top-k rows.
- Dynamic scene chunking.

## Networking & Authentication
- Listens on `127.0.0.1:19019` by default; bind address configurable via `RMB_ADDR` environment variable.
- To start on `0.0.0.0`, requires `USERNAME`/`PASSWORD` or `RMB_USERNAME`/`RMB_PASSWORD` environment variables.
- Uses HTTP Basic Auth for UI and API; `/healthz` is left unauthenticated when bound to `0.0.0.0`.
- Serves plain HTTP (not HTTPS), so Basic Auth credentials are transmitted in cleartext on a LAN.

## API & Endpoints
- Web UI accessible at `http://127.0.0.1:19019/ui/`.
- Exposes `/api/v1/version` and `/api/v1/config`.
- Exposes `/healthz` reporting status, SQLite version, and vector version.
- Exposes `/api/v1/onboarding/status` and `/api/v1/onboarding/complete`, backed by the `onboarding.complete` file in the rmb-desktop support directory.
- Onboarding can be bypassed by creating the `onboarding.complete` file or calling `POST /api/v1/onboarding/complete`.
- Debug endpoints: `/api/v1/debug/logs` (backed by a 2000-line ring buffer, tees all slog output to stderr), `/debug/workers`, `/debug/in-flight`, `/debug/pipeline/stuck`, and `browse/sessions/{key}` (pipeline_state.t2_last_error holds the actual L2 error text in SQLite).

## Memory Pipeline
- rmbd is a memory pipeline system with L1 extract, L2 scene, and L3 memory workers.
- Uses vector embeddings for memory.
- Stores memories in categories: profile, events, preferences, entities.
- Workers poll on intervals: L1/L2 every 15s, L3 every 5min, embed every 30s.
- L1 and L2 worker concurrency defaults are 64 and 16.
- DB connection pool ceiling is derived from L1/L2 concurrency config plus fixed workers and HTTP headroom.
- Runs T3 bucket distillation/rollup.
- Makes HTTPS requests to the LLM API at `stargate.youxi123.com`.
- Runs agent guide seeding on every startup after migrations.
- Must be restarted after embedding configuration changes.

## Deployment & Management
- Managed by launchd on macOS, with a single instance lock.
- Started via `make run-rmbd` or the desktop app.
- Does not auto-restart after an app upgrade.
- No CLI version command (version available via API).
- Built from the rmb-desktop project at `/Users/liguanghui/Virginia/colinleefish/rmb-desktop`.
- Desktop binary deployed at `~/.rmb/bin/rmbd-desktop`.
- Release process uses `make app-build`, notarize, and release-publish; code-signing keychain password only needed for publishing signed DMG and GitHub releases.
- Can be spawned by the installer/tray; can be SIGPIPE-killed if its stdout/stderr are pipes to an exited parent.
- Stores desired login-at-launch state in `config.yaml`.

## Logging & Debugging
- When run as a bundle, logs are discarded and there is no export diagnostics path.
- Otherwise, writes logs to `logs/rmbd.log` with rotation and 7-day cleanup.
- Debug logging endpoint at `/api/v1/debug/logs`.
- Known issues: `?worker=l2` log filter is broken because L2 logs use `session_id` instead of `worker`.
- No LLM request tracing: does not log per-call URL, status code, latency, or response size.
- Does not log `persist.scenes` failures because dry-run skips DB writes.

## Integration & Setup
- The rmb CLI talks to rmbd via HTTP API, not directly to the database.
- rmbd computes setup previews using built-in merge logic per agent, not dynamic detection.
- Has a mock setup mode for the integration tab, toggled via the `rmb.mockSetup` localStorage key or the `npm run dev:mock-setup` script in webui.

memories.body:
# starlink-bbc

## Overview
- starlink-bbc is a Helm chart for the BBC service.
- It is a repository in the user's starfamily-registry Aliyun ACR.
- The chart is located in `hs-devops/starlink-charts/charts/starlink-bbc`.

## Deployment
- The project lives in `starlink-dev-all-in-one` at `/data/starlink-dwb-blockblast`.
- A specific image tag `block-crush-feat-ne-tapd-v3.4.6-lite-8cf01fbe` is deployed on `archteam-starlink-dev-all-in-one` for `mx/block_crush`; its `ver-changelog/v3.4.6-lite-op-package` wrappers are not included.

## Service & Endpoints
- Exposes `/api` and an open `/health` endpoint for ALB health checks.
- The bbc service's health check endpoint is `/hello`, which returns 200 OK.
- It is a Kong service with retries set to 1 across all prod hosts and `kong.yaml`.
- It is the upstream behind the starlink RO Kong gateway serving `/api/fc/solution/*` endpoints.

## Gunicorn Configuration
- Uses a `gunicorn.conf.py` file mapped into the container.
- Binds to `0.0.0.0:12124` with `workers=4` and `timeout=360`.
- The chart renders the pod's `gunicorn.conf.py` by prepending bind from `.Values.gunicorn.bind` (tied to `service.port` 12124) and appending the per-environment body from the service's `gunicorn.conf.py`, so bind is not duplicated across environments.
- Version 0.1.2 manages gunicorn configuration via structured values and still supports the legacy `gunicornConf` field.

## Helm Chart Versions & Publishing
- Published to ACR at version 0.1.1.
- Version 0.1.2 manages gunicorn configuration as above.
- Version 0.1.3 synthesizes a `bbc-dotenv` Secret from config and secrets and mounts it at `/app/envs/{ENV_PROJ}/.env.{ENV_FILE}`.
- The chart is published to the OCI registry at `registry.hs99.vip` by a charts job triggered on push to main.
- The default image repository is `starfamily-registry-vpc.cn-beijing.cr.aliyuncs.com/starlink/bbc`; the published 0.1.3 chart used `registry.hs99.vip/starlink/bbc`.

## Secrets
- The chart always renders two Secret objects: `bbc-secret` and `bbc-dotenv`.

memories.body:
# Kong (API Gateway)

- **Role**: API gateway for the starlink infrastructure.
- **Current status**: Production gateway on ro-1, being replaced by ding. On ro-2 it is bypassed; ro-1 still serves until DNS cutover.
- **Version**: kong/kong-gateway:3.10 (DB-less).
- **Serving**: Main starlink RO hostnames on port 18000.
- **Configuration**: Defined in `kong.yaml`.

## Authentication & Routing
- **Key-auth plugin**: Uses `X-Starlink-ApiKey` header (no hyphen between Api and Key).
- **Routes**:
  - `/atomkit/*` → Atom Kit upstream with `strip_path: true`.
  - `/flow` → starflow upstream with `strip_path: false`.
  - Requires API key for `/atomkit` and `/flow`.
- **GQL API**: Exposed at `:18000/gql/*` with ACL enforcement.

## Trust & Security
- Honors `X-Forwarded-For` and trusts `172.16.0.0/12`.
- **Legacy s2s-gateway**: The `/api` route is completely open, returning 200 even for invalid keys or non-whitelisted IPs.

## Replacement
- Being replaced by **ding**; currently the production s2s API gateway.

# OpenResty

OpenResty is a web server and reverse proxy used as a gateway in multiple environments. It replaced Kong as the read-only gateway and is deployed in various stacks.

## Roles
- Acts as the gateway for BlockCrush production.
- Serves as an API gateway for the BlockCrush PM system, routing requests to BBC.
- Used as a reverse proxy for the starlink project and in the starlink stack.
- Proxies to BBC and starflow, using a Docker DNS resolver for upstream resolution.
- Used as a stopgap reverse proxy in all-in-one dev stacks and as the legacy gateway in dev stacks.
- Deployed as the gateway in the bc-cat environment (namespace starlink-blockcrush-cat).

## Deployment Details
- On starlink-dev-all-in-one, the openresty gateway is fronted by host nginx on 127.0.0.1:34207 and has an upstream configured to `starlink-mx-blockcrush-starflow-swagger-1:8080`.
- Openresty is a web server container running alongside starflow.
- It is the gateway for lsx-mjwd and depends on starflow, resolving it at startup.
- Openresty is a service that needs deployment.
- Openresty is **not** installed as a service on the starlink BlockBlast prod hosts 10.100.30.117/118/119.

## Notes
- OpenResty is used alongside the BBC project and as a web server in that context.
- It is the reverse proxy for blockblast environments.

memories.abstract: rmb-desktop is a macOS desktop app (pure Go tray app) for coding-agent memory, distilling conversations into L0-L3 memories, with local SQLite storage, daemon rmbd, CLI rmb, auto-updater for sidecars, and integrations with Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and WorkBuddy.
memories.body:
# RMB Desktop (rmb-desktop)

## Overview
- **Type**: macOS desktop application (pure Go tray app, migrated from Tauri).
- **Repository**: [github.com/colinleefish/rmb-desktop](https://github.com/colinleefish/rmb-desktop)
- **Purpose**: Coding-agent memory tool that hooks chats from Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and WorkBuddy; distills conversations into L0-L3 memories; recall via `rmb search` and `rmb://` URIs.
- **Version**: Under active development; latest known version 0.2.7 (as of fact set). Earlier versions: 0.1.0, 0.1.16, 0.1.18, 0.1.19.
- **Distribution**: Signed and notarized aarch64 DMGs via GitHub Releases and R2 update feed (`https://releases.re-mem-ber.me/latest.json`). Also distributed via Quick Whale.

## Architecture
- **Components**:
  - `rmbd` – Go backend daemon serving HTTP API on `127.0.0.1:19019`.
  - `rmb` – CLI with subcommands `ls`, `pull`, `put`.
  - `rmb-app` – app-shell tray app (pure Go, replaced Tauri shell).
  - Web UI settings page (built with Vite; source in `webui/`, generated output in `internal/http/static/web/`).
- **Sidecar binaries**: Installed at `~/.rmb/bin/rmb-app` and `~/.rmb/bin/rmbd-desktop`; also `~/.rmb/bin/rmb` for CLI.
- **Signing**: Developer ID Application: GUANGHUI LI (N4YPJBRBN4), hardened runtime, timestamped, notarized and stapled.
- **Sandbox**: Not sandboxed; ATS exceptions allow cleartext HTTP.

## Data Storage
- **Database**: Local SQLite at `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/data/rmb.db`.
- **Schema**: Includes `scenes` table and FTS5 virtual table `scenes_fts` (content='scenes', tokenize='unicode61'). Also `recall_stats` table keyed by URI.
- **Migrations**: Automatic via goose on startup; migration SQL embedded in binary. End users never run migration scripts manually.
- **WAL**: Enabled; foreign keys enabled.
- **Onboarding**: Marker file `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/onboarding.complete` (JSON with `completed_at` and `skipped_agents`).

## Pipeline
- **Workers**: L1, L2, and embed workers.
- **Flow**: Memory ingestion from L1 atoms to L2 scenes; L0-L1-L2-L3 pyramid (turns, atoms, scenes, memories) addressed by `rmb://` URIs.
- **L2 worker**: Located at `internal/worker/scene/worker.go`; manages `scenes` and `scenes_fts` writes.
- **Status**: `pipeline_state` table has columns `l1/l2/l3_last_error` and `l1/l2/l3_started_at`.
- **Stuck sessions**: L2 pipeline can get stuck if sessions remain in 'running' status after crashes/restarts.
- **FTS rebuild**: On startup, `scenes_fts` index is rebuilt; failure only logs a warning.

## Distribution & Installation
- **Installation**: Expected at `/Applications/RMB Desktop.app` (bundle identifier `me.remember.rmb`).
- **First-run bootstrap**: Copies bundled binaries to `~/.rmb/bin/` and installs a LaunchAgent for `rmbd`.
- **Updater**: Tauri updater disabled; custom auto-updater checks release feed, falls back to GitHub releases. Only updates sidecars (`rmb` CLI and `rmbd-desktop` daemon) under `~/.rmb/bin`; never touches the app shell; shell updates require manual DMG install.
- **Update check**: Compares release feed version to shell's compile-time version, not installed sidecar version, so it keeps offering an already-installed version (e.g., 0.2.7 after upgrading).
- **Release pipeline**: Requires `SIGN_KEYCHAIN_PASS`; without it, `make release` fails; can run as `app-build + notarize + sidecar-bundles + UPLOAD_ONLY=1 release`.

## Configuration & Data
- **Config file**: `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/config.yaml`.
- **Launch-at-login**: Stored in `config.yaml` under `launch_at_login`, registers a LaunchAgent at `~/Library/LaunchAgents/me.remember.rmb.plist`.
- **General settings**: Includes display language, distillation database path, and config file collection address.
- **API endpoints for onboarding**: `GET /api/v1/onboarding/status`, `POST /api/v1/onboarding/complete`, `POST /api/v1/onboarding/reset`.

## Debug & API
- **Debug endpoints**: Under `/debug/` and `/api/v1/debug/*` (unauthenticated).
- **Reachability**: Debug API at `10.254.24.7:19019` (remote instance) and local `127.0.0.1:19019`.
- **Endpoints cover**: workers, in-flight tasks, backpressure, logs, SQLite, pipeline stuck/unstick/requeue, LLM build-scenes, pipeline dry-run.
- **Health**: `GET /healthz` returns ok when DB opens (migrations passed).
- **Version**: `GET /api/v1/version` reports app version, not DB schema version.
- **Logging**: Every LLM request logged to `/api/v1/debug/logs` with fields: op, attempt, model, host, status, latency_ms, req_bytes, resp_bytes, err.

## Logging
- **Main log**: `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/logs/rmbd.log`.
- **Rotation**: Rotates at 5MB to `rmbd.log.old`; old logs cleaned after 7 days.
- **In-memory buffer**: 2000-entry buffer (`debug.NewLogBuffer`) exposed via webui Logs page and debug API.

## Known Issues & Fixes
- **0.1.19**: 2KB LLM truncation bug causing 'unexpected end of JSON input' in L2 pipeline.
- **0.1.18 fixes**: `llm.timeout` default 45s, T2 atom trim, real error text in logs.
- **README/Makefile**: As of 2026-08-14, README does not document automatic DB migrations; Makefile advertises non-existent `make migrate` target.
- **FTS corruption**: As of 2026-08-14, `scenes_fts` index appeared missing/corrupted (rebuild failed with 'no such table' while app logged 'malformed'), suspected cause of L2 persist failures.
- **Auto-updater quirk**: The `rmb-app` binary copied to `~/.rmb/bin` is SIGKILLed when run standalone because its code signature references the app bundle.

## Deployment
- **Remote instance**: Deployed on box at `10.254.24.7`.
- **Workspace**: Herdr workspace w7 corresponds to rmb-desktop project.

## Build & Release
- **Build**: Go codebase with `internal/worker/scene` and `internal/db` packages; built via Makefile.
- **Release assets**: `RMB.Desktop_<ver>_aarch64.dmg`, darwin_arm64 tarball, windows_amd64 zip, `manifest.json`.
- **Scripts**: `build-sidecar-bundles.sh`, `release.sh`, Makefile `sidecar-bundles` target.
- **Data migration**: `scripts/backfill-from-remote.py` imports sessions from remote rmb instances (not schema migration).

## Development
- **Local path**: `/Users/liguanghui/Virginia/colinleefish/rmb-desktop`.
- **WebUI dev server**: Started with `npm run dev:mock-setup`.
- **Build**: Uses `make webui-build` to copy assets from `webui/dist`.
- **Settings UI**: Tabs for General, Models, and Advanced; Integrations as a top-level sidebar item.
- **Integrations**: Supports OpenAI-compatible API format for LLM and embedding providers; has integrations for Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and WorkBuddy.
- **UI details**: Sidebar uses a Lucide Brain icon as placeholder brand mark; favicon is a purple gradient SVG at `ui/public/favicon.svg`.
- **Search**: Server's recall paths (FTS and vector) filter `superseded_at IS NULL`; Web UI search uses hand-built SQL in `internal/browse/browse.go`.

## Status
- Under active development by the user.
- Browser title and Tauri app name: 'RMB Desktop'.
- Includes a setup flow for installing agents.

Avatar scope is cached in Redis with a sliding TTL of 60 seconds, but cache invalidation only occurs in post_user_set_role, so direct DB edits do not invalidate the cache.
scenes.body:
## hs-code-keeper codebase

- `get_scope()` behavior:
  - On `main` branch: reads `avatar_role.scope` from the database.
  - On `main_ne` branch: returns the full `EAvatarScope` set without reading the DB when the user role contains `888`.
- Avatar scope caching:
  - Cached in Redis with a sliding TTL (`CACHE_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT=60`).
  - `cache.delete` is only called in `post_user_set_role`.
  - Direct DB edits do not invalidate the cache.

scenes.abstract: This scene captures a git operation where the latest local commit, identified by the hash e1aa0d6 and the commit message 'more memory', was removed from the repository's history. The removal was accomplished using the command 'git reset HEAD~1', which effectively undoes the commit by moving the branch pointer back one commit. This action discards the changes introduced by that commit, making it as if the commit never existed. The operation was performed locally, as the commit is described as a local commit.

It consists of two deployments (API and worker) from a single image. Recent changes include enabling the service in dolphin and other environments, updating image tags, removing nodeSelector, and adjusting resource requests/limits. The chart supports api.minDomains but not worker.minDomains.
scenes.body:
# Dataanalysis Service

The dataanalysis service is deployed in the crab, dolphin, shark, squid, and whale environments. It runs as two deployments: `dataanalysis-api` (HTTP API, uvicorn on port 8003) and `dataanalysis-worker` (background worker, `python -m src.worker`), both from a single image.

## Deployments

- **dataanalysis-api**: liveness probe `/health`, readiness probe `/ready` on port 8003. CPU request 200m, limit 1; memory request 512Mi, limit 1Gi.
- **dataanalysis-worker**: liveness exec probe (`python -m src.health_check`), no readiness probe. CPU request 500m, limit 2; memory request 2Gi, limit 4Gi.

## Configuration Changes

- Build #34 succeeded and published an image to registry.hs99.vip.
- The service was enabled in dolphin by setting `dataanalysis.enabled: true` in `envs/dolphin/env-values.yaml`.
- `versions.yaml` for dolphin was updated to reference image tag `feat-fglm-6811-data-analysis-skeleton-d0c175e5` and pushed to branch `feat/FGLM-6811-data-analysis-dolphin` (commit 2de8f01).
- The nodeSelector `project=starorigin419` was removed from `deploy.yaml` across all 5 dev environments.
- Worker resources in `envs/dolphin/services/dataanalysis/deploy.yaml` were updated to requests.cpu 500m, requests.memory 1Gi, limits.cpu 1, limits.memory 2Gi.
- The api block in the same file was updated to replicaCount: 2 and minDomains: 2.
- The branch `feat/FGLM-6811-data-analysis-dolphin` was committed and pushed (commit fee5606), enabling the service in crab, shark, squid, and whale environments.

## Chart Details

- The starorigin-dataanalysis chart supports `api.minDomains` but not `worker.minDomains`.
- The worker deployment uses topology spread with `whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway` and no `minDomains`.

## Repository

- The git repository for the service is `star-origin-mico`.

- Central figure of English Romanticism (1770–1850)
- Known for *Lyrical Ballads*, *Tintern Abbey*, and *The Prelude*

## John Keats
- Major Romantic poet of the second generation (1795–1821)
- Died at 25 of tuberculosis
- Known for odes: *Ode to a Nightingale*, *Ode on a Grecian Urn*, *Ode to Autumn*
- Concept of 'negative capability'

## Ode to a Nightingale
- Poem by John Keats written in 1819
- Contrasts the bird's immortal song with human mortality and suffering

scenes.abstract: Several codebase issues were identified: rustyme integration with missing transaction cleanup, feature_config lazy join and missing index, and solution_ai_marks update storm.
scenes.body:
### Rustyme Integration
- Rustyme is a conflict-detection integration (FGLM-5516) that uses a Redis queue.
- The `rustyme_result_consumer.py` `_process_result()` function has missing transaction cleanup (commit/rollback/session.remove) on early-return paths, returning connections to the pool 'idle in transaction'.

### Feature Config
- The BBC `feature_config` model's `fc_param_rules` relationship uses `lazy='joined'`, forcing a LEFT OUTER JOIN on every query and amplifying result sets.
- The `feature_config` table has unique indexes on `(platform, feature_id)` and `(platform, feature_desc)`, plus single-column indexes on `platform` and `feature_id`, but no index on `editer_time`.

### Solution AI Marks
- The `solution_ai_marks` table has accumulated ~21.4M UPDATEs across only 2,430 rows (~8,800 per row), likely from the `/ai_so/kafka/update_status` endpoint.

scenes.abstract: This scene records the user's market data source stack and preferences. Free sources are preferred over paid services such as Tushare Pro. The pipeline uses BaoStock, East Money, Sina, Tencent, AKShare, THS, Shenwan, CSIndex, and a curated benchmark list. BaoStock provides daily and financial data but has session and concurrency limits. East Money provides valuation history and financials but is often blocked locally and needs a server IP. Sina supplies valuation snapshots and Shenzhen index constituents, while Tushare supplies the official SW2021 mapping. Several sources have known anti-bot, SSL, and pagination issues.
scenes.body:
## Stack overview
- The user prefers free market data sources over paid ones like Tushare Pro. Tushare Pro is a paid market data service using a points system, costing roughly ¥200-1500/year.
- Tushare also provides the official SW2021 classify-to-index mapping (`index_classify`, doc_id=181).
- AKShare is a free Python SDK for Chinese market data used by the pbp pipeline; its `stock_zh_a_spot()` changed in Jan 2026 to drop per/pb/mktcap columns. It provides East Money financial indicators (`stock_financial_analysis_indicator_em`) and Shenwan index data (`sw_index_*_info`, `index_hist_sw`).
- BaoStock is a free Python SDK for Chinese market data and a data source for the pipeline, primarily covering Shanghai and Shenzhen stocks.
- The user considers Sina an acceptable stock data synchronization source.

## Source adapters and data coverage
- BaoStock provides daily stock data and A-share financial statement metrics. Its daily A-share K-line history spans 1990-12-19 to the last trading day, with each symbol's data starting at its listing date; data is unadjusted (`adjustflag=3`). It also provides profit and growth data via `query_profit_data` and `query_growth_data`. `query_all_stock` returns both indices and stocks (~7,202 rows), and `stock_info` includes non-equity index codes. It uses a global session model, but `query_history_k_data_plus` takes a single symbol; the session can expire mid-run during long backfills (用户未登录). It caps concurrent requests, so the pbp sync execute phase uses a single worker.
- East Money (EM / 东财 / 东方财富) is the primary financials data source in PBP, with BaoStock as fallback. Its `stock_value_em` API provides daily A-share valuation history (PE TTM, PE static, PB, market cap) back to 2018. Its concept constituents API `stock_board_concept_cons_em` returns the full constituent list in one call. EM is IP-blocked locally and is often blocked or flaky off-server; daily data falls back to baostock→sina→tencent, valuation may be Sina-only locally, and index spot API is blocked by anti-bot from the user's Mac IP. Spot lists work on the server IP.
- Sina (新浪) provides daily and valuation spot data; `fetch_valuation_spot` gives only a current valuation snapshot (per, pb, mktcap), not historic PE/PB time series. It provides Shenzhen 399* index constituents via `index_stock_cons_sina`, but the paginated API returns duplicate constituents for 399001.
- Tencent (腾讯) is a data source adapter in the pbp pipeline providing daily stock data.
- Shenwan (申万 / SW) is the industry classification standard used by the project, and its adapter provides index info and sector classification. The Shenwan 2021 classify XLS only contains columns 股票代码, 计入日期, 行业代码, 更新日期; the XLS at swsresearch.com returns an incomplete TLS certificate chain, and the site has an expired SSL certificate, requiring `SSL_VERIFY=false`.
- THS (同花顺 / Tonghuashun) is a concept-board data source; its daily, board, and board-stats data sync into the landing schema (e.g., `landing.ths_concept_board_stats`). Concept constituent pagination works via HTML pages, but pages 6 and beyond hit a login/anti-bot wall on many IPs. THS concept landing data has ~374 boards but is intentionally not merged for v1.
- CSIndex (中证指数网) provides index constituent data only for CSI-hosted codes like 000300 and 000905; it returns 404 for Shenzhen 399* indices.
- The project uses a curated list of 12 benchmark indices (000001, 000016, 000300, 000680, 000688, 000852, 000905, 932000, 399001, 399006, 399673, 899050) for index constituent mapping.

scenes.abstract: This scene describes the infrastructure entities for StarOrigin and aidaily: the StarOrigin production PostgreSQL 18 database on Alibaba Cloud RDS, the aidaily_svc service role, the staging and production aidaily databases, the production origin and dev dolphin origin databases, the read-only user dw_reader_starorigin_kol, the Kubernetes cluster ack-starorigin-prod and namespace starorigin-mcps-prod, the TLS certificate and secret for *.youxi123.com, the ingress route, and the user's credential storage location.
scenes.body:
### Databases

- StarOrigin production database is PostgreSQL 18 on Alibaba Cloud RDS at `archteam-starorigin419-prd-pg18.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com`.
- `starorigin_prod_origin` is the production origin database owned by the `starorigin` role.
- `starorigin_dolphin_origin` is the dev dolphin origin database where `aidaily_svc` has SELECT-only access on most tables.
- `staroriginmcp_staging_aidaily` is the staging aidaily database owned by `aidaily_svc` with full DML access.
- `staroriginmcp_prod_aidaily` is the production aidaily database owned by `aidaily_svc`.

### Roles and users

- `aidaily_svc` is a service role that owns `staroriginmcp_staging_aidaily` in dev with full DML, and has read-only SELECT on `starorigin_dolphin_origin`.
- `dw_reader_starorigin_kol` is a read-only user with SELECT access on `public.ai_question_metrics` in `starorigin_prod_origin`.

### Kubernetes

- `ack-starorigin-prod` is a Kubernetes cluster used for production deployments.
- `starorigin-mcps-prod` is a Kubernetes namespace in `ack-starorigin-prod`.
- The ingress `starorigin-mcps-aidaily-route` lives in the Kubernetes namespace `starorigin-mcps-prod` and references the TLS secret `mcp-youxi123-com-tls`.

### TLS certificates

- The wildcard TLS certificate for `*.youxi123.com` is stored in `starorigin419-prod` as `starorigin-new-youxi123-com-tls` and copied to `starorigin-mcps-prod` as `mcp-youxi123-com-tls`.
- The TLS secret `mcp-youxi123-com-tls` is in the Kubernetes namespace `starorigin-mcps-prod` and is a copy of the certificate `starorigin-new-youxi123-com-tls` from namespace `starorigin419-prod`.
- The TLS certificate `starorigin-new-youxi123-com-tls` lives in the Kubernetes namespace `starorigin419-prod`.
- On 2026-06-15, the TLS certificate `starorigin-new-youxi123-com-tls` was copied from namespace `starorigin419-prod` to `starorigin-mcps-prod` as `mcp-youxi123-com-tls`.

### Credentials

- The user stores credentials at `~/hungrystudio/e.credentials/`.

scenes.abstract: On 2026-06-19, the user created a security group in the caikuai-cn Aliyun account, cloned and initialized the hs-public-ip-addresses repo with uv and Aliyun PyPI mirror, and made several decisions about ip-rules.yaml: short 8-char hex hash IDs derived from public_cidr, created_at/updated_at timestamps, removing lan key in favor of description, and writing 72 generated IP rules as ingress allow-all rules into security group sg-2ze39zzh2m6qukikxxfo. A reconcile script was created to handle spreadsheet churn by marking disappeared CIDRs inactive.
scenes.body:
- On 2026-06-19, created security group `esg-allow-all-from-hungrystudio-office-public-ip-addresses` in the caikuai-cn Aliyun account.
- On 2026-06-19, cloned the `hs-public-ip-addresses` repo.
- On 2026-06-19, initialized the project with `uv` and configured the Aliyun PyPI mirror.
- Decided rule IDs in `ip-rules.yaml` should be short 8-char hex hashes derived from `public_cidr` so identical CIDRs always get the same ID.
- Decided each rule should carry `created_at` and `updated_at` timestamps.
- Decided to remove the `lan` key and fold LAN info into the description field.
- Created `reconcile-ip-rules.py` to handle the 85/15 spreadsheet churn scenario by marking disappeared CIDRs inactive.

scenes.abstract: Summarizes the attendance policy and related practices at 辽宁农商银行. It specifies weekday work hours from 8:30 to 17:00, attendance recording methods for headquarters versus other offices, and requirements for advance approval of leave and business outings. It defines absenteeism rules, including time thresholds for half-day and full-day absences, and counts repeated late arrivals as personal leave or absenteeism. It also covers consequences for falsifying attendance records and limits makeup clock-ins to three times per month.
scenes.body:
- 辽宁农商银行 has an attendance policy with weekday work hours 8:30–17:00.
- At headquarters, attendance is recorded by turnstile gates; other offices use WeChat face recognition.
- Leave and business outings require advance approval and cannot be filed retroactively.
- Being absent from post without approval counts as absenteeism: 3 hours equals half a day and 6 hours equals a full day.
- Three late arrivals in a month count as one day of personal leave; six count as one day of absenteeism.
- Falsifying attendance records is treated as absenteeism.
- Makeup clock-ins are limited to three times per month.

scenes.abstract: Covers feature_tag_config and its history tables, history2 coverage, the active Airflow server, the production database, and raw and wide tables used by the flush DAG.
scenes.body:
## Infrastructure & Data Entities

- `feature_tag_config` is a table in `prd_blockblast_client.public` holding tag definitions and Yunxiao creative metadata (`serial_number`, `url_cloud_effect`, etc.).
- `feature_tag_config_history` stores full-row snapshots of `feature_tag_config`, recorded continuously since 2025-03-28.
- `feature_tag_config_history` has no `tag_id` column; it links to `feature_tag_config` by `(platform, tag_desc)`.
- `feature_tag_config_history` never records `creator_aliyun_account_id` (all values null or empty).
- `feature_tag_config_history` covers 97.2% of active tags; 881 active tags created after 2025-10-21 have no history rows.
- `feature_tag_config_history2` is a newer, lighter operation log keyed by `tag_id`, covering about 17% of active tags.
- The active Airflow server is `archteam-starlink-airflow-prd`, reachable at `10.100.51.20`.
- `prd_blockblast_client` is the production database with 4 schemas (`public`, `uums`, `yunxiao`, `starorigin`) and about 10GB of data.
- `yunxiao.one_tag_solution_yunxiao_info` is the raw mapping table that the flush DAG upserts.
- `public.airflow_one_tag_solution_yunxiao_info_for_starmap` is the wide table the flush DAG writes for StarMap.

scenes.abstract: The Starlink dev infrastructure involves an old host (starlink-dev-all-in-one-uc at 10.9.114.160) and a new Aliyun ECS (archteam-starlink-dev-all-in-one at 10.100.48.251) running a matrix of 14 environments × 5 games with Docker Compose. PostgreSQL is on Aliyun RDS, images come from registry.hs99.vip, DNS lives in Cloudflare's hs99.vip zone, and all compose projects share starlink_network. Telemetry uses Alloy, Loki, and Prometheus; Jenkins and Kafka are part of the setup.
scenes.body:
Recorded Starlink dev infrastructure includes:

- Old host: `starlink-dev-all-in-one-uc`, reachable at `10.9.114.160`; DNS `starlink-dev-uc-internal.hs99.vip` (`10.9.114.160`) is the old Starlink dev host.
- New host: `archteam-starlink-dev-all-in-one`, an Aliyun ECS at `10.100.48.251` (Rocky 9.7, 32 vCPU/60 GiB, single 300 G root disk); DNS `starlink-dev-internal.hs99.vip` (`10.100.48.251`) is the new Starlink dev host that replaced the old box.
- The dev matrix is 14 environments × 5 games × ~14 services per game, run as Docker Compose projects under `/data` and wired by the XXYYZ port scheme.
- All Compose projects join the shared external Docker network `starlink_network`.
- PostgreSQL runs on Aliyun RDS at `starlink-dev-all-in-one.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com:5432`; per-environment databases are named `{env}_{game}_client`, `{env}_{game}_codekeeper`, `{env}_{game}_hfrog`, `{env}_{game}_starflow`.
- `starlink-envs` is a FastAPI + Vue management portal for the matrix, running as a host process on `:8900` (uv + uvicorn) and SSO-gated to a 19-developer whitelist.
- Dev container images are pulled from `registry.hs99.vip`.
- DNS is managed in the `hs99.vip` zone on Cloudflare; individual `<env>-<game>.hs99.vip` CNAMEs are recorded with `starlink-dev-uc-internal.hs99.vip` (old host) as their target.
- `starlink.youxi123.com` and `hfrog.youxi123.com` are pinned via `extra_hosts` to `10.9.144.217` on both the old host and the new starlink box.
- Shared Kafka broker cluster is on the 10.9 subnet (port 9092); AB3 service is at `10.9.87.141:8001`.
- Telemetry: Grafana Alloy 1.10.2 is installed on the new box and ships metrics to `prometheus.hs99.vip`; Alloy also ships logs/metrics to `loki.hs99.vip`/`prometheus.hs99.vip` and collects from dev containers. `loki.hs99.vip` (`10.9.94.63`) is the Starlink Loki/Prometheus endpoint.
- Jenkins (`devops-jenkins`) runs the Starlink deploy and db-migrator playbooks and connects to `starlink-dev-internal.hs99.vip` as root.
- RDS also hosts `dwb_mjwd` and `dwb_blockcrush`; on 2026-06-06 the orphaned replication slots `supabase_etl_apply_66192` (`dwb_mjwd`) and `supabase_etl_apply_39786` (`dwb_blockcrush`) were dropped from the RDS.
- Storage preference: enlarge the entire disk when storage runs out rather than adding separate mounts.

scenes.abstract: The user's infrastructure includes Aliyun ACK clusters, the hs-devops git repo, and a Jenkins sync job. In mid-July 2026, Loki and Alloy were removed from the relevant clusters, while the OSS bucket was left intact.
scenes.body:
## Clusters and Repositories
- ack-starfamily-devops is an Aliyun ACK cluster (cluster ID c2d24c874b7a74790a45566ce8bd7e12d, Kubernetes v1.35.2-aliyun.1) used as the StarFamily DevOps cluster, with config in hs-devops/deployments/environments/ack-starfamily-devops/.
- The kubeconfig context for ack-starfamily-devops has a user entry named by Aliyun UID 209712269600235313 instead of the context name, causing kubectl to prompt for credentials.
- ack-starorigin-dev is an Aliyun ACK cluster (StarOrigin dev) that previously shipped logs via Alloy to the shared Loki on ack-starfamily-devops.
- ack-starorigin-prod is an Aliyun ACK cluster (StarOrigin production) that previously shipped logs via Alloy to the shared Loki on ack-starfamily-devops.
- hs-devops is the git repository holding deployment configs for the ACK clusters under hs-devops/deployments/environments/<cluster>/.
- A Jenkins sync-envs job syncs deployment configs from the hs-devops repo to the ACK clusters.

## Logging Removal Events
- On 2026-07-16, the Loki entry point was removed from ack-starfamily-devops: Ingress loki-route, AlbConfig ack-starfamily-loki-alb, and IngressClass were deleted, and the objects were removed from the hs-devops git config.
- On 2026-07-16, Alloy was removed from ack-starorigin-dev and ack-starorigin-prod: target.yaml set to state: absent and the Helm release uninstalled from the monitoring namespace on both clusters.
- On 2026-07-17, Loki was fully removed from ack-starfamily-devops: Helm release uninstalled, 6x20Gi ESSD PVCs deleted, and the loki namespace deleted.
- starfamily-ack-loki-logging is an Aliyun OSS bucket in Beijing that stored Loki log chunks; it was left in place after Loki was removed.

scenes.abstract: The architecture scene describes tutu's structural design: self-contained segments in segments/*.zsh, each owning icon, colors, and content, with the core assembling generic payloads. It lists 17 segments, a pure-zsh philosophy (PHILOSOPHY.md) that conflicts with cache daemons, a single default behavior after removal of the calm profile, handling of supplementary-plane nerd icons and the \U000F10FE syntax, a text-only Bun segment, and built-in tutu-monitor and tutu diagnose debug commands.
scenes.body:
- tutu uses self-contained segments: each `segments/*.zsh` owns its icon, colors, and content; the core only assembles generic payloads.
- tutu has 17 segments: aws, azure, gcloud, aliyun, docker, kube, node, bun, python, uv, fnm, venv, golang, dir, git, clock, and status.
- `PHILOSOPHY.md` documents a pure-zsh philosophy, which conflicts with adding a cache daemon.
- tutu has a single default behavior; the former 'calm' profile was removed.
- `lib/segments.zsh` handles supplementary-plane nerd icons (e.g. U+F10FE) as single-width glyphs.
- tutu uses `$'\U000F10FE'` syntax, not `$'\uF10FE'`, for supplementary-plane codepoints.
- The Bun segment is text-only because the Meslo p10k font subset lacks the nf-dev-bun glyph.
- tutu includes `tutu-monitor` and `tutu diagnose` commands for debugging prompt performance.

  - `starlink-prd-blockblast-app-2` (`10.9.164.112`) runs frontend and Atomkit containers.

scenes.abstract: On 2026-06-04 CI build #299 failed due to a timeout downloading a large wheel from files.pythonhosted.org. The team fixed the issue by updating the agent-server Dockerfile to use Aliyun mirrors and rewriting all uv.lock URLs to mirrors.aliyun.com. Commit 945c4e9 made build #300 succeed in 84 seconds. On 2026-06-05, origin-build #463 was diagnosed as slow because its branch still used the unmirrored uv.lock.
scenes.body:
### Timeline
- **2026-06-04**: CI build #299 failed because `uv sync --frozen` timed out downloading the 70.6 MiB `claude-agent-sdk` wheel from `files.pythonhosted.org`.
- **2026-06-04**: The agent-server Dockerfile was updated to use Aliyun mirrors for PyPI (`UV_DEFAULT_INDEX`, `PIP_INDEX_URL`) and Debian apt packages.
- **2026-06-04**: All 2962 wheel/sdist URLs in `starorigin`'s `uv.lock` were rewritten from `files.pythonhosted.org` to `mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/packages/` to fix build #299.
- **2026-06-04**: The `uv.lock` Aliyun fix was committed to the `cicd/liguanghui` branch (commit `945c4e9`), and Jenkins build #300 succeeded in 84 seconds.
- **2026-06-05**: `origin-build` #463 was diagnosed as slow because its branch `feat/sandbox-pool-cost-optimization` had a `uv.lock` still pointing at `files.pythonhosted.org`.

Several hosts serve the endpoints used by the DAGs: wz-blockblast and starlink.youxi123.com serve /flow/solution_stats/v1/stats, while mx-blockcrush serves the PM requirement delay_status refresh endpoint. The DAG call_pm_requirement_delay_status_refresh_on_1am_every_day POSTs daily at 01:00 Asia/Shanghai, and call_flow_solution_stats_v1_stats_on_1st_every_month calls the stats endpoint monthly on the 1st. The stats API accepts an empty months string and defaults to the current month.
scenes.body:
**Scheduler**

**DAGs**

scenes.abstract: Infrastructure scene covers TLS certificate automation for hs99.vip. A fetch-certs.sh script downloads certificates from OSS, handles only hs99.vip, runs weekly on Mondays at 03:00, and supports a --check mode. A Let's Encrypt E8 certificate for hs99.vip and wildcard SANs was issued on 2026-04-07, valid until 2026-07-06, and published to the colin-certs OSS bucket. The installed certificate on Nginx hosts is at /etc/nginx/ssl/hs99.vip/fullchain.cer; JumpServer is used to access those hosts.
scenes.body:
## TLS Certificate Automation for hs99.vip

- `fetch-certs.sh` downloads certificates from OSS and does **not** run acme.sh or certbot.
- The script only handles `DOMAINS="hs99.vip"`; `xy678.vip` and `hungrystudio.pp.ua` are **not** covered.
- The cron for `fetch-certs.sh` runs weekly on Mondays at 03:00.
- The script supports a `--check` mode to verify installed certificates on hosts.

## Certificate Storage and Installation

- The OSS bucket `colin-certs` stores the published certificate for `hs99.vip` under `certs/hs99.vip/`.
- The TLS certificate for `hs99.vip` is issued by Let's Encrypt and published to the OSS bucket `colin-certs`.
- On 2026-04-07 a Let's Encrypt E8 certificate for `hs99.vip` (SANs: `hs99.vip`, `*.hs99.vip`) was issued, valid until 2026-07-06.
- The installed certificate for `hs99.vip` on Nginx hosts is at `/etc/nginx/ssl/hs99.vip/fullchain.cer`.

## Access

- JumpServer is used to access the Nginx hosts.

scenes.abstract: Migration of 133 starlink development databases from UCloud PostgreSQL to Aliyun RDS. Dump started on 2026-05-25, completed 2026-05-26. First restore hit a 100 GB cap and failed; storage was expanded and the second restore succeeded. Blockmj, mjwd, blockcrush, and blockblast environments were cut over, and source databases were dropped. A streaming test was about five times slower than dump-to-disk. Final blockblast environments were migrated on 2026-05-28, and locallogin families followed on 2026-05-29.
scenes.body:
### Dump
- On 2026-05-25, the dump phase of the starlink dev PostgreSQL migration started in tmux session `pgmig`.
- On 2026-05-26, the dump phase completed: 133 databases, 23.5 GB compressed, in about 7h42m.
- The starlink source databases were dumped from UCloud, running from 23:07 on 2026-05-25 to 06:49 on 2026-05-26.

### Restore
- On 2026-05-26, restore into Aliyun RDS started in tmux session `pgres`.
- The first restore attempt to `starlink-dev-all-in-one` failed after 44 minutes due to storage exhaustion (100 GB cap), with 14 of 133 databases restored.
- Storage was expanded after the 100 GB cap caused the restore failure.
- The second restore attempt completed successfully, restoring all 133 databases (136 GB) in about 18 minutes.
- The migration of 133 starlink databases from UCloud to the Aliyun RDS `starlink-dev-all-in-one` was completed.

### Cutovers and environment migrations
- On 2026-05-26, all 14 blockmj stacks were cut over from the UCloud PG host to the Aliyun RDS; dwb-blockmj was verified writing to the new RDS; 30 blockmj databases were dropped from the source UCloud PostgreSQL.
- On 2026-05-27, the mjwd database migration (dump/restore) began.
- On 2026-05-27, all 42 environments across blockcrush, mjwd, and blockmj were pointed at the starlink-dev-all-in-one RDS.
- On 2026-05-27, 86 old databases matching the 14-env prefix for mjwd, blockcrush, blockmj, sandcrush, and crushblast were dropped from the source PG, reclaiming ~15 GB.
- On 2026-05-27, a direct pg_dump|pg_restore streaming test from the source host to a temporary public RDS endpoint (`pgm-2zem02dsw7d3yvu8do.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com`) was attempted for dwb_blockblast and found to be ~1 MB/s, about 5x slower than the Aliyun-host dump-to-disk approach.
- `source-side-env.sh` is the blockblast dump/restore script and supports `EXCLUDE_TABLE_DATA`; the blockblast project has 14 environments.
- On 2026-05-27, yy_blockblast_client was restored to Aliyun RDS in 39 minutes and yy-blockblast was cut over.
- yl, cyx, hyx, dev, kwd, and yy blockblast environments were cut over to RDS and their source DBs were dropped.
- The migration script had a `DIR: unbound variable` bug at cyx cutover; it was fixed and a resume pipeline was started.
- On 2026-05-27, 9 Starlink dev blockblast environments (dev, kwd, yy, yl, cyx, hyx, lxy, lby, mx) were migrated to Aliyun RDS and cut over, with source DBs dropped.
- On 2026-05-28, 38 docker-compose files with duplicate profiles blocks under pgpour were deduplicated using `fix-pgpour-duplicate-profiles.sh`; `lint-docker-compose.sh` was added at `/data/migration-cutover/`.
- On 2026-05-28, the user started migration of the final five Blockblast envs (dwb, lgh, lhh, lsx, wz) to Aliyun RDS via tmux session `pgbb-final5`.
- On 2026-05-28, 16 of 19 databases had been restored in the starlink dev to Aliyun migration.
- On 2026-05-29, the user redid the blockblast migration to include cutover.
- On 2026-05-29, locallogin-blockblast databases were migrated to Aliyun RDS with cutover; client schema-only, codekeeper full data, source dropped; the `restore_blockblast_client` scratch database was dropped, reclaiming 60 GB on /data.
- On 2026-05-29, locallogin-blockmj, locallogin-blockcrush, and locallogin-mjwd database families were migrated to RDS with cutover and source dropped.

scenes.abstract: PBP (Print Baby Print) is the user's Chinese A-share quantitative data sync service: it syncs AKShare data into PostgreSQL, is idempotent and resumable from checkpoints, is deployed via Docker Compose with ofelia scheduling daily at 18:00 CST, uses uv, and lives at /app/pbp on the rmb server. sync_all.py orchestrates jobs and continues past failed jobs; concept_mapping is skipped while East Money is down. Separately, stock-funnel-analysis is a live 3-stage AI stock funnel that pulls live Sina snapshots directly.
scenes.body:
### PBP
- PBP (Print Baby Print) is a Chinese A-share quantitative data sync service.
- PBP syncs A-share market data from AKShare into PostgreSQL.
- PBP's sync is idempotent and resumable: it syncs a date range (default 2024-01-01 to last trading day) and resumes from checkpoints after failure.
- PBP is deployed via Docker Compose with ofelia scheduling pbp-sync daily at 18:00 CST.
- PBP uses uv for Python dependency management and running sync scripts.
- PBP's local checkout is at `/Users/liguanghui/Virginia/colinleefish/pbp`.
- PBP is the user's Chinese A-share stock data project, with a PostgreSQL database (`pbp_db`), sync scripts, and Docker-based sync jobs.
- pbp is a stock data sync project whose code lives at `/app/pbp` on the rmb server.

### PBP sync orchestration
- `scripts/sync/sync_all.py` is the PBP sync orchestrator; it supports `--job`/`--jobs` subset selection and continues past failed jobs.
- PBP's `concept_mapping` job has no fallback data source and is skipped when East Money is down.

### stock-funnel-analysis
- `~/stock-funnel-analysis` is a live 3-stage AI stock funnel (scan → deep dive → report) that fetches data on the fly from Sina Finance, requires `pi --mode rpc`, and writes to `~/stock-analysis-output/final_report.md`.
- The stock-funnel-analysis project (`stock-funnel-analyze.py`) pulls live Sina snapshots directly and does not depend on historical K-line data.

scenes.abstract: mypast is the user's personal long-term memory store for AI-agent conversations, with hooks capturing every turn from Cursor and Claude Code. Its stack is Go 1.26 with Gin, GORM, goose migrations, PostgreSQL (pgvector), and an OpenAI-compatible LLM client. Memory is organized as T0 session_turns, T1 atoms, T2 scenes, and T3 memories; truth flows upward from T0 evidence, with T0 append-only, T1 append-by-default, and T3 memories versioned by insert plus supersede. T1 and T2 workers run in production at mem.colinleefish.com, with agent-driven CI/deploy and no GitHub Actions.
scenes.body:
### What it is
- mypast is the user's personal long-term memory store for AI-agent conversations.
- Hooks capture every turn from Cursor and Claude Code.

### Stack
- Go 1.26 with Gin, GORM, and goose migrations.
- PostgreSQL with pgvector.
- OpenAI-compatible LLM client.

### Memory model
- T0 session_turns (raw turns) -> T1 atoms (structured facts) -> T2 scenes (session segments) -> T3 memories (cross-session long-term knowledge).
- Core invariant: truth flows upward from T0 evidence; T0 is append-only, T1 is append-by-default, and T3 memories are versioned by insert + supersede, never updated in place.

### Operations
- T1 (extract) and T2 (scene) workers run in production at mem.colinleefish.com.
- Agent-driven CI/deploy: `make ci`, `make deploy` over SSH.
- No GitHub Actions.

- Umami prod stores all data in the umami_db database on the shared RDS, with no local volume to migrate; the database is shared by the old and new Umami instances.

**Applications**
- Metabase prod runs from /data/metabase-prod on the new host 10.100.95.77 with a ./data:/metabase-data bind mount; it runs as the metabase-prod container.
- Umami prod runs from /data/umami-prod on the new host 10.100.95.77 as umami-prod at version 3.2.0; the deployment uses the floating image tag umamisoftware/umami:postgresql-latest, which does not guarantee the same version across hosts.

scenes.abstract: The codebase has multiple notable implementation details. The SQLite database is configured with WAL and foreign_keys but no busy_timeout, so concurrent writes can fail; vector recall brute-forces cosine similarity in memory instead of using sqlite_vec MATCH. L1 retries failed sessions indefinitely while L2 actively retries; L3 performs full table scans and sleeps while holding GlobalLock. The correction enqueue uses a non-indexable string concatenation join, l3_status acts as a dirty flag, L2 dupCount depends on LLM return order, and mergeTurnMessages can break UTF-8.
scenes.body:
- The project's SQLite database is configured with WAL and foreign_keys pragmas but no busy_timeout, so concurrent writes can fail with 'database is locked'.
- The vector recall path loads all embeddings into memory and brute-force computes cosine similarity instead of using sqlite_vec virtual table MATCH.
- The L1 extract worker retries failed sessions indefinitely because selectCandidateSessions only checks l1_extracted_at IS NULL.
- The L2 scene worker actively retries failed sessions because selectCandidateSessions includes l2_status IN ('pending','failed').
- The L3 memory worker performs full table scans without a watermark when rolling up atoms and scenes.
- The correction enqueue join uses a non-indexable string concatenation condition: JOIN scenes sc ON ('rmb://scenes/' || lower(sc.id)) = je.value.
- The l3_status column is used as a dirty flag by L2 persist and EnqueueSessionsForMemoryTargets.
- The scene worker's dupCount uses LLM return order to determine deterministic IDs.
- The extract worker's mergeTurnMessages can break UTF-8 by byte-truncating with next[:remaining].
- The memory worker sleeps 1s (distillDelay) while holding GlobalLock.

scenes.abstract: This scene documents current schema state and schema alignment facts across Blockcrush and Mahjong Wonders clients. mjwd environments lag blockcrush: feature_config.idea_label is text instead of text[], fc_workflow_info is missing four newer columns, and legacy submitter/follower fields remain. prd-blockcrush is in the same old state. fc_workflow_info is the B table in the merge chain; its new columns are actual_first_launch_batch, is_personal_recommendation, target_audience, and optimization_dir. solution_extension_id columns were added to dwb_blockcrush_client and prd_mahjongwonders_client, and feature_config_workflow_info is a merged wide table maintained by rebuild_refresh_feature_config_workflow_info().

- `prd-blockcrush` is in the same old schema state as the `mjwd` environments: `idea_label` is `text`, four `fc_workflow_info` columns are missing, and legacy submitter/follower fields remain.
- `fc_workflow_info` is the workflow info table, referred to as the B table in the merge chain.
- Compared to `dwb-blockcrush`, `fc_workflow_info` in `prd-blockcrush` and `prd-mahjongwonders` is missing `actual_first_launch_batch`, `is_personal_recommendation`, `target_audience`, and `optimization_dir`, and has extra legacy columns `submitter` and `follower`.

- In `prd-blockcrush` and `prd-mahjongwonders`, `feature_config` has 54 columns identical to `dwb-blockcrush` except `idea_label` is `text` instead of `text[]`.
- `fc_workflow_info` table schema includes four new columns: `actual_first_launch_batch` (`text`), `is_personal_recommendation` (`boolean`), `target_audience` (`text[]` default `'{}'`), and `optimization_dir` (`text[]` default `'{}'`).

scenes.abstract: The memory condensation pipeline consists of T1 extraction, T2 scene, and T3 memory stages. T1 and T2 process sessions independently with backpressure-controlled concurrency. T3 is a global distillation job that groups atoms by slug across sessions and distills one memory per bucket. T3 is currently serialized by a global lock and faces per-slug concurrency conflicts. Single-atom buckets bypass LLM distillation.
scenes.body:
- The memory condensation pipeline consists of T1 extraction, T2 scene, and T3 memory stages.
- T1 and T2 are session-based rollup stages that process each session independently and can run concurrently with backpressure-controlled worker counts.
- T3 (L3 rollup) is a global memory-distillation job that groups all sessions' atoms by slug across sessions and distills one memory per bucket, not per session.
- T3 currently cannot run multiple workers: its rollup is serialized by workerlock.GlobalLock and distills one bucket at a time with a 1-second holding-lock delay.
- T3's per-slug memory uses an active unique index plus versioning, so concurrent distillation of the same slug conflicts and needs per-slug sharded locks.
- distillBucket short-circuits single-atom buckets by using the atom's content directly as the memory body instead of calling the LLM.

scenes.abstract: RMB Desktop stores SQLite data at ~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/data/rmb.db, including a scenes table and scenes_fts FTS5 index rebuilt on startup. The system uses the stargate LLM gateway at stargate.youxi123.com serving deepseek-v4-flash, with 45-second gateway timeouts. A remote server and pipeline at 10.254.24.7 run another deployment. Concurrent L2 worker writes can corrupt the scenes_fts external-content table.
scenes.body:
**Storage**

- RMB Desktop stores data in SQLite at `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/data/rmb.db`.
- The database contains a `scenes` table and FTS5 virtual table `scenes_fts` (`content='scenes'`, `tokenize='unicode61'`), populated by the app's L2 pipeline stage.
- The rmb-desktop daemon (`rmbd`) rebuilds `scenes_fts` on startup but only logs a warning if the rebuild fails.
- As of 2026-08-14, the scenes table was empty and `scenes_fts` appeared missing or corrupted (`rebuild failed with 'no such table'` while the app logged `'malformed'`), suspected to cause L2 persist failures.
- The rmb project's SQLite database has a `scenes_fts` FTS5 external-content table that can corrupt under concurrent L2 worker writes.

**Gateway and model**

- Stargate is the LLM gateway at `stargate.youxi123.com` used by rmb-desktop.
- It serves the `deepseek-v4-flash` model.
- Requests awaiting Stargate response headers can time out at 45 seconds.

**Remote hosts**

- The remote server at `10.254.24.7` runs a separate deployment of the system (v0.1.19 as of 2026-08-14).
- An RMB Desktop instance is deployed on the remote box at `10.254.24.7`.
- The remote pipeline server, called 724.7, is reachable at `10.254.24.7:19019`.

scenes.abstract: RMB Desktop logging is split between the rmbd daemon and rmb-app tray shell. The daemon writes its main log to ~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/logs/rmbd.log, rotates at 5MB to rmbd.log.old, cleans old logs after 7 days, and keeps a 2000-entry in-memory log buffer exposed through the webui Logs page and debug API. The tray shell previously wrote /tmp/rmb-app.stderr.log and /tmp/rmb-app.stdout.log via a LaunchAgent plist; after switching to SMAppService the plist was removed and those files no longer grow. Under SMAppService, rmb-app discards stderr; bootstrap/health errors can be inspected with `log show --predicate 'process == "RMB Desktop"' --last 5m`.
scenes.body:
- **rmbd main log**: `~/Library/Application Support/rmb-desktop/logs/rmbd.log`.
- **Rotation**: rotates at 5MB to `rmbd.log.old`; old logs are cleaned after 7 days.
- **In-memory buffer**: 2000 entries (`debug.NewLogBuffer`), exposed through the webui Logs page and debug API.
- **rmb-app legacy /tmp logs**: `rmb-app.stderr.log` and `rmb-app.stdout.log` via a LaunchAgent plist; after switching to SMAppService the plist was removed and those files no longer grow.
- **rmb-app under SMAppService**: discards stderr; bootstrap/health errors can be inspected with `log show --predicate 'process == "RMB Desktop"' --last 5m`.

scenes.abstract: RMB recall stats are keyed by version-less URI, so counters persist across memory versions. persistMemory supersedes old memory rows and inserts new rows with the same URI and version+1, without touching recall_stats. Slug drift creates a new URI and resets recall counters. Scenes are keyed by UUID and never versioned, so scene stats are per-incarnation, while skills share slug-keyed URI stats across versions.
scenes.body:
- Recall stats are keyed by version-less URI, so counters persist across memory versions.
- `persistMemory` supersedes old memory rows and inserts new rows with the same URI and version+1, without touching `recall_stats`.
- Slug drift creates a new URI and resets recall counters.
- Scenes are keyed by UUID and never versioned, so scene stats are per-incarnation, while skills share slug-keyed URI stats across versions.

scenes.body:
**TapTile & Merge systems**
- TapTile is a system with client and codekeeper databases (`prd_taptile_client`, `prd_taptile_codekeeper`); configured APP_ID is `tap_tile`; GQL service runs the same image as block-bloom (`prod-mahjong-wonders-main-dda7f7bd`).
- Merge is a system with client and codekeeper databases (`prd_merge_client`, `prd_merge_codekeeper`).
- TapTile and Merge DBs were bootstrapped from an older schema snapshot than block-bloom's.
- TapTile production PostgreSQL databases are `prd_taptile_codekeeper` and `prd_taptile_client` on `starlink-taptile-prod.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com`.
- Merge production PostgreSQL databases are `prd_merge_codekeeper` and `prd_merge_client` on `starlink-merge-prod.pg.rds.aliyuncs.com`.
- `taptile` and `merge` are RDS databases.

**Roles & restore**
- `starlink_user` is a PostgreSQL role that owns the TapTile and Merge production databases on Aliyun RDS.
- On Aliyun RDS PostgreSQL, the postgres account cannot grant the predefined `pg_read_all_data` role.
- On 2026-08-17, `starlink_user` was granted CONNECT and ALL privileges on the TapTile and Merge production databases via SQL.
- Jenkins master is a host used to run the schema-only restore script for taptile and merge; Jenkins master host is at 10.100.27.205.
- db-migrator is a Jenkins job (`starlink/db-migrator-client-and-code-keeper`) that restores block-bloom dumps into other databases.
- block-bloom is the reference prod system whose client database has 161 tables and is the source for db-migrator restores; block-bloom is a production database with client and codekeeper schemas.

**SSO**
- HungryStudio's company SSO is at `sso.youxi123.com`.
- Starlink prod SSO apps are typically created with `access_everyone: true`, so any HungryStudio SSO account can authenticate.
- The `fework_prd_db.app_login` table maps SSO app ids to hosts for the SSO login flow.
- BBC verifies SSO tickets using `SSO_SECRET_KEY` from `config/bbc/env.prod`.
- On 2026-08-17 the TapTile prod SSO login chain was wired up: SSO app 1181083874 registered in `fework_prd_db.app_login`, `SSO_SECRET_KEY` set on both taptile hosts, nginx/compose stack deployed, and ALB/DNS pointed at the VMs.
